title.zh: 卷474 列傳二百六十一 吴三桂 耿精忠 尚之信 孙延龄
title.en: Volume 474 Biographies 261: Wu Sangui, Geng Jingzhong, Shang Zhixin, Sun Yanling
title.raw: 卷474 列傳二百六十一 吴三桂 耿精忠 尚之信 孙延龄

sentences.zh: 吳三桂，字長伯，江南高郵人，籍遼東。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui, style name Changbo, was a native of Gaoyou in Jiangnan, with household registration in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui, whose style name was Changbo, came from Gaoyou in Jiangnan but was registered as a resident of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 父襄，明崇禎初官錦州總兵。

translations.literal: His father Xiang, at the beginning of the Chongzhen reign of the Ming, served as regional commander of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wu Xiang had held the post of regional commander of Jinzhou since the early Chongzhen era.

sentences.zh: 三桂以武舉承父廕，初授都督指揮。

translations.literal: Sangui, as a military licentiate, received his father's hereditary privilege and was first appointed commander-in-chief of the guard.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui entered service through the military examinations and inherited his father's privilege, initially receiving appointment as a commander-in-chief of the guard.

sentences.zh: 襄坐失機下獄，擢三桂總兵，守寧遠。

translations.literal: Xiang, having been imprisoned for missing an opportunity, Sangui was promoted to regional commander and defended Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Xiang was imprisoned for a military failure, Wu Sangui was promoted to regional commander and stationed at Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 洪承疇出督師，合諸鎮兵，三桂其一也。

translations.literal: Hong Chengchou went out as supreme commander, gathering troops from all garrisons—Sangui was among them.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong Chengchou took supreme command, he mustered forces from all the frontier garrisons, and Wu Sangui was one of those commanders.

sentences.zh: 師攻松山，三桂戰敗，夜引兵去。

translations.literal: The army attacked Songshan; Sangui was defeated in battle and withdrew his troops by night.
translations.idiomatic: During the attack on Songshan, Wu Sangui was defeated and withdrew his forces under cover of darkness.

sentences.zh: 松山破，承疇降，三桂坐鐫三秩，收兵仍守寧遠。

translations.literal: When Songshan fell and Chengchou surrendered, Sangui was demoted three ranks, gathered his troops, and still defended Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Songshan fell and Hong Chengchou surrendered, Wu Sangui was stripped of three ranks, regrouped his army, and continued to hold Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 三桂，祖大壽甥也，大壽既降，太宗令張存仁書招三桂，不報。

translations.literal: Sangui was the nephew of Zu Dashou; after Dashou had surrendered, the Taizong ordered Zhang Cunren to write and recruit Sangui, but he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui was a nephew of Zu Dashou. After Dashou surrendered, the Taizong had Zhang Cunren send letters urging Wu Sangui to defect, but he gave no reply.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，李自成自西安東犯，太原、寧武、大同皆陷，又分兵破真定。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, Li Zicheng marched east from Xi'an; Taiyuan, Ningwu, and Datong all fell, and he also sent detachments to capture Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shunzhi, Li Zicheng advanced east from Xi'an. Taiyuan, Ningwu, and Datong all fell in turn, and he sent additional forces to seize Zhending.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝封三桂平西伯，並起襄提督京營，徵三桂入衛。

translations.literal: The Chongzhen Emperor enfeoffed Sangui as Marquis Who Pacifies the West, also recalled Xiang to supervise the capital garrison, and summoned Sangui to defend the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Chongzhen ennobled Wu Sangui as Marquis Who Pacifies the West, recalled Wu Xiang to command the capital garrison, and ordered Wu Sangui to march to the capital's defense.

sentences.zh: 寧遠兵號五十萬，三桂簡閱步騎遣入關，而留精銳自將為殿。

translations.literal: The Ningyuan army was said to number five hundred thousand; Sangui selected infantry and cavalry and sent them through the pass, while he himself led the elite troops as rearguard.
translations.idiomatic: The army at Ningyuan was said to number five hundred thousand men. Wu Sangui reviewed his infantry and cavalry and sent them through the pass, while he personally commanded the elite troops bringing up the rear.

sentences.zh: 三月甲辰，入關，戊申，次豐潤。

translations.literal: On jiachen of the third month he entered the pass; on wushen he halted at Fengrun.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiachen day of the third month he entered the pass, and on the wushen day he encamped at Fengrun.

sentences.zh: 而自成已以乙巳破明都，遣降將唐通、白廣恩將兵東攻灤州。

translations.literal: But Zicheng had already on yisi captured the Ming capital and sent the surrendered generals Tang Tong and Bai Guang'en east with troops to attack Luanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng had already taken the Ming capital on the yisi day and dispatched the surrendered generals Tang Tong and Bai Guang'en eastward to attack Luanzhou.

sentences.zh: 三桂擊破之，降其兵八千，引兵還保山海關。

translations.literal: Sangui defeated them, accepted the surrender of eight thousand of their troops, and led his army back to defend Shanhaiguan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui routed them, accepted the surrender of eight thousand of their men, and withdrew to hold Shanhaiguan.

sentences.zh: 自成脅襄以書招之，令通以銀四萬犒師，遣別將率二萬人代三桂守關。

translations.literal: Zicheng coerced Xiang to write and recruit him, ordered Tong to present forty thousand taels of silver to reward the army, and sent another general with twenty thousand men to replace Sangui in guarding the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng forced Wu Xiang to write urging surrender, sent Tang Tong with forty thousand taels of silver to reward the troops, and dispatched another general with twenty thousand men to relieve Wu Sangui of garrison duty at the pass.

sentences.zh: 三桂引兵西，至灤州，聞其妾陳為自成將劉宗敏掠去，怒，還擊破自成所遣守關將；

translations.literal: Sangui led his troops west; when he reached Luanzhou he heard that his concubine Chen had been seized by Zicheng's general Liu Zongmin—enraged, he turned back and defeated the general Zicheng had sent to guard the pass;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui marched west, and when he reached Luanzhou he learned that his concubine Lady Chen had been carried off by Li Zicheng's general Liu Zongmin. In a fury he turned back and routed the commander Li Zicheng had posted at the pass;

sentences.zh: 遣副將楊珅、游擊郭雲龍上書睿親王乞師。

translations.literal: He sent the vice commander Yang Shen and the guerrilla officer Guo Yunlong to write to Prince Rui begging for troops.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Vice Commander Yang Shen and Guerrilla Officer Guo Yunlong to petition Prince Rui for military aid.

sentences.zh: 王方西征，次翁後，三桂使至，明日，進次西拉塔拉，報三桂書，許之。

translations.literal: The Prince was on a western campaign, halted at Weng River; Sangui's envoy arrived, and the next day he advanced to Xilatala, replied to Sangui's letter, and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rui was campaigning westward and had halted at the Weng River when Wu Sangui's messenger arrived. The next day he advanced to Xilatala, answered Wu Sangui's letter, and granted his request.

sentences.zh: 自成聞三桂兵起，自將二十萬人以東，執襄置軍中；

translations.literal: Zicheng, hearing that Sangui's troops had risen, personally led two hundred thousand men east, seized Xiang and placed him in the army;
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zicheng heard that Wu Sangui had taken up arms, he personally led two hundred thousand men eastward, seized Wu Xiang, and kept him with the army;

sentences.zh: 復遣所置兵政部尚書王則堯招三桂，三桂留不遣。

translations.literal: He again sent his appointed Minister of War Wang Zeyao to recruit Sangui; Sangui detained him and would not let him go.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent his appointed Minister of War Wang Zeyao to win Wu Sangui over, but Wu Sangui detained him and refused to release him.

sentences.zh: 越四日，王進次連山，三桂又遣雲龍齎書趣進兵。

translations.literal: Four days later the Prince advanced to Lianshan; Sangui again sent Yunlong bearing a letter urging him to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Four days later the prince advanced to Lianshan, and Wu Sangui again sent Guo Yunlong with a letter urging him to press forward.

sentences.zh: 師夜發，逾寧遠，次沙河，明日，距山海關十里。

translations.literal: The army set out at night, passed beyond Ningyuan, halted at Shahe; the next day it was ten li from Shanhaiguan.
translations.idiomatic: The army marched by night, passed Ningyuan, and encamped at Shahe. The following day it was ten li from Shanhaiguan.

sentences.zh: 三桂遣邏卒報自成將唐通出邊立營，王遣兵攻之，戰於一片石，通敗走。

translations.literal: Sangui sent patrol soldiers to report that Zicheng's general Tang Tong had gone beyond the border and set up camp; the Prince sent troops to attack him, fought at Yipianshi, and Tong was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui sent scouts reporting that Li Zicheng's general Tang Tong had encamped beyond the border. The prince sent troops to attack him at Yipianshi, and Tang Tong was routed and fled.

sentences.zh: 又明日，師至關，三桂出迎。

translations.literal: On the following day the army reached the pass and Sangui came out to welcome it.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the army reached the pass, and Wu Sangui came out to welcome it.

sentences.zh: 王命設儀仗，吹螺，偕三桂拜天畢，三桂率部將謁王，王令其兵以白布系肩為識，前驅入關。

translations.literal: The Prince ordered ceremonial guards set up and conches blown; together with Sangui he completed worship of Heaven, after which Sangui led his subordinate generals to pay homage; the Prince ordered his soldiers to tie white cloth on their shoulders as identification and advance first through the pass.
translations.idiomatic: The prince ordered ceremonial guards arrayed and conches sounded. He and Wu Sangui completed their rites to Heaven, after which Wu Sangui led his subordinate generals to pay homage. The prince had his soldiers tie white cloth on their shoulders for identification and sent them forward through the pass as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 自成兵橫亙山海間，列陣以待。

translations.literal: Zicheng's troops stretched across the area between the mountains and the sea, forming battle lines to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng's army stretched across the ground between mountain and sea, drawn up in battle formation to meet them.

sentences.zh: 王令諸軍向自成兵而陣，三桂兵列右翼之末。

translations.literal: The Prince ordered all armies to form ranks facing Zicheng's troops; Sangui's army was placed at the end of the right wing.
translations.idiomatic: The prince ordered the armies to deploy facing Li Zicheng's forces, with Wu Sangui's troops at the far end of the right wing.

sentences.zh: 陣定，三桂先與自成兵戰，力斗數十合。

translations.literal: When the formations were set, Sangui first fought Zicheng's troops, fiercely battling for several dozen exchanges.
translations.idiomatic: Once the lines were formed, Wu Sangui engaged Li Zicheng's forces first and fought fiercely for dozens of rounds.

sentences.zh: 及午，大風塵起，咫尺莫能辨，師噪風止。

translations.literal: By noon a great wind raised dust, and at arm's length nothing could be distinguished; the army shouted and the wind ceased.
translations.idiomatic: By midday a fierce wind whipped up dust so thick that nothing could be seen an arm's length away. The army raised a great shout, and the wind died down.

sentences.zh: 武英郡王阿濟格、豫郡王多鐸以二萬騎自三桂陣右突入，騰躍摧陷。

translations.literal: Prince Wuying Ajige and Prince Yu Dodo, with twenty thousand cavalry, burst in from the right of Sangui's formation, leaping forward and breaking through.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ajige of Wuying and Prince Dodo of Yu led twenty thousand cavalry in a charge through the right of Wu Sangui's line, surging forward and smashing the enemy ranks.

sentences.zh: 自成方立馬高岡觀戰，詫曰：「此滿洲兵也！」

translations.literal: Zicheng was standing his horse on a high mound watching the battle and exclaimed in surprise: "These are Manchu troops!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng had been watching the battle from horseback on a high mound. He cried out in astonishment, "Those are Manchu troops!"

sentences.zh: 策馬下岡走，自成兵奪氣，奔潰。

translations.literal: He spurred his horse down from the mound and fled; Zicheng's troops lost their spirit and broke and ran.
translations.idiomatic: He wheeled his horse down from the mound and fled. Li Zicheng's army lost heart and scattered in rout.

sentences.zh: 逐北四十里，即日王承製進三桂爵平西王，分馬步兵各萬隸焉，令前驅逐自成。

translations.literal: They pursued the fleeing enemy forty li; that same day the Prince, by imperial commission, advanced Sangui to Prince Who Pacifies the West, assigned ten thousand cavalry and infantry to him, and ordered him to advance in pursuit of Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: They pursued the enemy forty li. That same day, acting under imperial authority, the prince promoted Wu Sangui to Prince Who Pacifies the West, assigned him ten thousand cavalry and infantry, and ordered him to press the pursuit of Li Zicheng.

sentences.zh: 三桂執則堯送王所，命斬之。

translations.literal: Sangui seized Zeyao and sent him to the Prince's headquarters, who ordered him beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui seized Wang Zeyao and sent him to the prince's camp, where he was ordered executed.

sentences.zh: 自成至永平，殺襄，走還明都，屠襄家，棄明都西走。

translations.literal: Zicheng reached Yongping, killed Xiang, returned to the Ming capital, slaughtered Xiang's family, abandoned the Ming capital, and fled west.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng reached Yongping, killed Wu Xiang, returned to the Ming capital, massacred the Wu family, then abandoned the capital and fled west.

sentences.zh: 命三桂從阿濟格逐自成至慶都，屢戰皆勝。

translations.literal: He ordered Sangui to follow Ajige in pursuing Zicheng to Qingdu; in repeated battles they were victorious.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui was ordered to follow Ajige in pursuing Li Zicheng to Qingdu, and they won victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 自成走山西，乃還師。

translations.literal: Zicheng fled to Shanxi, and they then returned with the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zicheng fled into Shanxi, the army turned back.

sentences.zh: 世祖定京師，授三桂平西王冊印，賜銀萬、馬三。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor secured the capital, conferred on Sangui the patent and seal of Prince Who Pacifies the West, and bestowed ten thousand taels of silver and three horses.
translations.idiomatic: After the Shunzhi Emperor secured the capital, he conferred on Wu Sangui the patent and seal of Prince Who Pacifies the West and granted him ten thousand taels of silver and three horses.

sentences.zh: 明福王由崧稱帝南京，使封三桂薊國公，又遣沈廷揚自海道運米十萬、銀五萬犒師，三桂不受；

translations.literal: The Ming Prince of Fu, Zhu Yousong, declared himself emperor at Nanjing, sent envoys to enfeoff Sangui as Duke of Ji, and also dispatched Shen Tingyang by sea route with one hundred thousand piculs of grain and fifty thousand taels of silver to reward the army—Sangui did not accept;
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Prince of Fu, Zhu Yousong, had himself proclaimed emperor at Nanjing and sent envoys to enfeoff Wu Sangui as Duke of Ji. He also dispatched Shen Tingyang by sea with one hundred thousand piculs of grain and fifty thousand taels of silver to reward the army, but Wu Sangui refused;

sentences.zh: 尋遣其侍郎左懋第、都督陳洪範等使於我，复齎銀幣勞三桂，三桂仍辭不受。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he sent his Vice Minister Zuo Maodi, Regional Commander Chen Hongfan, and others as envoys to us, again bringing silver and gifts to reward Sangui—Sangui still declined to accept.
translations.idiomatic: He soon sent his Vice Minister Zuo Maodi, Regional Commander Chen Hongfan, and others as envoys to the Qing court, again bearing silver and gifts to reward Wu Sangui, but Wu Sangui once more refused.

sentences.zh: 尋命英親王阿濟格為大將軍，西討自成，三桂率所部從，自邊外趨綏德，二年，克延安、鄜州，進攻西安。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Prince Ying Ajige was appointed grand general to campaign west against Zicheng; Sangui led his own troops in attendance, advancing from beyond the border toward Suide; in the second year they captured Yan'an and Fuzhou and advanced to attack Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: The court soon appointed Prince Ajige of Ying grand general for a western campaign against Li Zicheng. Wu Sangui led his own forces along the outer route toward Suide. In the second year they took Yan'an and Fuzhou and advanced on Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 自成以數十萬人迎戰，三桂督兵奮擊，斬數万級。

translations.literal: Zicheng met them with several hundred thousand men; Sangui supervised the troops in fierce attack and beheaded tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng met them with several hundred thousand men. Wu Sangui directed a fierce assault and slew tens of thousands of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 自成出武關南走，師從之，自襄陽下武昌，自成走死。

translations.literal: Zicheng went out through Wu Pass and fled south; the army followed, descending from Xiangyang to Wuchang, and Zicheng fled to his death.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng broke out through Wu Pass and fled south. The army pursued him from Xiangyang down to Wuchang, and Li Zicheng died in flight.

sentences.zh: 師復東徇九江。

translations.literal: The army then turned east and subdued Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: The army then marched east and subdued Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 八月，師還，賜繡朝衣一襲、馬二，命進稱親王，出鎮錦州，所部分屯寧、錦、中右、中後、中前、前屯諸地。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the army returned; he was granted one embroidered court robe and two horses, ordered advanced to the title of prince, sent out to garrison Jinzhou, and his troops were distributed to garrison Ning, Jin, Zhongyou, Zhonghou, Zhongqian, Qiantun, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the army returned. He was granted an embroidered court robe and two horses, promoted to princely rank, and sent to garrison Jinzhou, with his forces distributed among Ningyuan, Jinzhou, Zhongyou, Zhonghou, Zhongqian, Qiantun, and other stations.

sentences.zh: 三桂疏言丁給地五晌，各所房屋灰燼，地土磽薄，請增給；

translations.literal: Sangui memorialized that each man was allotted five shang of land, but the houses at each post were ashes and the soil poor and thin, and requested additional grants;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui memorialized that although each man had been allotted five shang of land, the dwellings at every post lay in ashes and the soil was poor and thin, and he requested additional grants;

sentences.zh: 並為珅、雲龍及諸將吳國貴、高得捷等請世職，屬吏童達行等乞優擢；

translations.literal: and also requested hereditary offices for Shen, Yunlong, and the generals Wu Guogui, Gao Dejie, and others, and that subordinate officials Tong Daxing and others be given preferential promotion;
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned for hereditary offices for Yang Shen, Guo Yunlong, and generals such as Wu Guogui and Gao Dejie, and asked that subordinates such as Tong Daxing receive preferential promotion;

sentences.zh: 又以父襄、母祖氏、弟三輔並為自成所殺，疏乞賜卹：並如所請。

translations.literal: and further, because his father Xiang, mother the Zu clan, and younger brother Sanfu had all been killed by Zicheng, he memorialized begging posthumous honors—all were granted as requested.
translations.idiomatic: He further noted that his father Wu Xiang, his mother of the Zu clan, and his younger brother Sanfu had all been killed by Li Zicheng and petitioned for posthumous honors. All his requests were granted.

sentences.zh: 三桂辭親王，下部議，許之。

translations.literal: Sangui declined the princely title; the matter was referred to the ministries for discussion, and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui declined the princely title. The matter was referred to the ministries for deliberation, and his request was approved.

sentences.zh: 三年，入覲，賜銀二萬。

translations.literal: In the third year he came to court for audience and was granted twenty thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he came to court for an audience and was granted twenty thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 五年，命與定西將軍墨爾根侍衛李國翰同鎮漢中。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was ordered to garrison Hanzhong jointly with the General Who Pacifies the West, Mergen Bodyguard Li Guohan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was ordered to garrison Hanzhong jointly with Li Guohan, General Who Pacifies the West and imperial bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 六年，明宗室硃森滏攻階州，三桂與國翰督兵擊斬之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the Ming imperial clansman Zhu Senyu attacked Jiezhou; Sangui and Guohan supervised the troops, attacked, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the Ming imperial clansman Zhu Senyu attacked Jiezhou. Wu Sangui and Li Guohan led the troops against him and killed him in battle.

sentences.zh: 有王永強者為亂，破延安、榆林等十九州縣，延綏巡撫王正志、靖遠道夏時芳死之；

translations.literal: There was one Wang Yongqiang who raised a rebellion, captured Yan'an, Yulin, and nineteen other prefectures and counties; the Yansui governor Wang Zhengzhi and the Jingyuan circuit intendant Xia Shifang died in the fighting;
translations.idiomatic: A rebel named Wang Yongqiang rose in revolt and overran Yan'an, Yulin, and nineteen other prefectures and counties. The Yansui governor Wang Zhengzhi and the Jingyuan circuit intendant Xia Shifang were killed;

sentences.zh: 复陷同官、定邊、花馬池。

translations.literal: He again captured Tongguan, Dingbian, and Huamachi.
translations.idiomatic: He also seized Tongguan, Dingbian, and Huamachi.

sentences.zh: 三桂督兵克宜君、同官，擊斬七千餘級。

translations.literal: Sangui supervised the troops in capturing Yijun and Tongguan, attacking and beheading more than seven thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui led his troops in recovering Yijun and Tongguan and slew more than seven thousand of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 進克蒲城、宜川、安塞、清澗諸縣，誅永強所置吏。

translations.literal: He advanced to capture Pucheng, Yichuan, Ansai, Qingjian, and other counties, and executed the officials Yongqiang had appointed.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to take Pucheng, Yichuan, Ansai, Qingjian, and other counties and executed the officials Wang Yongqiang had installed.

sentences.zh: 定邊、榆林、府谷皆下。

translations.literal: Dingbian, Yulin, and Fugu all fell.
translations.idiomatic: Dingbian, Yulin, and Fugu all submitted.

sentences.zh: 八年，入覲，賜金冊印。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he came to court for audience and was granted a golden patent and seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he came to court for an audience and was granted a golden patent and seal.

sentences.zh: 時明桂王由榔稱帝居南寧，張獻忠將孫可望、李定國等皆降於明，率兵擾川北諸郡縣。

translations.literal: At that time the Ming Prince of Gui, Zhu Youlang, had declared himself emperor and resided at Nanning; Zhang Xianzhong's generals Sun Kewang, Li Dingguo, and others had all surrendered to the Ming and led troops to harass the prefectures and counties of northern Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Ming Prince of Gui, Zhu Youlang, had proclaimed himself emperor and was based at Nanning. Sun Kewang, Li Dingguo, and other generals of Zhang Xianzhong had submitted to the Ming and were raiding the prefectures and counties of northern Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 命三桂偕國翰率師討之。

translations.literal: He was ordered that Sangui together with Guohan lead an army to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui was ordered to join Li Guohan in leading an army against them.

sentences.zh: 九年七月，三桂與國翰遣兵西撫漳臘、松潘，東拔重慶；

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the ninth year Sangui and Guohan sent troops west to pacify Zhangla and Songpan, and east to capture Chongqing;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the ninth year Wu Sangui and Li Guohan sent forces west to pacify Zhangla and Songpan and east to take Chongqing;

sentences.zh: 進攻成都，明將劉文秀棄城走；

translations.literal: they advanced to attack Chengdu; the Ming general Liu Wenxiu abandoned the city and fled;
translations.idiomatic: they advanced on Chengdu, and the Ming general Liu Wenxiu abandoned the city and fled;

sentences.zh: 復進克嘉定，駐軍綿州。

translations.literal: they again advanced to capture Jiading and stationed the army at Mianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: they went on to take Jiading and encamped the army at Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 文秀及王復臣復自貴州向四川，招倮儸為助，陷重慶，進破敘州。

translations.literal: Wenxiu and Wang Fuchen again came from Guizhou toward Sichuan, recruited the Lolo as allies, captured Chongqing, and advanced to break Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wenxiu and Wang Fuchen marched again from Guizhou into Sichuan, enlisted Yi tribesmen as allies, retook Chongqing, and advanced to defeat Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 三桂屢戰不利。

translations.literal: Sangui repeatedly fought without success.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui suffered repeated defeats.

sentences.zh: 文秀、复臣圍巡按御史郝浴於保寧。

translations.literal: Wenxiu and Fuchen besieged the touring censor Hao Yu at Baoning.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wenxiu and Wang Fuchen besieged the touring censor Hao Yu at Baoning.

sentences.zh: 浴趣三桂等赴援，擊斬复臣，文秀引兵走。

translations.literal: Yu urged Sangui and others to come to the rescue; they attacked and beheaded Fuchen, and Wenxiu led his troops away.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Yu urged Wu Sangui and the others to relieve him. They attacked and killed Wang Fuchen, and Liu Wenxiu withdrew.

sentences.zh: 浴疏劾三桂擁兵觀望狀，三桂摘疏中「親冒矢石」語劾浴冒功，浴坐謫徙。

translations.literal: Yu memorialized impeaching Sangui for holding troops and watching from the sidelines; Sangui seized on the phrase in the memorial "personally braving arrows and stones" to impeach Yu for claiming false merit, and Yu was punished by banishment.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Yu memorialized accusing Wu Sangui of holding back his troops and merely watching events unfold. Wu Sangui seized on the phrase in the memorial about "personally braving arrows and stones" to accuse Hao Yu of claiming credit he did not deserve, and Hao Yu was banished.

sentences.zh: 三桂敘功，歲增俸千。

translations.literal: Sangui reported his merits, and his annual salary was increased by one thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui reported his achievements, and his annual stipend was increased by one thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 子應熊尚主，為和碩額駙，授三等精奇尼哈番，加少保兼太子太保。

translations.literal: His son Yingxiong married a princess, became a prince consort of the first rank, was granted the third-rank jingqi niha, and was given the additional titles of Junior Guardian and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wu Yingxiong married an imperial princess and became a prince consort of the first rank. He was granted the third-rank jingqi niha banner rank and given the additional titles of Junior Guardian and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十四年，可望反明，攻由榔，定國御之，可望敗走長沙，來降。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Kewang turned against the Ming and attacked Youlang; Dingguo resisted him; Kewang was defeated and fled to Changsha, then came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Sun Kewang rebelled against the Ming and attacked Zhu Youlang. Li Dingguo defended him. Sun Kewang was defeated, fled to Changsha, and then surrendered to the Qing.

sentences.zh: 詔授三桂平西大將軍，與國翰率師徇貴州；

translations.literal: An edict appointed Sangui Grand General Who Pacifies the West, and together with Guohan he led an army to subdue Guizhou;
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Wu Sangui Grand General Who Pacifies the West, and he and Li Guohan led an army to subdue Guizhou;

sentences.zh: 時大將軍羅託、經略洪承疇等出湖南，將軍卓布泰等出廣西：三道並進。

translations.literal: At that time the grand general Luo Tuo, the supreme commander Hong Chengchou, and others went out from Hunan, and the general Zhuobutai and others from Guangxi—all three routes advanced together.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Grand General Luo Tuo, Supreme Commander Hong Chengchou, and others advanced from Hunan, while General Zhuobutai and others advanced from Guangxi. The three columns moved forward together.

sentences.zh: 三桂等發漢中，道保寧、順慶，次合州，破明兵，收江中戰艦。

translations.literal: Sangui and others set out from Hanzhong, passed through Baoning and Shunqing, halted at Hezhou, defeated Ming troops, and captured warships on the river.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui and his forces set out from Hanzhong, passed through Baoning and Shunqing, and encamped at Hezhou, where they defeated Ming troops and seized warships on the river.

sentences.zh: 定國遣其將劉正國、楊武守三坡、紅關諸隘，石壺關者尤險峻，明兵阻關。

translations.literal: Dingguo sent his generals Liu Zhengguo and Yang Wu to guard the passes at Sanpo, Hongguan, and others; Shihuguan was especially steep and perilous, and Ming troops blocked the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dingguo posted his generals Liu Zhengguo and Yang Wu to hold the passes at Sanpo, Hongguan, and elsewhere. Shihuguan was especially steep and perilous, and Ming troops barred the way.

sentences.zh: 三桂令騎兵循山麓，步兵陟其巔，以砲發其伏，明兵驚潰，遂下遵義，克開州。

translations.literal: Sangui ordered cavalry to follow the mountain foot and infantry to climb its summit, using cannon to strike their ambush; the Ming troops were startled and routed, then they descended on Zunyi and captured Kaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui sent cavalry along the foot of the mountain and infantry up its crest, using artillery to blast their ambush positions. The Ming troops broke in panic, after which he took Zunyi and captured Kaizhou.

sentences.zh: 會羅託等已克貴陽，卓布泰亦自都勻、安遠入，信郡王多尼將禁旅至。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Luo Tuo and others had already captured Guiyang; Zhuobutai also entered from Duyun and Anyuan; Prince Xin Duoni led the forbidden troops to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: By then Luo Tuo and the others had already taken Guiyang, Zhuobutai had entered from Duyun and Anyuan, and Prince Duoni of Xin arrived with the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 國翰還師遵義，尋卒。

translations.literal: Guohan returned his army to Zunyi and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guohan withdrew his army to Zunyi and soon died.

sentences.zh: 三桂馳與羅託等會於平越楊老堡，議分道進兵。

translations.literal: Sangui hurried to join Luo Tuo and others at Yanglaobao in Pingyue, where they discussed dividing forces to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui hurried to join Luo Tuo and the others at Yanglaobao in Pingyue, where they agreed to advance by separate routes.

sentences.zh: 三桂自遵義出天生橋，聞白文選據七星關，遂繞出烏撒土司境，次霑益。

translations.literal: Sangui set out from Zunyi through Tiansheng Bridge; hearing that Bai Wenxuan held Qixing Pass, he therefore made a detour through the territory of the Wusa chieftain and halted at Zhanyi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui marched from Zunyi by way of Tiansheng Bridge. Learning that Bai Wenxuan held Qixing Pass, he swung around through Wusa tribal territory and encamped at Zhanyi.

sentences.zh: 多尼師進曲靖，敗文選。

translations.literal: Duoni's army advanced to Qujing and defeated Wenxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Duoni's army advanced on Qujing and defeated Bai Wenxuan.

sentences.zh: 卓布泰師進羅平，敗定國。

translations.literal: Zhuobutai's army advanced to Luoping and defeated Dingguo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuobutai's army advanced on Luoping and defeated Li Dingguo.

sentences.zh: 十六年正月，由榔奔永昌。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixteenth year Youlang fled to Yongchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixteenth year Zhu Youlang fled to Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 二月，三桂與尚善、卓布泰合軍克雲南會城，破文選玉龍關，取永昌，由榔走緬甸。

translations.literal: In the second month Sangui joined with Shangshan and Zhuobutai to capture the Yunnan provincial capital, broke Wenxuan at Yulong Pass, took Yongchang, and Youlang fled to Burma.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Wu Sangui joined Shangshan and Zhuobutai in taking the Yunnan provincial capital, broke through Bai Wenxuan at Yulong Pass, seized Yongchang, and Zhu Youlang fled into Burma.

sentences.zh: 師渡潞江，定國設伏磨盤山，诇知之，分八隊迎擊，斬殺過半。

translations.literal: The army crossed the Lu River; Dingguo set an ambush at Mopan Mountain; having learned of it through scouts, they divided into eight columns to meet the attack and beheaded more than half.
translations.idiomatic: The army crossed the Lu River. Li Dingguo laid an ambush at Mopan Mountain, but scouts discovered it. The Qing forces divided into eight columns to meet the attack and killed more than half the enemy.

sentences.zh: 取騰越，追至南甸，乃振旅自永昌、大理、姚安還。

translations.literal: They captured Tengyue, pursued to Nandian, then rallied the army and returned by way of Yongchang, Dali, and Yao'an.
translations.idiomatic: They took Tengyue and pursued the enemy to Nandian, then withdrew the army by way of Yongchang, Dali, and Yao'an.

sentences.zh: 明將馬寶、李如碧、高啟隆、劉之复、塔新策、王會、劉偁、馬惟興、楊武、楊威、高應鳳、狄三品等，及景東、蒙化、麗江、東川、鎮雄諸土司，先後來降。

translations.literal: The Ming generals Ma Bao, Li Rubi, Gao Qilong, Liu Zhifu, Ta Xince, Wang Hui, Liu Cheng, Ma Weixing, Yang Wu, Yang Wei, Gao Yingfeng, Di Sanpin, and others, as well as the chieftains of Jingdong, Menghua, Lijiang, Dongchuan, Zhenxiong, and other tribes, came to surrender one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Ming generals including Ma Bao, Li Rubi, Gao Qilong, Liu Zhifu, Ta Xince, Wang Hui, Liu Cheng, Ma Weixing, Yang Wu, Yang Wei, Gao Yingfeng, and Di Sanpin, together with the tribal chiefs of Jingdong, Menghua, Lijiang, Dongchuan, Zhenxiong, and other regions, surrendered in succession.

sentences.zh: 多尼、卓布泰等師還，留固山額真伊爾德、卓羅等分軍駐守，而詔三桂鎮雲南，命總管軍民事。

translations.literal: Duoni, Zhuobutai, and others returned with their armies; they left the gushan ejen Ierde, Zhuoluo, and others with divided forces to garrison, while an edict ordered Sangui to garrison Yunnan and placed him in overall charge of military and civil affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Duoni, Zhuobutai, and the others withdrew their armies, leaving gushan ejen Ierde, Zhuoluo, and others with detachments to garrison the region. An edict then ordered Wu Sangui to govern Yunnan and placed all military and civil affairs under his authority.

sentences.zh: 諭吏、兵二部，雲南將吏聽三桂黜陟。

translations.literal: The civil and military ministries were instructed that Yunnan's officers and officials were subject to Sangui's appointment and dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: The civil and military ministries were instructed that all officers and officials in Yunnan were subject to Wu Sangui's appointment and dismissal.

sentences.zh: 定國求出由榔緬甸，軍孟艮。

translations.literal: Dingguo sought to bring Youlang out of Burma and stationed his army at Menggen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dingguo sought to bring Zhu Youlang out of Burma and encamped his army at Menggen.

sentences.zh: 元江土司那嵩與降將高應鳳舉兵應定國。

translations.literal: The Yuanjiang chieftain Na Song and the surrendered general Gao Yingfeng raised troops in response to Dingguo.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuanjiang chieftain Na Song and the surrendered general Gao Yingfeng took up arms in support of Li Dingguo.

sentences.zh: 三桂督兵自石屏進圍元江，踰月，擊斬應鳳，嵩自焚死，收其地為元江府。

translations.literal: Sangui supervised the troops advancing from Shiping to besiege Yuanjiang; after more than a month he attacked and beheaded Yingfeng; Song burned himself to death; his territory was incorporated as Yuanjiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui led his troops from Shiping to besiege Yuanjiang. After more than a month he attacked and killed Gao Yingfeng. Na Song burned himself to death, and his territory was reorganized as Yuanjiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十七年，戶部疏言雲南俸餉歲九百餘萬，議檄滿洲兵還京，裁綠旗兵五之二。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the Board of Revenue memorialized that Yunnan's salaries and provisions exceeded nine million annually; it was proposed to order the Manchu troops back to the capital and reduce the Green Standard troops by two-fifths.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the Board of Revenue reported that salaries and provisions for Yunnan exceeded nine million taels a year. It was proposed to recall the Manchu troops to the capital and cut the Green Standard forces by two-fifths.

sentences.zh: 三桂謂邊疆不寧，不宜減兵力。

translations.literal: Sangui said the frontier was not yet settled and it was not appropriate to reduce military strength.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui argued that the frontier was still unsettled and that troop strength should not be reduced.

sentences.zh: 是時三桂已陰有異志，其籓下副都統楊珅說以先除由榔絕人望。

translations.literal: At this time Sangui already harbored secret designs of rebellion; his subordinate vice commander Yang Shen urged that they first eliminate Youlang to cut off popular hope.
translations.idiomatic: By then Wu Sangui was already secretly nursing rebellious ambitions. His subordinate Vice Commander Yang Shen urged him first to eliminate Zhu Youlang and thereby extinguish the last focus of Ming loyalist hopes.

sentences.zh: 三桂乃疏言：「前者密陳進兵緬甸，奉諭：'若勢有不可，慎勿強，務詳審斟酌而行。

translations.literal: Sangui then memorialized: "Previously I secretly reported on advancing troops into Burma and received the imperial instruction: 'If circumstances make it impossible, be careful not to force the matter; you must deliberate carefully and act with discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui then memorialized: "When I previously reported in secret on advancing into Burma, I received the imperial instruction: 'If circumstances make action impossible, do not force the issue; deliberate carefully and act with discretion.

sentences.zh: '臣籌畫再三，竊謂渠魁不滅，有三患二難：李定國、白文選等分住三宣六慰，以擁戴為名，引潰眾肆擾，其患在門戶；

translations.literal: I have planned again and again and venture to say that if the chief rebel is not destroyed, there are three perils and two difficulties: Li Dingguo, Bai Wenxuan, and others are stationed separately in the Three Pacifications and Six Comforts, using support of the [Ming heir] as a pretext, drawing scattered troops to rampage at will—the peril lies at the gateway;
translations.idiomatic: After repeated deliberation I am convinced that if the chief rebel is not destroyed, three perils and two difficulties remain. Li Dingguo, Bai Wenxuan, and others are posted across the Three Pacifications and Six Comforts districts, rallying scattered troops under the banner of restoring the Ming heir. That peril lies at our very gates;

sentences.zh: 土司反覆，惟利是趨，一被煽惑，遍地蜂起，其患在肘腋；

translations.literal: the tribal chieftains are fickle and follow profit alone—once incited, they rise everywhere like swarming bees—the peril lies at the armpit;
translations.idiomatic: the tribal chieftains are fickle and follow profit wherever it leads. Once stirred up, they rise everywhere like swarming bees. That peril lies at our elbow;

sentences.zh: 投誠將士，尚未革心，萬一邊關有警，若輩乘隙而起，其患在腠理。

translations.literal: the surrendered officers and soldiers have not yet changed their hearts—if perchance the frontier should have an alarm, such men will seize the opportunity to rise—the peril lies in the flesh beneath the skin.
translations.idiomatic: the surrendered officers and soldiers have not yet truly changed their loyalties. Should the frontier face any alarm, they will seize the chance to rise. That peril lies in our very flesh.

sentences.zh: 且兵糧取之民間，無論各省餉運愆期，即到滇召買，民方懸磬，米價日增，公私交困，措糧之難如此；

translations.literal: Moreover, military grain is taken from the people; regardless of whether the transport of provisions from the provinces is delayed, even when grain is purchased in Yunnan, the people have nothing left in their pots, the price of rice rises daily, public and private affairs alike are distressed—such is the difficulty of securing provisions;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, military grain is drawn from the people. Even if provincial supply convoys arrive on time, purchases within Yunnan itself find the people with empty pots, rice prices rising daily, and both public and private affairs in distress. Securing provisions is as difficult as this;

sentences.zh: 年年召買，歲歲輸將，民力既盡，勢必逃亡，培養之難又如此。

translations.literal: Year after year purchases are summoned, year after year supplies are transported—the people's strength is exhausted and they must flee; the difficulty of nurturing them is again like this.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year the people are levied for purchases and year after year supplies must be transported. Once their strength is exhausted they will inevitably flee. The difficulty of sustaining the population is as great as this.

sentences.zh: 惟及時進兵，早收全局，乃救時之計。」

translations.literal: Only by advancing troops in timely fashion and recovering the whole situation early is this a plan to save the times."
translations.idiomatic: Only by advancing troops without delay and securing the entire situation at once can the present crisis be addressed."

sentences.zh: 下議政王大臣會戶、兵二部議，令學士麻勒吉、侍郎石圖如雲南諮三桂機宜，乃決策進兵。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the regent princes and ministers meeting with the Boards of Revenue and War; they ordered the academician Mele and Vice Minister Shi Tu to go to Yunnan to consult Sangui on strategy, and then decided to advance troops.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the regent princes and ministers in consultation with the Boards of Revenue and War. They ordered Academician Mele and Vice Minister Shi Tu to proceed to Yunnan to consult Wu Sangui on strategy, after which the decision to advance was made.

sentences.zh: 命內大臣愛星阿為定西將軍，率禁旅南征。

translations.literal: The inner minister Ai-xing-a was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and ordered to lead the forbidden troops on a southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The inner minister Ai-xing-a was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and ordered to lead the imperial guard south on campaign.

sentences.zh: 三桂所部五丁出一甲，甲二百置佐領，積數十佐領，以吳應麒、吳國貴為左、右都統分統之。

translations.literal: Among Sangui's troops one soldier was taken from every five men; every two hundred soldiers formed a zuoling, and when dozens of zuoling were accumulated, Wu Yingqi and Wu Guogui were made left and right commanders-in-chief to divide command.
translations.idiomatic: Among Wu Sangui's forces one soldier was levied from every five men. Every two hundred soldiers formed a zuoling company, and when dozens of such companies had been assembled, Wu Yingqi and Wu Guogui were appointed left and right commanders-in-chief to divide command among them.

sentences.zh: 七月，三桂疏請部勒降兵，分置十營，營千二百人，以降將為總兵：馬寶、李如碧、高啟隆、劉之复、塔新策將忠勇五營；

translations.literal: In the seventh month Sangui memorialized requesting to organize the surrendered troops into ten camps of twelve hundred men each, with surrendered generals as regional commanders: Ma Bao, Li Rubi, Gao Qilong, Liu Zhifu, and Ta Xince commanded the five Loyal and Brave camps;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Wu Sangui memorialized asking to organize the surrendered troops into ten camps of twelve hundred men each, with surrendered generals as regional commanders. Ma Bao, Li Rubi, Gao Qilong, Liu Zhifu, and Ta Xince commanded the five Loyal and Brave camps;

sentences.zh: 王會、劉偁、馬惟興、楊威、吳子聖將義勇五營。

translations.literal: Wang Hui, Liu Cheng, Ma Weixing, Yang Wei, and Wu Zisheng commanded the five Righteous and Brave camps.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui, Liu Cheng, Ma Weixing, Yang Wei, and Wu Zisheng commanded the five Righteous and Brave camps.

sentences.zh: 十月，又疏請置援剿四鎮，以馬寧、沈應時、王輔臣、楊武為總兵。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he again memorialized requesting establishment of four garrisons for relief and suppression, appointing Ma Ning, Shen Yingshi, Wang Fuchen, and Yang Wu as regional commanders.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he memorialized again asking to establish four garrisons for relief and suppression, with Ma Ning, Shen Yingshi, Wang Fuchen, and Yang Wu as regional commanders.

sentences.zh: 皆允之。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 三桂請拊循南甸、隴川、千崖、盞達、車裡諸土司，頒敕印；

translations.literal: Sangui requested to pacify and comfort the chieftains of Nandian, Longchuan, Qianya, Zhanda, Cheli, and others, and issue imperial patents and seals;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui asked to pacify the chieftains of Nandian, Longchuan, Qianya, Zhanda, Cheli, and other districts and to issue them imperial patents and seals;

sentences.zh: 复檄緬甸，令執由榔以獻。

translations.literal: and again sent a proclamation to Burma ordering them to seize Youlang and present him.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent a proclamation to Burma ordering them to seize Zhu Youlang and deliver him up.

sentences.zh: 定國、文選屢攻緬甸求出由榔，緬甸頻年被兵，患苦之，使告師破定國等，請以由榔獻。

translations.literal: Dingguo and Wenxuan repeatedly attacked Burma to bring Youlang out; Burma suffered from years of warfare and was distressed, and sent envoys asking the army to defeat Dingguo and others, offering to present Youlang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dingguo and Bai Wenxuan repeatedly attacked Burma to extract Zhu Youlang. Burma, worn down by years of warfare, sent envoys asking the Qing army to defeat Li Dingguo and the others and offering to hand over Zhu Youlang.

sentences.zh: 十八年，三桂遣使緬甸刻師期，令於猛卯迎師；

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Sangui sent envoys to Burma to fix the date of the army's arrival and ordered them to welcome the army at Mengmao;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Wu Sangui sent envoys to Burma to fix a date for the campaign and ordered the Burmese to welcome the army at Mengmao;

sentences.zh: 遣副都統何進忠及應時、寧等率師出騰越，道隴川，三月，至猛卯。

translations.literal: He dispatched the vice commander He Jinzhong together with Yingshi, Ning, and others to lead troops out from Tengyue, passing through Longchuan; in the third month they reached Mengmao.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Vice Commander He Jinzhong together with Shen Yingshi, Ma Ning, and others to lead troops from Tengyue by way of Longchuan. In the third month they reached Mengmao.

sentences.zh: 緬甸又與定國戰，道阻。

translations.literal: Burma was again fighting Dingguo, and the route was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Burma was again at war with Li Dingguo, and the route was blocked.

sentences.zh: 既，緬甸使至迎師，會瘴發，進忠等引還。

translations.literal: Later Burma's envoys came to welcome the army, but miasma broke out and Jinzhong and others withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Later Burmese envoys arrived to welcome the army, but malarial fever broke out and He Jinzhong and the others withdrew.

sentences.zh: 三桂以馬乃土司龍吉兆稱兵應定國，遣寶、啟隆及游擊趙良棟等討之，攻七十餘日，破其寨，斬吉兆，以其地為普安縣。

translations.literal: Sangui, because the Manai chieftain Long Jizhao had raised troops in support of Dingguo, sent Bao, Qilong, and the guerrilla officer Zhao Liangdong and others to suppress him; after more than seventy days of attack they broke his stockade, beheaded Jizhao, and made his territory Pu'an County.
translations.idiomatic: When the Manai chieftain Long Jizhao took up arms in support of Li Dingguo, Wu Sangui sent Ma Bao, Gao Qilong, and Guerrilla Officer Zhao Liangdong and others against him. After more than seventy days of fighting they stormed his stockade, killed Long Jizhao, and organized his territory as Pu'an County.

sentences.zh: 九月，瘴息。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the miasma subsided.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the malarial season ended.

sentences.zh: 三桂與愛星阿及前鋒統領白爾赫圖，都統果爾欽、遜塔等督兵攻大理，復出騰越，道南甸、隴川至猛卯，分兵二萬，遣寧、輔臣別取道姚關、鎮康、孟定；

translations.literal: Sangui together with Ai-xing-a, the vanguard commander Bai'ertu, and the commanders Guo'erqin, Xunta, and others supervised troops attacking Dali, again set out from Tengyue, passed through Nandian and Longchuan to Mengmao, divided twenty thousand troops, and sent Ning and Fuchen by another route through Yao Pass, Zhenkang, and Mengding;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui joined Ai-xing-a, Vanguard Commander Bai'ertu, and commanders Guo'erqin, Xunta, and others in an attack on Dali. They marched again from Tengyue by way of Nandian and Longchuan to Mengmao, detached twenty thousand men, and sent Ma Ning and Wang Fuchen by a separate route through Yao Pass, Zhenkang, and Mengding;

sentences.zh: 又慮蠻暮、猛密二土司助定國阻我師後，留總兵張國柱將三千人屯南甸為備。

translations.literal: He also feared that the chieftains of Manmu and Mengmi would assist Dingguo in blocking the army's rear, and left Regional Commander Zhang Guozhu with three thousand men stationed at Nandian as a precaution.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that the chieftains of Manmu and Mengmi might aid Li Dingguo in cutting off the army's rear, he left Regional Commander Zhang Guozhu with three thousand men encamped at Nandian as a precaution.

sentences.zh: 十一月，會師木邦。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the armies united at Mubang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the armies united at Mubang.

sentences.zh: 文選毀錫箔江橋走茶山，定國走景線。

translations.literal: Wenxuan destroyed the Xibo River bridge and fled to Chashan; Dingguo fled to Jingxian.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Wenxuan destroyed the bridge over the Xibo River and fled to Chashan, while Li Dingguo fled to Jingxian.

sentences.zh: 三桂令寧等以偏師逐文選，而與愛景阿趨緬甸，复檄令執送由榔。

translations.literal: Sangui ordered Ning and others with a detached force to pursue Wenxuan, while he himself with Ai-xing-a pressed toward Burma and again sent a proclamation ordering Youlang seized and delivered.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui ordered Ma Ning and others with a detached force to pursue Bai Wenxuan, while he and Ai-xing-a pressed on toward Burma and again demanded that Zhu Youlang be seized and delivered.

sentences.zh: 十二月，師進次舊晚坡，距緬甸都六十里。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the army advanced and halted at Jiuwanpo, sixty li from the Burmese capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the army advanced and encamped at Jiuwanpo, sixty li from the Burmese capital.

sentences.zh: 緬甸使告請遣兵進次蘭鳩江濱扞衛，乃遣白爾赫圖將百人以往。

translations.literal: Burmese envoys reported requesting troops advance to the banks of the Lanjiu River to guard them, and Bai'ertu was sent with a hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Burmese envoys asked that troops advance to the banks of the Lanjiu River to guard the crossing, and Bai'ertu was sent forward with a hundred men.

sentences.zh: 緬甸遂執由榔及其母、妻等送軍前。

translations.literal: Burma then seized Youlang together with his mother, wife, and others and sent them before the army.
translations.idiomatic: Burma then seized Zhu Youlang together with his mother, wife, and others and delivered them to the army.

sentences.zh: 寧等逐文選及於猛卯，文選以數千人降，師還。

translations.literal: Ning and others pursued Wenxuan as far as Mengmao; Wenxuan surrendered with several thousand men, and the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Ning and the others pursued Bai Wenxuan to Mengmao, where he surrendered with several thousand men. The army then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，捷聞，詔進三桂親王，並命兼轄貴州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi, news of victory arrived; an edict advanced Sangui to prince and ordered him to govern Guizhou as well.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kangxi, news of victory arrived. An edict promoted Wu Sangui to princely rank and placed Guizhou under his authority as well.

sentences.zh: 召愛星阿率師還。

translations.literal: Ai-xing-a was summoned to lead the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Ai-xing-a was recalled to lead the army back.

sentences.zh: 四月，三桂執由榔及其子，以弓弦絞殺之，送其母、妻詣京師，道自殺。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Sangui seized Youlang and his son and strangled them with bowstrings; he sent the mother and wife toward the capital, and they killed themselves on the road.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Wu Sangui seized Zhu Youlang and his son and strangled them with bowstrings. He sent the mother and wife toward the capital, but they killed themselves on the journey.

sentences.zh: 定國尚往來邊上伺由榔消息，三桂令提督張勇將萬餘人戍普洱、元江為備。

translations.literal: Dingguo was still moving along the frontier watching for news of Youlang; Sangui ordered the provincial commander Zhang Yong to lead more than ten thousand men to garrison Pu'er and Yuanjiang as a precaution.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dingguo was still moving along the frontier watching for news of Zhu Youlang. Wu Sangui ordered Provincial Commander Zhang Yong to garrison Pu'er and Yuanjiang with more than ten thousand men as a precaution.

sentences.zh: 未幾，定國走死猛臘。

translations.literal: Before long Dingguo fled and died at Mengla.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Dingguo fled and died at Mengla.

sentences.zh: 三桂招其子嗣興，以千餘人降，明亡。

translations.literal: Sangui recruited his son Suxing, who surrendered with more than a thousand men—the Ming perished.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui won over his son Li Suxing, who surrendered with more than a thousand men. With that the Ming cause was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 二年，遣會等攻隴納山蠻，破巢，斬渠。

translations.literal: In the second year he sent Hui and others to attack the Longna mountain tribes, broke their lair, and beheaded their leader.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he sent Wang Hui and others against the Longna mountain tribes, destroyed their stronghold, and killed their leader.

sentences.zh: 三年，遣之复及總兵李世耀率兵出大方、烏蒙，攻水西土司安坤、烏撒土司安重聖，並擊斬之，以其地設府：隴納曰平遠，大方曰大定，水西曰黔西，烏撒曰威寧。

translations.literal: In the third year he sent Zhifu and Regional Commander Li Shiyao to lead troops out from Dafang and Wumeng to attack the Shuixi chieftain An Kun and the Wusa chieftain An Zhongsheng, attacking and beheading both; their territories were made prefectures: Longna as Pingyuan, Dafang as Dading, Shuixi as Qianxi, and Wusa as Weining.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he sent Liu Zhifu and Regional Commander Li Shiyao from Dafang and Wumeng against the Shuixi chieftain An Kun and the Wusa chieftain An Zhongsheng, killing both. Their territories were organized as prefectures: Longna became Pingyuan, Dafang became Dading, Shuixi became Qianxi, and Wusa became Weining.

sentences.zh: 四年，奏裁雲南綠旗兵五千有奇。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he memorialized to reduce Yunnan's Green Standard troops by more than five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he memorialized to cut Yunnan's Green Standard forces by more than five thousand men.

sentences.zh: 五年，復遣兵攻土司祿昌賢於隴箐，取其寨數十。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he again sent troops to attack the chieftain Lu Changxian at Longqing and took several dozen of his stockades.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he again sent troops against the chieftain Lu Changxian at Longqing and captured several dozen of his stockades.

sentences.zh: 迤東悉定，設府曰開化，州曰永定。

translations.literal: The entire eastern region was pacified; a prefecture called Kaihua and a subprefecture called Yongding were established.
translations.idiomatic: The entire eastern region was pacified. A prefecture named Kaihua and a subprefecture named Yongding were established.

sentences.zh: 三桂初以開關迎師，位望出諸降將孔有德、耿仲明、尚可喜輩右。

translations.literal: Sangui had at first opened the pass to welcome the army, and his position and prestige stood above the other surrendered generals Kong Youde, Geng Zhongming, Shang Kexi, and their like.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui had first opened the pass to welcome the Qing army, and his standing surpassed that of fellow surrendered generals such as Kong Youde, Geng Zhongming, and Shang Kexi.

sentences.zh: 有德專徵定湖廣，徇廣西，李定國破桂林，殉焉；

translations.literal: Youde was specially commissioned to pacify Huguang, subdued Guangxi, and died when Li Dingguo broke Guilin;
translations.idiomatic: Kong Youde was commissioned to pacify Huguang, subdued Guangxi, and died when Li Dingguo captured Guilin;

sentences.zh: 可喜與仲明子繼茂分兵定廣東、福建；

translations.literal: Kexi together with Zhongming's son Jimaomao divided forces to pacify Guangdong and Fujian;
translations.idiomatic: Shang Kexi and Geng Zhongming's son Jimaomao divided their forces to pacify Guangdong and Fujian;

sentences.zh: 而三桂功最高。

translations.literal: but Sangui's achievements were the highest.
translations.idiomatic: but Wu Sangui's achievements were the greatest.

sentences.zh: 雲、貴初定，洪承疇疏用明黔國公沐英故事，請以三桂世鎮雲南。

translations.literal: When Yunnan and Guizhou were first pacified, Hong Chengchou memorialized citing the Ming precedent of the Prince of Qian Mu Ying, requesting that Sangui hereditarily garrison Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: When Yunnan and Guizhou were first pacified, Hong Chengchou memorialized citing the Ming precedent of Prince Mu Ying of Qian, asking that Wu Sangui be established as hereditary governor of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 三桂復請敕雲南督撫受節制，移總督駐貴陽，提督駐大理。

translations.literal: Sangui again requested an edict that Yunnan's governor and provincial administration commissioner be placed under his command, that the governor-general be moved to Guiyang, and the provincial commander to Dali.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui further asked that an edict place Yunnan's governor and administration commissioner under his command, move the governor-general to Guiyang, and station the provincial commander at Dali.

sentences.zh: 據由榔所居五華山故宮為籓府，增華崇麗。

translations.literal: He took the former palace on Wuhua Mountain where Youlang had resided as his princely mansion and made it more splendid and magnificent.
translations.idiomatic: He took the former palace on Wuhua Mountain where Zhu Youlang had lived as his princely residence and enlarged it into a lavish mansion.

sentences.zh: 籍沐天波莊田七百頃為籓莊。

translations.literal: He registered seven hundred qing of manor fields belonging to Mu Tianbo as princely estates.
translations.idiomatic: He seized seven hundred qing of manor land belonging to Mu Tianbo and made it princely estates.

sentences.zh: 假濬渠築城為名，重榷關市，壟鹽井、金銅礦山之利，厚自封殖。

translations.literal: Under the pretext of dredging canals and building walls, he heavily taxed markets and passes, monopolized the profits of salt wells and gold and copper mines, and greatly enriched himself.
translations.idiomatic: Under the pretext of dredging canals and building fortifications, he imposed heavy taxes on markets and passes, monopolized profits from salt wells and gold and copper mines, and amassed enormous wealth for himself.

sentences.zh: 通使達賴喇嘛，互市北勝州。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to the Dalai Lama and conducted mutual trade at Beisheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He exchanged envoys with the Dalai Lama and conducted trade at Beisheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遼東參，四川黃連、附子，就其地採運，官為之鬻，收其值。

translations.literal: Liaodong ginseng, Sichuan coptis, and aconite were gathered and transported locally, sold by official agency, and their value collected.
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong ginseng, Sichuan coptis, and aconite were gathered and transported locally, sold through official channels, and the proceeds collected for his treasury.

sentences.zh: 貨財充溢，貸諸富賈，謂之「籓本」。

translations.literal: Goods and wealth overflowed; he lent to wealthy merchants—this was called "princely capital."
translations.idiomatic: His stores of goods and wealth overflowed. He lent money to wealthy merchants under the name "princely capital."

sentences.zh: 權子母，斥其羨以餌士大夫之無藉者。

translations.literal: He charged interest on principal and spent the surplus to win over needy scholars and officials.
translations.idiomatic: He charged interest on the principal and used the surplus to win over needy scholars and officials.

sentences.zh: 擇諸將子弟，四方賓客，與肄武備，謂以儲將帥之選。

translations.literal: He selected the sons of his generals and guests from all quarters to study military affairs, saying this was to store up candidates for command.
translations.idiomatic: He selected the sons of his generals and guests from all quarters to train in military affairs, claiming this was to cultivate future commanders.

sentences.zh: 部兵多李自成、張獻忠百戰之餘，勇健善鬥，以時訓練。

translations.literal: His troops were mostly veterans of a hundred battles under Li Zicheng and Zhang Xianzhong, brave, hardy, and skilled in fighting, and were trained on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: His troops were mostly veterans of Li Zicheng's and Zhang Xianzhong's armies, hardened by a hundred battles, brave and skilled in combat, and he drilled them regularly.

sentences.zh: 所轄文武將吏，選用自擅。

translations.literal: The civil and military officers under his jurisdiction were selected and appointed at his own discretion.
translations.idiomatic: The civil and military officers under his command were appointed entirely at his own discretion.

sentences.zh: 各省員缺，時亦承製除授，謂之「西選」。

translations.literal: Vacancies in the provinces were at times filled by commission on his authority—this was called the "western selection."
translations.idiomatic: Vacancies in the provinces were at times filled on his own authority—this was called the "western selection."

sentences.zh: 又屢引京朝官、各省將吏用以自佐。

translations.literal: He also repeatedly drew in capital officials and provincial officers and generals to serve as his assistants.
translations.idiomatic: He also repeatedly recruited capital officials and provincial officers and generals to serve on his staff.

sentences.zh: 御史楊素蘊疏論劾，三桂摘疏中「防微杜漸」語，請旨詰素蘊。

translations.literal: The censor Yang Suyun memorialized impeaching him; Sangui seized on the phrase in the memorial "guard against the first signs and stop gradual encroachment" and requested an imperial order to interrogate Suyun.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yang Suyun memorialized impeaching him. Wu Sangui seized on the phrase in the memorial about "guarding against the first signs and stopping gradual encroachment" and asked the throne to interrogate Yang Suyun.

sentences.zh: 素蘊覆奏，言「防微杜漸，古今通義。」

translations.literal: Suyun replied in a further memorial, saying "Guarding against the first signs and stopping gradual encroachment is a universal principle of ancient and modern times."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Suyun replied in a further memorial: "Guarding against the first signs and stopping gradual encroachment is a universal principle of ancient and modern times."

sentences.zh: 事遂寢。

translations.literal: The matter was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was then dropped.

sentences.zh: 六年，三桂疏言兩目昏瞀，精力日減，辭總管雲、貴兩省事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Sangui memorialized that both eyes were dim and his energy daily diminished, and resigned overall charge of Yunnan and Guizhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Wu Sangui memorialized that his eyes were growing dim and his strength daily failing, and resigned overall charge of Yunnan and Guizhou affairs.

sentences.zh: 下部議，如各省例，歸督撫管理，文吏由吏部題授。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the ministries; following the precedent of other provinces, affairs were returned to the governor-general and governor, and civil officials were appointed through the Board of Civil Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the ministries. Following the precedent of other provinces, affairs were returned to the governor-general and governor, and civil officials were to be appointed through the Board of Civil Appointments.

sentences.zh: 雲貴總督卞三元、雲南提督張國柱、貴州提督李本深交章陳三桂勞績，請敕仍總管。

translations.literal: The Yunnan-Guizhou governor-general Bian Sanyuan, Yunnan provincial commander Zhang Guozhu, and Guizhou provincial commander Li Benshen submitted successive memorials stating Sangui's merits and requesting an edict that he still hold overall charge.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Bian Sanyuan of Yunnan and Guizhou, Yunnan Provincial Commander Zhang Guozhu, and Guizhou Provincial Commander Li Benshen submitted successive memorials praising Wu Sangui's achievements and asking that he retain overall authority.

sentences.zh: 得旨：「王以精力日減奏辭，若召仍令總管，恐其過勞。

translations.literal: The response came: "The Prince memorialized resignation because his energy daily diminishes; if summoned and still ordered to hold overall charge, I fear he would be overtaxed.
translations.idiomatic: The response came: "The prince memorialized his resignation because his strength is daily failing. If he were recalled and still ordered to hold overall charge, I fear he would be overtaxed.

sentences.zh: 如邊疆遇有軍事，王自應經理。」

translations.literal: If the frontier should encounter military affairs, the Prince himself should manage them."
translations.idiomatic: If military affairs arise on the frontier, the prince himself should manage them."

sentences.zh: 尋進應熊少傅兼太子太傅，命赴雲南視疾，仍還京師。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Yingxiong was advanced to Junior Tutor and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, ordered to go to Yunnan to inquire after his father's illness, and then return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Wu Yingxiong was promoted to Junior Tutor and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and ordered to go to Yunnan to inquire after his father's health, then return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 三桂益欲攬事權，構釁苗、蠻，藉事用兵，私割中甸畀諸番屯牧，通商互市。

translations.literal: Sangui increasingly wished to seize administrative power, provoked conflicts with the Miao and tribal peoples, used incidents as pretexts for military action, privately ceded Zhongdian to various tribes for pasture, and conducted trade and mutual markets.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui increasingly sought to seize administrative power. He provoked conflicts with Miao and tribal peoples, used incidents as pretexts for military action, privately ceded Zhongdian to various tribes for pasture, and conducted trade across the border.

sentences.zh: 迨三元乞歸養，甘文焜代為總督，不附三桂。

translations.literal: When Sanyuan requested leave to return home for parental care, Gan Wenkan replaced him as governor-general and would not attach himself to Sangui.
translations.idiomatic: When Bian Sanyuan requested leave to retire and care for his parents, Gan Wenkan replaced him as governor-general and refused to align himself with Wu Sangui.

sentences.zh: 三桂詐稱邊寇，檄赴剿；

translations.literal: Sangui falsely claimed border bandits and issued a dispatch ordering him to go suppress them;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui falsely reported border bandits and issued a dispatch ordering him to go suppress them;

sentences.zh: 比至，又稱寇退，檄使還。

translations.literal: when he arrived, he again claimed the bandits had retreated and issued a dispatch ordering him to return.
translations.idiomatic: when Gan Wenkan arrived, Wu Sangui claimed the bandits had withdrawn and ordered him to return.

sentences.zh: 籓屬將吏士卒糜俸餉鉅萬，各省輸稅不足，徵諸江南，歲二千餘萬，絀則連章入告，贏不復請稽核。

translations.literal: The princely domain's officers, soldiers, and troops consumed salaries and provisions in the millions; provincial tax deliveries were insufficient and levies were imposed on Jiangnan of more than twenty million annually—if short they submitted successive memorials reporting it, if in surplus they no longer requested audit.
translations.idiomatic: The officers and soldiers of the princely domain consumed salaries and provisions totaling millions. Provincial tax deliveries fell short, so levies were imposed on Jiangnan of more than twenty million taels a year. When funds ran short they submitted successive memorials reporting the deficit; when they had a surplus they no longer asked for an audit.

sentences.zh: 是時可喜鎮廣東，繼茂子精忠鎮福建，與三桂並稱「三籓」，而三桂驕恣尤甚。

translations.literal: At this time Kexi garrisoned Guangdong and Jimaomao's son Jingzhong garrisoned Fujian; together with Sangui they were called the "Three Feudatories," but Sangui's arrogance and willfulness were especially extreme.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Shang Kexi garrisoned Guangdong and Jimaomao's son Geng Jingzhong garrisoned Fujian. Together with Wu Sangui they were known as the Three Feudatories, but Wu Sangui's arrogance and willfulness were the most extreme of all.

sentences.zh: 十二年二月，上遣侍衛吳丹、塞扈立勞三桂，賜御用貂帽、團龍裘、青蟒狐腋袍、束帶，亦遣使賚可喜。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twelfth year the emperor sent the bodyguards Wu Dan and Saihuli to console Sangui, bestowing an imperial sable hat, dragon-round robe, blue python and fox-axilla robe, and girdle; envoys were also sent with gifts for Kexi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twelfth year the emperor sent bodyguards Wu Dan and Saihuli to console Wu Sangui, granting him an imperial sable hat, dragon-round robe, blue python and fox-fur robe, and girdle. Envoys were also sent with gifts for Shang Kexi.

sentences.zh: 可喜旋疏引疾乞歸老，下部議，請並移所部。

translations.literal: Kexi soon memorialized citing illness and begging to retire; the matter was referred to the ministries, which proposed moving his troops as well.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Kexi soon memorialized citing illness and asking to retire. The matter was referred to the ministries, which proposed relocating his troops as well.

sentences.zh: 七月，三桂亦疏請移籓，並言：「所部繁眾，昔自漢中移雲南，閱三歲始畢。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Sangui also memorialized requesting transfer of his princedom, further stating: "My following is numerous and crowded; formerly when moving from Hanzhong to Yunnan, it took three years to complete.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Wu Sangui also memorialized requesting transfer of his princedom, further stating: "My following is numerous. When we moved from Hanzhong to Yunnan in the past, it took three years to complete the relocation.

sentences.zh: 今生齒彌增，乞賜土地，視世祖時分畀錦州、寧遠諸區倍廣，庶安輯得所。」

translations.literal: Now our numbers have greatly increased; I beg land be granted twice as broad as the Jinzhou, Ningyuan, and other districts allotted in the Shizu Emperor's time, so that settlement may be properly arranged."
translations.idiomatic: Our numbers have greatly increased since then. I beg that land be granted to us twice as extensive as the Jinzhou, Ningyuan, and other districts allotted in the Shunzhi era, so that my people may be properly settled."

sentences.zh: 聖祖察三籓分鎮擅兵為國患，得三桂疏，下議政王大臣會戶、兵二部議奏。

translations.literal: The Shengzu Emperor perceived that the Three Feudatories' separate garrisons and monopoly of troops were a national peril; receiving Sangui's memorial, he referred it to the regent princes and ministers meeting with the Boards of Revenue and War for deliberation and report.
translations.idiomatic: The Kangxi Emperor had long seen the Three Feudatories' separate garrisons and monopoly of troops as a threat to the state. Receiving Wu Sangui's memorial, he referred it to the regent princes and ministers in consultation with the Boards of Revenue and War.

sentences.zh: 諸王大臣度三桂疏非由衷，遽議遷徙，必致紛紜，議移籓不便；

translations.literal: The princes and ministers judged that Sangui's memorial was not sincere; to deliberate hastily on relocation would certainly cause turmoil, and they argued that transferring the princedom was inconvenient;
translations.idiomatic: The princes and ministers judged that Wu Sangui's memorial was not sincere. To deliberate hastily on relocation would certainly cause turmoil, and they argued that transferring the princedom was inadvisable;

sentences.zh: 獨尚書米思翰、明珠謂苗、蠻既平，三桂不宜久鎮，議移籓便。

translations.literal: only the ministers Misihan and Mingzhu said that since the Miao and tribal peoples were already pacified, Sangui should not long garrison the region, and argued that transferring the princedom was expedient.
translations.idiomatic: only Ministers Misihan and Mingzhu argued that since the Miao and tribal peoples were already pacified, Wu Sangui should not remain in long-term garrison there and that transferring the princedom was expedient.

sentences.zh: 乃為二議以上：一議移三桂山海關外，別遣滿洲兵戍雲南；

translations.literal: Two proposals were then submitted: one proposed moving Sangui beyond Shanhaiguan and separately dispatching Manchu troops to garrison Yunnan;
translations.idiomatic: Two proposals were then submitted: one proposed moving Wu Sangui beyond Shanhaiguan and separately dispatching Manchu troops to garrison Yunnan;

sentences.zh: 一議留三桂鎮雲南如故。

translations.literal: the other proposed leaving Sangui to garrison Yunnan as before.
translations.idiomatic: the other proposed leaving Wu Sangui to garrison Yunnan as before.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「三桂蓄異志久，撤亦反，不撤亦反。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Sangui has long harbored rebellious designs; if removed he will rebel, if not removed he will also rebel.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Wu Sangui has long harbored rebellious designs. If we remove him he will rebel; if we do not remove him he will rebel anyway.

sentences.zh: 不若及今先發，猶可製也。」

translations.literal: Better to strike first now while he can still be controlled."
translations.idiomatic: Better to strike first now, while he can still be controlled."

sentences.zh: 遂命允三桂請移籓，並諭如當用滿洲兵，仍俟三桂奏請遣發。

translations.literal: He then ordered Sangui's request to transfer the princedom granted, and instructed that when Manchu troops should be used, they would still await Sangui's memorial requesting their dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: He then granted Wu Sangui's request to transfer his princedom, adding that when Manchu troops were needed, dispatch would still await Wu Sangui's memorial requesting them.

sentences.zh: 即令侍郎折爾肯、學士傅達禮齎詔諭三桂。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered Vice Minister Zhe'erken and Academician Fudali to carry the edict and instruct Sangui.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered Vice Minister Zhe'erken and Academician Fudali to carry the edict to Wu Sangui.

sentences.zh: 三桂初上疏，度廷議未即許，冀慰留久鎮。

translations.literal: When Sangui first submitted his memorial, he judged that court deliberation would not immediately approve it and hoped to be comforted and retained in long-term garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui first submitted his memorial, he expected that the court would not immediately approve it and hoped to be comforted and allowed to remain in long-term garrison.

sentences.zh: 九月，詔使至，三桂大失望。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the edict-bearers arrived, and Sangui was greatly disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the imperial envoys arrived, and Wu Sangui was deeply disappointed.

sentences.zh: 與所部都統吳應麒、吳國貴，副都統高大節及其壻夏國相、胡國柱謀為亂，部署腹心扼關隘，聽入不聽出，與使者期以十一月己丑發雲南。

translations.literal: Together with his commanders-in-chief Wu Yingqi and Wu Guogui, vice commander Gao Dajie, and his sons-in-law Xia Guoxiang and Hu Guozhu he plotted rebellion, deployed trusted men to hold the passes—allowing entry but not exit—and agreed with the envoys to depart Yunnan on jichou of the eleventh month.
translations.idiomatic: Together with his commanders-in-chief Wu Yingqi and Wu Guogui, Vice Commander Gao Dajie, and his sons-in-law Xia Guoxiang and Hu Guozhu he plotted rebellion. He posted trusted men to hold the passes, allowing entry but not exit, and agreed with the envoys to depart Yunnan on the jichou day of the eleventh month.

sentences.zh: 先三日丙戌，邀巡撫硃國治脅之叛，不從，榜殺之。

translations.literal: Three days earlier on bingxu he invited the governor Zhu Guozhi and coerced him to rebel; when he refused, he had him publicly executed.
translations.idiomatic: Three days earlier, on the bingxu day, he summoned Governor Zhu Guozhi and tried to force him to rebel. When Zhu refused, Wu Sangui had him publicly executed.

sentences.zh: 遂召諸總兵寶、啟隆、之复、足法、會、屏籓等舉兵反，自號周王天下都招討兵馬大元帥。

translations.literal: He then summoned the regional commanders Bao, Qilong, Zhifu, Zufa, Hui, Pingfan, and others to raise troops in rebellion, styling himself Grand Marshal of All Forces for Suppression under the Zhou King Who Pacifies the Realm.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned regional commanders including Ma Bao, Gao Qilong, Liu Zhifu, Zufa, Wang Hui, and Pingfan to raise troops in rebellion, styling himself Grand Marshal of All Forces for Suppression under the Zhou King Who Pacifies the Realm.

sentences.zh: 蓄髮，易衣冠，幟色白，步騎皆以白氈為帽。

translations.literal: He grew his hair long, changed clothing and caps, used white banners, and both infantry and cavalry wore white felt caps.
translations.idiomatic: He grew his hair long again, changed clothing and caps to Ming style, used white banners, and had both infantry and cavalry wear white felt caps.

sentences.zh: 執折爾肯、傅達禮，按察使李興元，知府高顯辰，同知劉昆，不為三桂屈，具楚毒，徙置瘴地。

translations.literal: He seized Zhe'erken and Fudali, the provincial surveillance commissioner Li Xingyuan, the prefect Gao Xianchen, and the subprefect Liu Kun; when they would not submit to Sangui, they were subjected to cruel torture and exiled to miasmal regions.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Zhe'erken and Fudali, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Li Xingyuan, Prefect Gao Xianchen, and Subprefect Liu Kun. When they refused to submit, he subjected them to cruel torture and exiled them to malarial regions.

sentences.zh: 國柱及總兵杜輝、柯鐸，布政使崔之瑛等皆降。

translations.literal: Guozhu and the regional commanders Du Hui and Ke Duo, the provincial administration commissioner Cui Zhiying, and others all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guozhu and regional commanders Du Hui and Ke Duo, Administration Commissioner Cui Zhiying, and others all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 三桂傳檄遠近，並致書平南、靖南二籓，及貴州、四川、湖廣、陝西諸將吏與相識者，要約響應。

translations.literal: Sangui circulated proclamations far and near, and also sent letters to the Princes Who Pacify the South and Pacify the West, and to officers and officials in Guizhou, Sichuan, Huguang, Shaanxi, and others he knew, arranging mutual response.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui circulated proclamations far and wide and sent letters to the Princes Who Pacify the South and Pacify the West, as well as to officers and officials in Guizhou, Sichuan, Huguang, Shaanxi, and elsewhere whom he knew, urging them to rise in concert.

sentences.zh: 遣馬寶將兵前驅向貴陽，李本深謀應之。

translations.literal: He sent Ma Bao with troops as vanguard toward Guiyang; Li Benshen plotted to respond.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Ma Bao with troops as vanguard toward Guiyang, while Li Benshen plotted to join the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 文焜馳書告川湖總督蔡毓榮，並趣折爾肯、傅達禮從官郎中黨務禮、員外郎薩穆哈、主事辛珠、筆帖式薩爾圖速還京師告變。

translations.literal: Wenkan urgently sent letters informing the Sichuan-Huguang governor-general Cai Yurong, and urged Zhe'erken and Fudali's attendants—the director Dang Wuli, vice director Samuha, secretary Xin Zhu, and clerk Sa'ertu—to hurry back to the capital and report the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Wenkan urgently sent word to Sichuan-Huguang Governor-General Cai Yurong and urged the attendants of Zhe'erken and Fudali—Director Dang Wuli, Vice Director Samuha, Secretary Xin Zhu, and Clerk Sa'ertu—to hurry back to the capital and report the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 三桂遣騎追之，辛珠、薩爾圖為所殺。

translations.literal: Sangui sent cavalry in pursuit; Xin Zhu and Sa'ertu were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui sent cavalry in pursuit. Xin Zhu and Sa'ertu were killed.

sentences.zh: 文焜率數騎趨鎮遠，鎮遠副將江義已得三桂檄，以兵圍文焜，文焜死之。

translations.literal: Wenkan led several horsemen toward Zhenyuan; the Zhenyuan vice commander Jiang Yi had already received Sangui's proclamation and surrounded Wenkan with troops—Wenkan died.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Wenkan rode with a small escort toward Zhenyuan, but Vice Commander Jiang Yi had already received Wu Sangui's proclamation and surrounded him with troops. Gan Wenkan was killed.

sentences.zh: 寶兵至，巡撫曹申吉、總兵王永清皆降。

translations.literal: When Bao's troops arrived, the governor Cao Shenji and regional commander Wang Yongqing both surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Bao's troops arrived, Governor Cao Shenji and Regional Commander Wang Yongqing both surrendered.

sentences.zh: 十二月，黨務禮、薩穆哈至京師，三桂反問聞。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Dang Wuli and Samuha reached the capital, and news of Sangui's rebellion was heard.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Dang Wuli and Samuha reached the capital, and news of Wu Sangui's rebellion arrived.

sentences.zh: 上以荊州咽喉地，即日遣前鋒統領碩岱率禁旅馳赴鎮守。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Jingzhou was a strategic throat-point, that same day dispatched the vanguard commander Shuodai to lead the forbidden troops in haste to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jingzhou was a strategic choke point, the emperor that same day dispatched Vanguard Commander Shuodai with the imperial guard to garrison it at once.

sentences.zh: 尋命順承郡王勒爾錦為寧南靖寇大將軍，率師討三桂，分遣將軍赫業入四川，副都統馬哈達、擴爾坤駐軍兗州、太原備調遣，並停撤平南、靖南二籓。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the emperor appointed Prince Shuncheng Le'erjin as Grand General for Pacifying the South and Quelling Rebels, leading an army to campaign against Sangui; he dispatched General Heyeh into Sichuan, and had the vice commandants-in-chief Mahada and Kuo'erkun station troops at Yanzhou and Taiyuan in readiness for deployment, and also halted the withdrawal of the Pingnan and Jingnan feudatories.
