translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, the emperor appointed Prince Shuncheng Le'erjin Grand General for Pacifying the South and Quelling Rebels and sent him at the head of an army against Wu Sangui. He dispatched General Heyeh into Sichuan and stationed Vice Commandants-in-Chief Mahada and Kuo'erkun at Yanzhou and Taiyuan to hold troops in reserve, while also halting the planned withdrawal of the Pingnan and Jingnan feudatories.

sentences.zh: 王大臣等請逮應熊治罪，命暫行拘禁。

translations.literal: Wang Dachen and others requested that Yingxiong be arrested and punished; the emperor ordered that he be placed under temporary detention.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dachen and others asked that Wu Yingxiong be arrested and punished. The emperor ordered that he be placed under temporary detention.

sentences.zh: 三桂兵陷清浪衛；

translations.literal: Sangui's troops captured Qinglangwei;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui's forces captured Qinglangwei.

sentences.zh: 毓榮​​遣總兵崔世祿防沅州，三桂兵至，以城降；

translations.literal: Yurong dispatched regional commander Cui Shilu to defend Yuanzhou; when Sangui's troops arrived, he surrendered the city;
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yurong dispatched Regional Commander Cui Shilu to defend Yuanzhou, but when Wu Sangui's troops arrived, Cui surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 復進陷辰州。

translations.literal: They then advanced and captured Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then advanced and captured Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 十三年正月，三桂僭稱周王元年，部署諸將：楊寶廕陷常德，夏國相陷澧州，張國柱陷衡州，吳應麒陷岳州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirteenth year Sangui presumptuously proclaimed the first year of the Zhou King, deploying his generals: Yang Baoban captured Changde, Xia Guoxiang captured Lizhou, Zhang Guozhu captured Hengzhou, and Wu Yingqi captured Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the thirteenth year, Wu Sangui presumptuously declared the first year of his Zhou dynasty and deployed his generals: Yang Baoban took Changde, Xia Guoxiang took Lizhou, Zhang Guozhu took Hengzhou, and Wu Yingqi took Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 偏沅巡撫盧震棄長沙走，副將黃正卿、參將陳武衡以城降。

translations.literal: The Pianyuan governor Lü Zhen abandoned Changsha and fled; vice commander Huang Zhengqing and battalion commander Chen Wuheng surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Pianyuan Governor Lü Zhen abandoned Changsha and fled. Vice Commander Huang Zhengqing and Battalion Commander Chen Wuheng surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 襄陽總兵楊來嘉舉兵叛，鄖陽副將洪福舉兵攻提督佟國瑤，擊破之；

translations.literal: The Xiangyang regional commander Yang Laijia raised troops in rebellion; the Yunyang vice commander Hong Fu raised troops and attacked the provincial commander Tong Guoyao, defeating him;
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyang Regional Commander Yang Laijia rose in rebellion, and Yunyang Vice Commander Hong Fu took up arms and attacked Provincial Commander Tong Guoyao, routing him.

sentences.zh: 走保山寨，皆應三桂，受署置。

translations.literal: They fled to hold mountain stockades; all responded to Sangui and accepted appointments from him.
translations.idiomatic: They withdrew into mountain redoubts, all declared for Wu Sangui, and accepted posts under his authority.

sentences.zh: 三桂自雲南至常德，具疏付折爾肯、傅達禮還奏，語不遜。

translations.literal: Sangui went from Yunnan to Changde, prepared a memorial and gave it to Zhe'erken and Fudali to return and report, with language that was not deferential.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui traveled from Yunnan to Changde and sent a memorial back to court through Zhe'erken and Fudali, couched in impertinent language.

sentences.zh: 上命誅應熊及其子世霖，諸幼子貸死入官。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Yingxiong and his son Shilin put to death; the younger sons were spared death and enrolled as bondservants of the government.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Wu Yingxiong and his son Wu Shilin executed. The younger sons were spared death and enrolled as government bondsmen.

sentences.zh: 六月，命貝勒尚善為安遠靖寇大將軍，與勒爾錦分道進兵。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he appointed Prince Shangshan as Grand General for Pacifying the Distant and Quelling Rebels, to advance by a separate route with Le'erjin.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, the emperor appointed Prince Shangshan Grand General for Pacifying the Distant and Quelling Rebels to advance along a separate route from Le'erjin.

sentences.zh: 是時雲南、貴州、湖南地皆入三桂，通番市，以茶易馬，結倮儸助戰，伐木造巨艦，治舟師，採銅鑄錢，文曰「利用。」

translations.literal: At this time the territories of Yunnan, Guizhou, and Hunan had all fallen to Sangui; he opened markets with frontier peoples, traded tea for horses, allied with the Luoluo to assist in warfare, felled trees to build great warships, organized a naval force, mined copper to cast coins bearing the inscription "Li Yong."
translations.idiomatic: By then Yunnan, Guizhou, and Hunan had all fallen under Wu Sangui's control. He opened frontier markets, traded tea for horses, enlisted the Luoluo to fight for him, cut timber to build large warships, organized a naval force, and mined copper to cast coins bearing the inscription "Li Yong."

sentences.zh: 所至掠庫金、倉粟，資軍用。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he plundered treasury gold and granary grain to supply military expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever his forces went they looted treasury funds and storehouse grain to pay for the war effort.

sentences.zh: 勒爾錦師次荊州，三桂遣劉之复、王會、陶繼智等屢以舟師攻彝陵，勒爾錦遣將屢擊敗之，未即渡江。

translations.literal: Le'erjin's army halted at Jingzhou; Sangui sent Liu Zhifu, Wang Hui, Tao Jizhi, and others repeatedly to attack Yiling with a naval force; Le'erjin dispatched generals who repeatedly defeated them, but did not immediately cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: Le'erjin halted his army at Jingzhou. Wu Sangui sent Liu Zhifu, Wang Hui, Tao Jizhi, and others repeatedly against Yiling with his fleet, but Le'erjin's generals drove them back each time and did not immediately cross the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 尚善師次武昌，以書諭三桂降，置不答。

translations.literal: Shangshan's army halted at Wuchang; he sent a letter urging Sangui to surrender, but received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Shangshan halted at Wuchang and sent a letter urging Wu Sangui to surrender, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 三桂傳檄所至，反者四起：提督鄭蛟麟，總兵譚弘、吳之茂反四川，巡撫羅森、降將軍孫延齡以有德舊部反廣西，精忠反福建，河北總兵蔡祿反彰德，三桂勢益張；

translations.literal: Wherever Sangui's proclamation spread, rebellions arose on all sides: provincial commander Zheng Jiaolin, regional commanders Tan Hong and Wu Zhimao rebelled in Sichuan; governor Luo Sen and the surrendered general Sun Yanling rebelled in Guangxi with Youde's old troops; Jingzhong rebelled in Fujian; the Hebei regional commander Cai Lu rebelled at Zhangde; Sangui's power grew ever greater;
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Wu Sangui's manifestos reached, rebels rose on all sides. Provincial Commander Zheng Jiaolin, Regional Commanders Tan Hong and Wu Zhimao rebelled in Sichuan; Governor Luo Sen and the surrendered general Sun Yanling revolted in Guangxi with troops from Wu Sangui's former command; Geng Jingzhong rebelled in Fujian; Hebei Regional Commander Cai Lu rose at Zhangde. Wu Sangui's power grew ever greater.

sentences.zh: 又遣使與達賴喇嘛通好。

translations.literal: He also sent envoys to establish friendly relations with the Dalai Lama.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent envoys to establish friendly relations with the Dalai Lama.

sentences.zh: 達賴喇嘛為上書乞罷兵，上弗許。

translations.literal: The Dalai Lama wrote a letter to the emperor on his behalf begging that hostilities cease; the emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: The Dalai Lama wrote to the emperor on Wu Sangui's behalf begging that the war be halted, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 先後遣經略大學士莫洛、大將軍康親王杰書、貝勒董額等四出征撫，將軍阿密達擒祿誅之。

translations.literal: Successively he dispatched the frontier coordinator Grand Secretary Mo Luo, the Grand General Prince Kang Jieshu, Prince Dong'e, and others on four campaigns to suppress and pacify; General Amida captured Lu and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor in succession dispatched Frontier Coordinator Grand Secretary Mo Luo, Grand General Prince Kang Jieshu, Prince Dong'e, and others on four separate pacification campaigns. General Amida captured Cai Lu and executed him.

sentences.zh: 上趣尚善攻岳州，三桂使吳應麒、廖進忠、馬寶、張國柱、柯鐸、高啟隆等分道拒戰，又遣兵窺江西，循江達南康，陷都昌；

translations.literal: The emperor urgently pressed Shangshan to attack Yuezhou; Sangui had Wu Yingqi, Liao Jinzhong, Ma Bao, Zhang Guozhu, Ke Duo, Gao Qilong, and others resist in separate routes; he also sent troops to probe Jiangxi, followed the river to Nankang, and captured Duchang;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor urgently pressed Shangshan to attack Yuezhou. Wu Sangui sent Wu Yingqi, Liao Jinzhong, Ma Bao, Zhang Guozhu, Ke Duo, Gao Qilong, and others to resist along separate lines, and also dispatched troops to probe Jiangxi, following the river to Nankang and capturing Duchang.

sentences.zh: 復自長沙入袁州，陷萍鄉、安福、上高、新昌諸縣。

translations.literal: He then entered Yuanzhou from Changsha and captured the counties of Pingxiang, Anfu, Shanggao, and Xinchang.
translations.idiomatic: From Changsha he then entered Yuanzhou and captured Pingxiang, Anfu, Shanggao, Xinchang, and other counties.

sentences.zh: 上命安親王岳樂為定遠平寇大將軍，徇江西；

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Prince An Yuele as Grand General for Pacifying the Distant and Quelling Rebels, to advance through Jiangxi;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Prince An Yuele Grand General for Pacifying the Distant and Quelling Rebels and sent him into Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 簡親王喇佈為揚威大將軍，鎮江南。

translations.literal: Prince Jian Labu was appointed Grand General Who Displays Might, to garrison Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian Labu was appointed Grand General Who Displays Might to secure Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 時王輔臣已為陝甘提督，復以寧羌叛應三桂，莫洛死之。

translations.literal: At this time Wang Fuchen had already become provincial commander of Shaanxi-Gansu; he again rebelled from Ningqiang in response to Sangui, and Mo Luo died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fuchen had by then become Provincial Commander of Shaanxi-Gansu, but he rebelled again from Ningqiang in support of Wu Sangui, and Mo Luo was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 三桂遣其將王屏籓入四川，與吳之茂合軍助輔臣。

translations.literal: Sangui sent his general Wang Pingfan into Sichuan to join forces with Wu Zhimao and assist Fuchen.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui sent his general Wang Pingfan into Sichuan to join Wu Zhimao's army and assist Wang Fuchen.

sentences.zh: 上复趣尚善速攻岳州，尚善疏請益兵，未即進。

translations.literal: The emperor again urgently pressed Shangshan to attack Yuezhou quickly; Shangshan memorialized requesting more troops and did not advance immediately.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again pressed Shangshan to attack Yuezhou quickly, but Shangshan memorialized asking for reinforcements and did not advance at once.

sentences.zh: 十四年正月，上命岳樂自袁州取長沙，岳樂遣兵先後克上高、新昌、東鄉、萬年、安仁、新城諸縣，復進克廣信、饒州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourteenth year the emperor ordered Yuele to take Changsha from Yuanzhou; Yuele dispatched troops who in succession captured the counties of Shanggao, Xinchang, Dongxiang, Wannian, Anren, and Xincheng, and then advanced to capture Guangxin and Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourteenth year, the emperor ordered Yuele to take Changsha from Yuanzhou. Yuele sent troops who in succession captured Shanggao, Xinchang, Dongxiang, Wannian, Anren, Xincheng, and other counties, then advanced to capture Guangxin and Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 夏國相堅守萍鄉，攻之不下。

translations.literal: Xia Guoxiang defended Pingxiang stubbornly; the attack could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Guoxiang defended Pingxiang stubbornly, and the Qing forces could not break the city.

sentences.zh: 上以岳樂師向湖南，命喇布移鎮南昌。

translations.literal: Because Yuele's army was heading toward Hunan, the emperor ordered Labu to transfer his headquarters to Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: With Yuele's army advancing toward Hunan, the emperor ordered Labu to transfer his headquarters to Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 三桂遣將率兵七萬、倮儸三千防醴陵，築木城以守；

translations.literal: Sangui dispatched a general leading seventy thousand troops and three thousand Luoluo to defend Liling, building a wooden fort to hold it;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui sent a general with seventy thousand troops and three thousand Luoluo warriors to defend Liling, where they built a wooden fortress.

sentences.zh: 又於岳州城外掘壕三重，環竹木為穽；

translations.literal: Outside Yuezhou city they dug triple moats and ringed bamboo and timber as pits;
translations.idiomatic: Outside Yuezhou they dug three lines of ditches and ringed the approaches with bamboo and timber traps.

sentences.zh: 於洞庭湖峽口植業木為椿，阻舟師；

translations.literal: At the gorge mouth of Dongting Lake they planted standing timber as piles to block the naval force;
translations.idiomatic: At the gorge mouth of Dongting Lake they planted standing timber as stakes to block the imperial fleet.

sentences.zh: 陸軍築壘皆設鹿角重疊，阻騎兵；

translations.literal: The land army built ramparts all with overlapping abatis to obstruct cavalry;
translations.idiomatic: The land army built earthen ramparts layered with abatis to block cavalry.

sentences.zh: 乃自常德赴松滋，駐舟師虎渡口，截勒爾錦、尚善兩軍使不相應；

translations.literal: Sangui then went from Changde to Songzi, stationed his naval force at Hukou Ferry, and cut off Le'erjin's and Shangshan's two armies so they could not coordinate;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui then moved from Changde to Songzi and stationed his fleet at Hukou Ferry, blocking Le'erjin's and Shangshan's armies from supporting each other.

sentences.zh: 揚言將渡江攻荊州，決堤以灌城，分岳州守兵據彝陵東北鎮荊山，令王會、楊來嘉、洪福等合兵陷穀城，執提督馬胡拜，攻鄖陽、均州、南漳。

translations.literal: He declared that he would cross the river to attack Jingzhou and breach the dyke to flood the city; he divided Yuezhou's garrison troops to hold Zhenjing Mountain northeast of Yiling, and ordered Wang Hui, Yang Laijia, Hong Fu, and others to join forces and capture Gucheng, seize provincial commander Ma Hubai, and attack Yunyang, Junzhou, and Nanzhang.
translations.idiomatic: He declared that he would cross the Yangzi to attack Jingzhou and breach the dykes to flood the city. He detached Yuezhou's garrison to hold Zhenjing Mountain northeast of Yiling and ordered Wang Hui, Yang Laijia, and Hong Fu to combine forces, capture Gucheng, seize Provincial Commander Ma Hubai, and attack Yunyang, Junzhou, and Nanzhang.

sentences.zh: 勒爾錦遣貝勒察尼守彝陵，與都統宜理布等力御​​之，疏請益兵。

translations.literal: Le'erjin dispatched Prince Chani to defend Yiling; with Commandant-in-Chief Yilibu and others he resisted with all his strength and memorialized requesting more troops.
translations.idiomatic: Le'erjin sent Prince Chani to hold Yiling. Chani and Commandant-in-Chief Yilibu resisted with all their strength and memorialized asking for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 上責勒爾錦逗遛，不許。

translations.literal: The emperor reproached Le'erjin for dawdling and refused his request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Le'erjin for dragging his feet and refused the request.

sentences.zh: 是歲，察哈爾布爾尼叛，上遣大將軍信親王鄂札、副將軍大學士圖海擊破之。

translations.literal: That year Chahar's Bu'erni rebelled; the emperor dispatched Grand General Prince Xin Ezha and Vice General Grand Secretary Tu Hai, who defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: That year Bu'erni of the Chahars rebelled. The emperor dispatched Grand General Prince Xin Ezha and Vice General Grand Secretary Tu Hai, who defeated him.

sentences.zh: 十五年，三桂遣兵侵廣東，授之信招討大將軍。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Sangui dispatched troops to invade Guangdong and appointed Zhixin Grand General for Recruitment and Punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, Wu Sangui sent troops into Guangdong and appointed Shang Zhixin Grand General for Recruitment and Punishment.

sentences.zh: 時可喜已病篤，之信遂降。

translations.literal: At this time Kexi was already gravely ill, and Zhixin then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: By then Shang Kexi was gravely ill, and Shang Zhixin surrendered.

sentences.zh: 三桂別遣其將韓大任、高大節將數万人陷吉安。

translations.literal: Sangui separately sent his generals Han Daren and Gao Dajie leading tens of thousands of men to capture Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui separately sent his generals Han Daren and Gao Dajie with tens of thousands of men to capture Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 上令喇布固守饒州，岳樂攻萍鄉，力戰破十二壘，斬萬餘級，國相引兵走，乃克之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Labu to hold Raozhou firmly; Yuele attacked Pingxiang, fought fiercely and broke twelve ramparts, beheaded more than ten thousand, Guoxiang led his troops in flight, and the city was then taken.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Labu to hold Raozhou firmly while Yuele attacked Pingxiang. After fierce fighting the Qing forces broke twelve ramparts and killed more than ten thousand men. Xia Guoxiang withdrew his troops, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 師進复醴陵、瀏陽，復進攻長沙。

translations.literal: The army advanced and recaptured Liling and Liuyang, then advanced again to attack Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing army then recaptured Liling and Liuyang and advanced again on Changsha.

sentences.zh: 三桂遣胡國柱益兵以守，馬寶、高啟隆自岳州以兵會。

translations.literal: Sangui sent Hu Guozhu with reinforcements to defend it; Ma Bao and Gao Qilong came from Yuezhou with troops to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui sent Hu Guozhu with reinforcements to hold the city, while Ma Bao and Gao Qilong marched from Yuezhou to join him.

sentences.zh: 三桂自松滋移屯岳麓山，為長沙聲援；

translations.literal: Sangui moved his encampment from Songzi to Mount Yuelu to support Changsha from afar;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui shifted his headquarters from Songzi to Mount Yuelu to support Changsha.

sentences.zh: 又令大任、大節自吉安分兵犯新淦，屯泰和，复陷萍鄉、醴陵，斷岳樂軍後。

translations.literal: He also ordered Daren and Dajie from Ji'an to divide their troops and strike Xingan, encamp at Taihe, again capture Pingxiang and Liling, and cut off Yuele's army from the rear.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Han Daren and Gao Dajie to split their forces from Ji'an, strike Xingan, and encamp at Taihe, recapturing Pingxiang and Liling and cutting Yuele's army off from the rear.

sentences.zh: 上嚴趣喇布援岳樂，乃自饒州進复餘幹、金谿，攻吉安，大節將四千人來拒，戰於大覺寺，以百騎陷陣，師左次螺子山。

translations.literal: The emperor severely pressed Labu to reinforce Yuele; Labu then advanced from Raozhou and recaptured Yugan and Jinxi, attacked Ji'an, and Dajie came with four thousand men to resist; they fought at the Dajue Temple, where a hundred cavalry broke the formation; the army withdrew to camp at Luozi Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sharply ordered Labu to reinforce Yuele. Labu then advanced from Raozhou, recaptured Yugan and Jinxi, and attacked Ji'an. Gao Dajie came out with four thousand men to resist. At the Dajue Temple, a hundred cavalry broke through the Qing line, and the army withdrew to encamp at Mount Luozi.

sentences.zh: 大節復以少兵力戰，喇布及副將軍希爾根倉卒棄營走，師敗績。

translations.literal: Dajie again fought with inferior numbers; Labu and Vice General Xirgen in haste abandoned the camp and fled—the army suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Dajie again fought against heavy odds. Labu and Vice General Xirgen hastily abandoned camp and fled, and the army suffered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 會大任與大節不相能，大節怏怏死。

translations.literal: As it happened Daren and Dajie could not get along; Dajie died in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: As it happened, Han Daren and Gao Dajie could not work together, and Gao Dajie died embittered.

sentences.zh: 喇布遣兵复圍吉安，大任不敢出戰。

translations.literal: Labu again dispatched troops to besiege Ji'an; Daren did not dare to sally out.
translations.idiomatic: Labu sent troops again to besiege Ji'an, and Han Daren did not dare to give battle.

sentences.zh: 勒爾錦以三桂去松滋，率兵渡江取石首，遣貝勒察尼攻太平街三桂兵壘，師敗續，退保荊州。

translations.literal: Le'erjin, because Sangui had left Songzi, led troops across the river to take Shishou and dispatched Prince Chani to attack Sangui's encampments at Taiping Street; the army was defeated in succession and withdrew to hold Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Le'erjin, seeing that Wu Sangui had left Songzi, led troops across the river to take Shishou and sent Prince Chani to attack Wu Sangui's camps at Taiping Street. The army was repeatedly defeated and withdrew to hold Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 是歲大將軍、大學士圖海代董額徵陝西，輔臣降。

translations.literal: That year the Grand General Grand Secretary Tu Hai replaced Dong'e in campaigning in Shaanxi, and Fuchen surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: That year Grand General and Grand Secretary Tu Hai replaced Prince Dong'e in the Shaanxi campaign, and Wang Fuchen surrendered.

sentences.zh: 上令將軍穆佔將陝西兵赴荊州，康親王杰書自浙江下福建，精忠降。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered General Muzhan to lead Shaanxi troops to Jingzhou; Prince Kang Jieshu descended into Fujian from Zhejiang, and Jingzhong surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered General Muzhan to lead Shaanxi troops to Jingzhou, while Prince Kang Jieshu advanced into Fujian from Zhejiang and Geng Jingzhong surrendered.

sentences.zh: 之信亦遣使詣喇布降。

translations.literal: Zhixin also sent envoys to Labu to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Zhixin also sent envoys to Labu to surrender.

sentences.zh: 延齡聞，亦原降，三桂使從孫世琮襲桂林，執而殺之，掠柳州、橫州、平樂、南寧。

translations.literal: When Yanling heard this, he too wished to surrender; Sangui had his grand-nephew Shizong attack Guilin, seized and killed him, and plundered Liuzhou, Hengzhou, Pingle, and Nanning.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Yanling heard this, he too wished to surrender. Wu Sangui had his grand-nephew Wu Shizong attack Guilin, seize and kill him, and plunder Liuzhou, Hengzhou, Pingle, and Nanning.

sentences.zh: 十六年，尚善分兵送馬三千益岳樂軍，三桂邀奪於七里台，復遣兵援吉安，與喇布軍相持。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Shangshan divided his troops to deliver three thousand horses to reinforce Yuele's army; Sangui intercepted and seized them at Qilitai, and again sent troops to relieve Ji'an, where they stood in stalemate with Labu's army.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, Shangshan dispatched three thousand horses to reinforce Yuele's army, but Wu Sangui intercepted and seized them at Qilitai. He again sent troops to relieve Ji'an, where they remained locked in stalemate with Labu's forces.

sentences.zh: 穆佔自岳州進，與岳樂夾攻長沙，克之。

translations.literal: Muzhan advanced from Yuezhou and joined Yuele in a pincer attack on Changsha; they captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhan advanced from Yuezhou and joined Yuele in a pincer attack on Changsha, which then fell.

sentences.zh: 三桂所遣援吉安諸軍皆引去，大任棄城走。

translations.literal: All the troops Sangui had sent to relieve Ji'an withdrew; Daren abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: All the troops Wu Sangui had sent to relieve Ji'an withdrew, and Han Daren abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 吉安乃下。

translations.literal: Ji'an then fell.
translations.idiomatic: Ji'an then fell to the Qing.

sentences.zh: 三桂自岳麓徙衡州，分兵犯南安、韶州，並益世琮兵掠廣西。

translations.literal: Sangui moved from Mount Yuelu to Hengzhou, divided his troops to strike Nan'an and Shaozhou, and also reinforced Shizong's troops in plundering Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui moved from Mount Yuelu to Hengzhou, sent detachments against Nan'an and Shaozhou, and reinforced Wu Shizong's forces plundering Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 十七年，岳樂復平江、湘陰，三桂將林興珠率所將水師降。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Yuele recaptured Pingjiang and Xiangyin; Sangui's general Lin Xingzhu led the naval force under his command in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, Yuele recaptured Pingjiang and Xiangyin, and Wu Sangui's general Lin Xingzhu surrendered with the fleet under his command.

sentences.zh: 穆佔攻永興，拔之，並下茶陵、攸、酃、安仁、興寧、郴、宜章、臨武、藍山、嘉禾、桂陽、桂東十二城。

translations.literal: Muzhan attacked Yongxing, took it, and also captured the twelve cities of Chaling, You, Ling, Anren, Xingning, Chen, Yizhang, Linwu, Lanshan, Jiahe, Guiyang, and Guidong.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhan attacked Yongxing and captured it, then took twelve more cities: Chaling, You, Ling, Anren, Xingning, Chen, Yizhang, Linwu, Lanshan, Jiahe, Guiyang, and Guidong.

sentences.zh: 喇布亦與江西總督董衛國率師逐大任，及於寧都，大任敗走福建，詣傑書降。

translations.literal: Labu also joined Jiangxi governor-general Dong Weiguo in leading troops to pursue Daren; they caught up with him at Ningdu; Daren was defeated and fled to Fujian, where he went to Jieshu and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Labu and Jiangxi Governor-General Dong Weiguo also pursued Han Daren and caught up with him at Ningdu. Han Daren was defeated, fled to Fujian, and surrendered to Prince Kang Jieshu.

sentences.zh: 三桂遣馬寶、胡國柱等攻永興，都統宜理布、護軍統領哈克山出戰，死。

translations.literal: Sangui sent Ma Bao, Hu Guozhu, and others to attack Yongxing; Commandant-in-Chief Yilibu and Guard Commander Hakeshan went out to fight and were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui sent Ma Bao, Hu Guozhu, and others to attack Yongxing. Commandant-in-Chief Yilibu and Guard Commander Hakeshan went out to fight and were killed.

sentences.zh: 穆佔與碩岱等力守。

translations.literal: Muzhan and Shuodai and others defended with all their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhan, Shuodai, and their officers held the city with all their strength.

sentences.zh: 是歲，三桂年六十有七，兵興六年，地日蹙，援日寡，思竊號自娛。

translations.literal: That year Sangui was sixty-seven years old; warfare had continued six years; his territory shrank daily and reinforcements grew daily fewer; he contemplated usurping the title to amuse himself.
translations.idiomatic: That year Wu Sangui was sixty-seven. The war had now dragged on for six years, his territory was shrinking daily, and reinforcements were growing ever scarcer. He decided to proclaim himself emperor as a consolation.

sentences.zh: 其下爭勸進，遂以三月朔稱帝​​，改元昭武，以衡州為定天府。

translations.literal: His subordinates all urged him to advance and accept the throne; he therefore on the first day of the third month proclaimed himself emperor, changed the era name to Zhaowu, and made Hengzhou the capital prefecture of Dingtian.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinates all urged him to take the throne. On the first day of the third month he proclaimed himself emperor, adopted the era name Zhaowu, and made Hengzhou his capital under the name Dingtian.

sentences.zh: 置百官，大封諸將，首國公，次郡公，亞以侯、伯。

translations.literal: He established the full bureaucracy, enfeoffed the generals on a grand scale—first rank state duke, next rank commandery duke, then marquises and earls in descending order.
translations.idiomatic: He established a full bureaucracy and lavished titles on his generals—state dukes first, then commandery dukes, followed by marquises and earls.

sentences.zh: 造新歷。

translations.literal: He created a new calendar.
translations.idiomatic: He promulgated a new calendar.

sentences.zh: 舉雲、貴、川、湖鄉試。

translations.literal: He held provincial examinations for Yunnan, Guizhou, Sichuan, and Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He held provincial civil examinations in Yunnan, Guizhou, Sichuan, and Huguang.

sentences.zh: 號所居舍曰殿，瓦不及易黃，以漆髹之。

translations.literal: He styled his dwelling a palace hall; having no time to replace the tiles with yellow ones, he lacquered them instead.
translations.idiomatic: He styled his residence a palace, and because there was no time to replace the roof tiles with the imperial yellow, he lacquered them instead.

sentences.zh: 構廬舍萬間為朝房。

translations.literal: He built ten thousand thatched lodges as court chambers.
translations.idiomatic: He erected ten thousand thatched lodges to serve as court chambers.

sentences.zh: 築壇衡山，行郊天即位禮，將吏入賀。

translations.literal: He built an altar on Mount Heng and performed the suburban-heaven enthronement rite; generals and officials entered to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: He built an altar on Mount Heng and performed the suburban sacrifice and enthronement rites, after which his officers and officials came to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 是日大風雨，草草成禮而罷。

translations.literal: That day there was great wind and rain; the rite was hastily completed and then brought to a close.
translations.idiomatic: That day a violent storm broke out, and the ceremony was hurried through and cut short.

sentences.zh: 俄病噎，八月，又病下痢，噤不能語。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he fell ill with choking; in the eighth month he also suffered from dysentery and could not speak for being silenced by illness.
translations.idiomatic: He soon developed a choking illness, and in the eighth month he was also stricken with dysentery and could no longer speak.

sentences.zh: 召其孫世璠於雲南，未至，乙酉，三桂死。

translations.literal: He summoned his grandson Shifan from Yunnan, but before he arrived, on yiyou Sangui died.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned his grandson Wu Shifan from Yunnan, but before Shifan arrived, on the day yiyou Wu Sangui died.

sentences.zh: 寶、國柱攻永興方急，聞喪，自焚其壘，引軍還衡州。

translations.literal: Bao and Guozhu were pressing the attack on Yongxing when they heard of the death; they burned their own encampments and led their armies back to Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Bao and Hu Guozhu were pressing hard on Yongxing when they heard the news. They burned their own camps and withdrew to Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 世璠，應熊庶子，留雲南，奔三桂之喪，至貴陽，其下擁稱帝，改號洪化，倚方光琛、郭壯圖為腹心。

translations.literal: Shifan was Yingxiong's son by a concubine; remaining in Yunnan, he hurried to Sangui's funeral; upon reaching Guiyang his subordinates enthroned him, changed the era title to Honghua, and relied on Fang Guangchen and Guo Zhuangtu as his inner circle.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shifan was a son of Wu Yingxiong by a concubine. Remaining in Yunnan, he set out for Wu Sangui's funeral. When he reached Guiyang, his followers proclaimed him emperor, adopted the era name Honghua, and relied on Fang Guangchen and Guo Zhuangtu as his closest advisers.

sentences.zh: 光琛，三桂所署大學士；

translations.literal: Guangchen was the Grand Secretary appointed by Sangui;
translations.idiomatic: Fang Guangchen had been the grand secretary Wu Sangui appointed.

sentences.zh: 壯圖，封國公。

translations.literal: Zhuangtu was enfeoffed as a state duke.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhuangtu was enfeoffed as a state duke.

sentences.zh: 三桂初起兵，其下或言宜疾行渡江，全師北向；

translations.literal: When Sangui first raised his army, some of his subordinates said he ought to march swiftly across the river with the full army and turn north;
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui first rose in rebellion, some of his advisers urged him to cross the Yangzi swiftly with his entire army and drive north.

sentences.zh: 或言直下金陵，扼長江，絕南北運道；

translations.literal: others said he ought to drive straight down to Jinling, choke the Yangzi, and cut off north-south supply routes;
translations.idiomatic: Others urged him to push straight to Nanjing, seize the Yangzi, and cut off the north-south supply lines.

sentences.zh: 或言宜出巴蜀，據關中，塞殽、函自固。

translations.literal: others said he ought to emerge through Ba-Shu, hold Guanzhong, and block Xiao and Han to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: Still others urged him to move through Ba and Shu, hold the Guanzhong region, and seal the Xiao and Han passes to secure his position.

sentences.zh: 三桂皆不能用，屯松滋，與勒爾錦夾江而軍，相持，皆不敢渡江決戰。

translations.literal: Sangui could adopt none of these plans; he encamped at Songzi, facing Le'erjin across the river with their armies facing each other in stalemate, neither side daring to cross the river for a decisive battle.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui accepted none of these plans. He encamped at Songzi and faced Le'erjin across the Yangzi in a prolonged standoff, with neither side daring to cross for a decisive battle.

sentences.zh: 既，還援長沙。

translations.literal: Afterward he returned to relieve Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: He then turned back to relieve Changsha.

sentences.zh: 晚乃欲通閩、粵道，糾精忠、之信复叛，攻永興未下而死。

translations.literal: Only late did he wish to open routes through Fujian and Guangdong, rally Jingzhong and Zhixin to rebel again, and he died before Yongxing could be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Only late in the war did he try to open routes through Fujian and Guangdong and urge Geng Jingzhong and Shang Zhixin to rebel again. He died before Yongxing had fallen.

sentences.zh: 吳國貴复議舍湖南，北向爭天下，陸軍出荊、襄趨河南，水軍下武昌，掠舟順流撼江左。

translations.literal: Wu Guogui again proposed abandoning Hunan, turning north to contest the empire: the land army would emerge through Jing and Xiang toward Henan, the naval force would descend on Wuchang, seize boats, and sweep downstream to shake the lower Yangzi region.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Guogui again proposed abandoning Hunan and turning north to contest the empire: the land army would advance through Jing and Xiang toward Henan, while the fleet would descend on Wuchang, seize boats, and sweep downstream to threaten the lower Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 諸將俱重棄滇、黔，馬寶首梗議，乃罷。

translations.literal: All the generals heavily opposed abandoning Yunnan and Guizhou; Ma Bao was foremost in obstructing the proposal, and the plan was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The generals were strongly opposed to abandoning Yunnan and Guizhou, with Ma Bao leading the opposition, and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 上以勒爾錦頓兵荊州不進，時尚善卒，貝勒察尼代為安遠靖寇大將軍，攻岳州，吳應麒守堅，久未下。

translations.literal: Because Le'erjin's army was stalled at Jingzhou without advancing, and at this time Shangshan died, Prince Chani replaced him as Grand General for Pacifying the Distant and Quelling Rebels; he attacked Yuezhou, but Wu Yingqi defended stubbornly and it was long not taken.
translations.idiomatic: With Le'erjin's army stalled at Jingzhou and Prince Shangshan now dead, Prince Chani replaced him as Grand General for Pacifying the Distant and Quelling Rebels and attacked Yuezhou, but Wu Yingqi defended stubbornly and the city long remained untaken.

sentences.zh: 下詔將親征，聞三桂死，乃罷。

translations.literal: An edict was issued that the emperor would personally campaign; when news came of Sangui's death, the plan was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict announcing that he would take the field in person, but when news of Wu Sangui's death arrived, the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 趣諸軍分道並進，並敕招撫陷賊官民。

translations.literal: He urgently pressed all armies to advance by separate routes together, and also ordered that officials and commoners who had fallen to the rebels be induced to surrender and submit.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered all armies to advance together along separate routes and issued instructions to offer surrender and pacification to officials and commoners who had sided with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 察尼屯君山，不能斷湖道，至是造鳥船百、沙船四百餘，配以兵三萬，水師始成軍，以貝勒鄂鼐統之。

translations.literal: Chani was encamped at Junshan and could not cut the lake route; at this time they built one hundred bird boats and more than four hundred sand boats, assigned thirty thousand troops to them, and the naval force at last became an army, with Prince E'nai commanding it.
translations.idiomatic: Chani had been encamped at Junshan but could not sever Wu Sangui's lake supply lines. At this point the Qing forces built one hundred bird boats and more than four hundred sand boats, manned them with thirty thousand troops, and at last had a proper navy under Prince E'nai.

sentences.zh: 用林興珠策，以其半泊君山，斷常德道；

translations.literal: Adopting Lin Xingzhu's strategy, half were moored at Junshan to cut the Changde route;
translations.idiomatic: Following Lin Xingzhu's plan, half the fleet was moored at Junshan to block the Changde route.

sentences.zh: 以其半分泊扁山、香爐峽、布袋口諸地；

translations.literal: the other half were divided and moored at Bianshan, Xianglu Gorge, Budai Mouth, and other places;
translations.idiomatic: The other half was divided among Bianshan, Xianglu Gorge, Budai Mouth, and other positions.

sentences.zh: 陸軍屯九貴山，斷岳州、衡州道。

translations.literal: the land army encamped at Jiuguishan to cut the routes between Yuezhou and Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The land army encamped at Jiuguishan to block the routes between Yuezhou and Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 水陸綿亙百里，岳州餉竭援窮，應麒與諸將江義、巴養元、杜輝駕巨艦二百，乘風犯柳林嘴。

translations.literal: The land and water forces stretched in an unbroken line for a hundred li; Yuezhou's supplies were exhausted and reinforcements cut off; Yingqi with the generals Jiang Yi, Ba Yangyuan, and Du Hui manned two hundred great warships, caught the wind, and attacked Willow Grove Mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Land and naval forces now stretched for a hundred li in an unbroken cordon. With Yuezhou's supplies exhausted and reinforcements cut off, Wu Yingqi and his generals Jiang Yi, Ba Yangyuan, and Du Hui took two hundred great warships, caught a favorable wind, and attacked Willow Grove Mouth.

sentences.zh: 察尼令水師棹輕舟，越敵艦，發砲擊之，毀過半，兵皆入水死。

translations.literal: Chani ordered the naval force to row light boats, pass over the enemy warships, open fire on them, destroyed more than half, and the soldiers all died in the water.
translations.idiomatic: Chani ordered his fleet to row light boats past the enemy warships and open fire. More than half were destroyed, and the rebel soldiers all drowned.

sentences.zh: 應麒復將五千人犯陸石，將軍鄂訥、前鋒統領杭奇率師擊之，應麒敗走。

translations.literal: Yingqi again led five thousand men to attack Lushi; General E'ne and Vanguard Commander Hang Qi led troops to strike them; Yingqi was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yingqi again led five thousand men against Lushi. General E'ne and Vanguard Commander Hang Qi led troops against him, and Wu Yingqi was defeated and fled.

sentences.zh: 杜輝有子在師中，通使約降，事泄，應麒殺輝。

translations.literal: Du Hui had a son in the Qing army; through an envoy he arranged to surrender, but when the affair was exposed Yingqi killed Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hui had a son serving in the Qing army and sent a messenger to arrange surrender, but when the plot was exposed Wu Yingqi executed him.

sentences.zh: 諸將日構隙，陳華、李超、王度衝等以舟師降。

translations.literal: The generals daily bred discord; Chen Hua, Li Chao, Wang Duchong, and others surrendered with the naval force.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel generals grew more estranged from one another by the day, until Chen Hua, Li Chao, Wang Duchong, and others surrendered with their fleet.

sentences.zh: 應麒收殘卒，挾輜重，潰圍奔長沙，胡國柱亦棄城與俱走。

translations.literal: Yingqi gathered the remnant soldiers, took the baggage train, broke through the encirclement and fled to Changsha; Hu Guozhu also abandoned the city and fled together with him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yingqi gathered the surviving troops, loaded the baggage train, and broke through the siege to flee toward Changsha; Hu Guozhu abandoned the city as well and withdrew with him.

sentences.zh: 察尼率師自岳州進克華容、安鄉、湘潭、衡山諸縣。

translations.literal: Chani led the army from Yuezhou forward and captured the counties of Huarong, Anxiang, Xiangtan, and Hengshan.
translations.idiomatic: Chani led his army south from Yuezhou and captured Huarong, Anxiang, Xiangtan, and Hengshan.

sentences.zh: 勒爾錦聞三桂死，率師自荊州渡江，三桂所部勒水師泊虎渡上游、陸師屯鎮荊山，皆潰走。

translations.literal: Le'erjin, hearing that Sangui was dead, led the army from Jingzhou across the river; Sangui's former forces had the naval army moored upstream at Hudu and the land army encamped at Zhenjing Mountain—all fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: When Le'erjin learned of Wu Sangui's death, he led his army from Jingzhou across the Yangzi. Wu Sangui's former naval force lay moored upstream at Hudu and his land army at Zhenjing Mountain; both broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 分兵定松滋、枝江、宜都、石門、慈利、澧州，進克常德。

translations.literal: He divided the army to pacify Songzi, Zhijiang, Yidu, Shimen, Cili, and Lizhou, then advanced and captured Changde.
translations.idiomatic: He sent detachments to secure Songzi, Zhijiang, Yidu, Shimen, Cili, and Lizhou, then advanced and took Changde.

sentences.zh: 喇布率師入衡州，進取祁陽、耒陽，復進克寶慶。

translations.literal: Labu led the army into Hengzhou, advanced to take Qiyang and Leiyang, and again advanced to capture Shaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Labu led his army into Hengzhou, seized Qiyang and Leiyang, and then pushed on to capture Shaocheng.

sentences.zh: 是時吳國貴自衡州退屯武岡，與馬寶俱。

translations.literal: At this time Wu Guogui withdrew from Hengzhou and encamped at Wugang, together with Ma Bao.
translations.idiomatic: By then Wu Guogui had withdrawn from Hengzhou to Wugang, where he joined Ma Bao.

sentences.zh: 吳應麒自岳州退屯辰州，胡國柱自長沙退屯辰龍關，相犄角力守。

translations.literal: Wu Yingqi withdrew from Yuezhou and encamped at Chenzhou; Hu Guozhu withdrew from Changsha and encamped at Chenlong Pass; they supported each other like horn and corner and strove to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yingqi fell back from Yuezhou to Chenzhou, while Hu Guozhu withdrew from Changsha to Chenlong Pass; the two positions formed a mutual defense, and they fought hard to hold the line.

sentences.zh: 穆佔師進克永明、江華、東安、道州，復進取永州。

translations.literal: Muzhan's army advanced and captured Yongming, Jianghua, Dong'an, and Daozhou, then again advanced to take Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhan's army captured Yongming, Jianghua, Dong'an, and Daozhou, then pressed on toward Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 岳樂師自衡州復常寧，攻武岡，國貴以二萬人據楓木嶺拒戰。

translations.literal: Yuele's army from Hengzhou recovered Changning and attacked Wugang; Guogui with twenty thousand men held Fengmu Ridge and resisted battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yuele's army recovered Changning from Hengzhou and attacked Wugang. Wu Guogui took twenty thousand men to Fengmu Ridge and made a stand.

sentences.zh: 岳樂令林興珠與提督趙國祚督兵奮擊，國貴死，兵潰。

translations.literal: Yuele ordered Lin Xingzhu and Regional Commander Zhao Guozuo to supervise the troops in fierce attack; Guogui died and the army collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuele ordered Lin Xingzhu and Regional Commander Zhao Guozuo to lead a fierce assault. Wu Guogui was killed and his army broke.

sentences.zh: 貝子彰泰等逐至木瓜橋，大破之，武岡下。

translations.literal: Prince Zhangtai and others pursued them to Mugua Bridge, routed them utterly, and Wugang fell.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhangtai and others pursued the rebels to Mugua Bridge and crushed them; Wugang then fell.

sentences.zh: 上召岳樂還京師，彰泰代為定遠平寇大將軍，令與穆佔議進取。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Yuele back to the capital; Zhangtai replaced him as Grand General for Pacifying Bandits at a Distance and was ordered to consult with Muzhan on the advance.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor recalled Yuele to the capital and appointed Prince Zhangtai Grand General for Pacifying Bandits at a Distance in his place, instructing him to plan the next advance with Muzhan.

sentences.zh: 是歲，將軍莽依圖等師徇廣西，世琮走死。

translations.literal: That year, General Mangyitu and others' army campaigned through Guangxi; Shicong fled and died.
translations.idiomatic: That year General Mangyitu swept through Guangxi; Wu Shicong fled and perished.

sentences.zh: 十九年春，將軍趙良棟自略陽破陽平關，克成都。

translations.literal: In the spring of the nineteenth year, General Zhao Liangdong from Lueyang broke Yangping Pass and captured Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the nineteenth year, General Zhao Liangdong broke through Yangping Pass from Lueyang and took Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 王進寶自鳳縣破武關，取漢中。

translations.literal: Wang Jinbao from Feng County broke Wuguan Pass and took Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jinbao broke through Wuguan Pass from Feng County and seized Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 王屏籓走保寧，師從之，戰於錦屏山，薄城，屏籓自殺。

translations.literal: Wang Pingfan fled to Baoning; the army followed him, fought at Jinping Mountain, pressed close to the city, and Pingfan killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pingfan fled to Baoning, and the Qing army pursued. After fighting at Jinping Mountain and closing on the city walls, Wang Pingfan took his own life.

sentences.zh: 保寧下，進克順慶。

translations.literal: Baoning fell, and they advanced to capture Shunqing.
translations.idiomatic: Once Baoning fell, the army advanced and took Shunqing.

sentences.zh: 將軍吳丹、提督徐治都自巫山克夔州、重慶，楊來嘉、譚弘先後降。

translations.literal: General Wu Dan and Regional Commander Xu Zhidu from Wushan captured Kuizhou and Chongqing; Yang Laijia and Tan Hong surrendered one after another.
translations.idiomatic: General Wu Dan and Regional Commander Xu Zhidu advanced from Wushan and captured Kuizhou and Chongqing. Yang Laijia and Tan Hong surrendered in turn.

sentences.zh: 察尼攻辰龍關，出間道襲破之，克辰州。

translations.literal: Chani attacked Chenlong Pass, sent troops by a hidden path to strike and break it, and captured Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chani assaulted Chenlong Pass, sent a detachment by a hidden route to take it by surprise, and then captured Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 楊寶廕、崔世祿皆降。

translations.literal: Yang Baoyin and Cui Shilu both surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Baoyin and Cui Shilu both surrendered.

sentences.zh: 彰泰師克沅州，吳應麒、胡國柱走貴陽。

translations.literal: Zhangtai's army captured Yuanzhou; Wu Yingqi and Hu Guozhu fled to Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhangtai's army took Yuanzhou, and Wu Yingqi and Hu Guozhu fled to Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 上召勒爾錦、察尼還京師，趣彰泰與穆佔、蔡毓榮等自沅州，喇布自南寧，吳丹、趙良棟自遵義，三道並進。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Le'erjin and Chani back to the capital and urged Zhangtai with Muzhan, Cai Yurong, and others from Yuanzhou, Labu from Nanning, and Wu Dan and Zhao Liangdong from Zunyi to advance together by three routes.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor recalled Le'erjin and Chani to the capital and ordered a three-pronged advance: Zhangtai with Muzhan and Cai Yurong from Yuanzhou, Labu from Nanning, and Wu Dan and Zhao Liangdong from Zunyi.

sentences.zh: 世璠令應麒與王會、高啟隆、夏國相合兵入四川，掠瀘州、敘州，進陷永寧。

translations.literal: Shifan ordered Yingqi together with Wang Hui, Gao Qilong, and Xia Guoxiang to combine forces and enter Sichuan, plunder Luzhou and Xuzhou, and advance to seize Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shifan sent Wu Yingqi, Wang Hui, Gao Qilong, and Xia Guoxiang into Sichuan with a combined force. They raided Luzhou and Xuzhou and then captured Yongning.

sentences.zh: 譚弘复叛，陷夔州。

translations.literal: Tan Hong again rebelled and seized Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Hong rebelled again and retook Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 上复趣彰泰速下貴陽，命賚塔為平南大將軍，盡護廣西諸軍。

translations.literal: The Emperor again urged Zhangtai to take Guiyang quickly, appointed Prince La Grand General for Pacifying the South, and put all the Guangxi armies under his command.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor again pressed Zhangtai to seize Guiyang without delay, appointed Prince La Grand General for Pacifying the South, and placed all Guangxi forces under his command.

sentences.zh: 吳丹坐不援永寧，罷，命趙良棟盡護四川諸軍，仍三道入雲南。

translations.literal: Wu Dan was punished for failing to relieve Yongning and dismissed; Zhao Liangdong was ordered to command all Sichuan armies, and still the three routes entered Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Dan was dismissed for failing to relieve Yongning. Zhao Liangdong was given command of all Sichuan forces, and the three armies continued their advance into Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 世璠召會、啟隆、國相自四川還援貴陽，令馬寶、胡國柱等掠四川。

translations.literal: Shifan summoned Hui, Qilong, and Guoxiang back from Sichuan to relieve Guiyang and ordered Ma Bao, Hu Guozhu, and others to plunder Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shifan recalled Wang Hui, Gao Qilong, and Xia Guoxiang from Sichuan to defend Guiyang and sent Ma Bao, Hu Guozhu, and others to ravage Sichuan instead.

sentences.zh: 十月，彰泰師克鎮遠，世璠將張足法等敗走。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Zhangtai's army captured Zhenyuan; Shifan's generals Zhang Zufa and others were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Prince Zhangtai's army took Zhenyuan, and Wu Shifan's generals Zhang Zufa and others were routed.

sentences.zh: 復進取平越，克新添、龍里二衛，薄貴陽。

translations.literal: They again advanced to take Pingyue, captured the two guards of Xintian and Longli, and pressed close to Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: They pushed on toward Pingyue, captured the garrisons of Xintian and Longli, and closed in on Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 世璠與應麒等奔還雲南。

translations.literal: Shifan with Yingqi and others fled back to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shifan fled back to Yunnan with Wu Yingqi and the others.

sentences.zh: 貴陽與安順、石阡、都勻諸府並下。

translations.literal: Guiyang together with the prefectures of Anshun, Shiqian, and Duyun all fell.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyang fell, along with the prefectures of Anshun, Shiqian, and Duyun.

sentences.zh: 世璠所署侍郎郭昌、邱元，總兵臧世遠、齊聘金、文台等，率將吏百數十人、兵一千三百有奇，詣彰泰軍降。

translations.literal: Shifan's appointed Vice Ministers Guo Chang and Qiu Yuan, Regional Commanders Zang Shiyuan, Qi Pinjin, and Wentai, and others led more than one hundred officers and more than thirteen hundred soldiers to Zhangtai's army to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: More than one hundred officers and some thirteen hundred soldiers appointed by Wu Shifan—including Vice Ministers Guo Chang and Qiu Yuan and Regional Commanders Zang Shiyuan, Qi Pinjin, and Wentai—went over to Prince Zhangtai and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 師復進，世璠所署總兵蔡國昌、平遠知府鄭開樞等以平遠降。

translations.literal: The army again advanced; Shifan's appointed Regional Commander Cai Guochang, Prefect of Pingyuan Zheng Kaishu, and others surrendered Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing army pressed forward, and Wu Shifan's appointees Regional Commander Cai Guochang and Pingyuan Prefect Zheng Kaishu surrendered the city of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 戰於永寧，至雞公背，世璠兵焚盤江鐵索橋走。

translations.literal: Battle was joined at Yongning; reaching Jigongbei, Shifan's soldiers burned the iron-chain bridge over the Pan River and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting reached Yongning and then Jigongbei, where Wu Shifan's troops burned the iron-chain bridge over the Pan River and fled.

sentences.zh: 普安土司龍天祜，永寧土司沙起龍、禮廷試造浮橋濟師。

translations.literal: Pu'an native chieftain Long Tianyou and Yongning native chieftains Sha Qilong and Li Tingshi built floating bridges to ferry the army across.
translations.idiomatic: The native chieftain Long Tianyou of Pu'an and the Yongning chieftains Sha Qilong and Li Tingshi built pontoon bridges to help the army cross.

sentences.zh: 二十年春，世璠以高啟隆為大將軍，與夏國相、王會、王永清、張足法等將二萬人拒彰泰，复陷平遠，屯城西南山上，穆佔與提督趙賴進擊破之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twentieth year, Shifan made Gao Qilong Grand General; with Xia Guoxiang, Wang Hui, Wang Yongqing, Zhang Zufa, and others he led twenty thousand men to resist Zhangtai, again seized Pingyuan, and encamped on the mountain southwest of the city; Muzhan and Regional Commander Zhao Lai advanced and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twentieth year Wu Shifan appointed Gao Qilong Grand General and sent him with Xia Guoxiang, Wang Hui, Wang Yongqing, Zhang Zufa, and twenty thousand men to block Prince Zhangtai. They retook Pingyuan and held the heights southwest of the city until Muzhan and Regional Commander Zhao Lai attacked and broke them.

sentences.zh: 啟隆等走，會降，復取平遠。

translations.literal: Qilong and the others fled; Hui surrendered, and Pingyuan was again recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qilong and the others fled, Wang Hui surrendered, and the Qing army recovered Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 彰泰師進次安南衛，世璠將線緎、巴養元、鄭旺、李繼業以萬餘人屯盤江西坡，為像陣，師初戰，為緎等所敗。

translations.literal: Zhangtai's army advanced and halted at Annan Guard; Shifan's generals Xian Yu, Ba Yangyuan, Zheng Wang, and Li Jiye with more than ten thousand men encamped at Panjiang Xipo, formed an elephant formation, and in the first battle the army was defeated by Yu and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhangtai's army halted at Annan Guard. Wu Shifan's generals Xian Yu, Ba Yangyuan, Zheng Wang, and Li Jiye held Panjiang Xipo with more than ten thousand men in an elephant formation and repulsed the Qing force in the first engagement.

sentences.zh: 越二日，彰泰令總兵白成功等進擊，戰於沙子哨，力鬥，自午至酉，師分隊奮進，緎等夜走。

translations.literal: After two days Zhangtai ordered Regional Commander Bai Chenggong and others to advance and attack; battle was joined at Shazishao; they fought fiercely from noon to you hour; the army divided into teams and pressed forward vigorously, and Yu and the others fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later Prince Zhangtai ordered Regional Commander Bai Chenggong and others to attack. At Shazishao the armies fought from noon until evening; the Qing forces then split into columns and pressed the attack, and Xian Yu and his men fled under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 遣都統龔圖等逐之，至臘茄坡，再戰，緎等退保交水城。

translations.literal: He dispatched Commandant Gong Tu and others to pursue them to Lajia Slope; they fought again, and Yu and the others withdrew to hold Jiaoshui City.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhangtai sent Commandant Gong Tu and others in pursuit to Lajia Slope. After another battle, Xian Yu and his men fell back to defend Jiaoshui City.

sentences.zh: 克新興所、普安州，黔西、大定諸府皆下，斬世璠所署巡撫張維堅。

translations.literal: They captured Xinxing Post and Pu'an Prefecture; the prefectures of Qianxi, Dading, and others all fell, and Shifan's appointed Grand Coordinator Zhang Weijian was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing army took Xinxing Post and Pu'an Prefecture, and the prefectures of Qianxi and Dading followed. Zhang Weijian, whom Wu Shifan had appointed Grand Coordinator, was executed.

sentences.zh: 賚塔師自田州進次西隆州，世璠將何繼祖以萬人屯石門坎守隘。

translations.literal: Prince La's army from Tianzhou advanced and halted at Xilong Prefecture; Shifan's general He Jizu with ten thousand men encamped at Shimenkan to guard the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Prince La's army advanced from Tianzhou to Xilong Prefecture, where Wu Shifan's general He Jizu blocked the route with ten thousand men at Shimenkan.

sentences.zh: 賚塔督兵分隊進攻，奪隘，復安籠所。

translations.literal: Prince La supervised the troops in divided teams advancing to attack, seized the pass, and recovered Anlong Post.
translations.idiomatic: Prince La attacked in columns, broke the pass, and recovered Anlong Post.

sentences.zh: 繼祖退至新城所，復與世璠將詹養、王有功等，合兵二萬人屯黃草壩，為像陣堅守。

translations.literal: Jizu withdrew to Xincheng Post, again joined with Shifan's generals Zhan Yang and Wang Yougong and others, combined forces of twenty thousand men, encamped at Huangcao Dam, formed an elephant formation, and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: He Jizu fell back to Xincheng Post and joined Wu Shifan's generals Zhan Yang and Wang Yougong with a combined force of twenty thousand men at Huangcao Dam, where they drew up an elephant formation and dug in.

sentences.zh: 賚塔督兵進，力戰，奪壘二十二，獲養、有功，俘兵千餘。

translations.literal: Prince La supervised the army in advance, fought fiercely, captured twenty-two stockades, seized Yang and Yougong, and took more than a thousand soldiers prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Prince La pressed the attack in heavy fighting, took twenty-two stockades, captured Zhan Yang and Wang Yougong, and made more than a thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 復進破曲靖，取交水城。

translations.literal: They again advanced, broke Qujing, and took Jiaoshui City.
translations.idiomatic: They pushed on, broke through at Qujing, and captured Jiaoshui City.

sentences.zh: 緎等復走，遂克馬龍州易龍所、揚林城，彰泰師亦至，兩軍會於嵩明。

translations.literal: Yu and the others again fled; they then captured Malong Prefecture, Yilong Post, and Yanglin City; Zhangtai's army also arrived, and the two armies joined at Songming.
translations.idiomatic: Xian Yu and his men fled again. The Qing forces then took Malong Prefecture, Yilong Post, and Yanglin City. Prince Zhangtai's army arrived as well, and the two columns united at Songming.

sentences.zh: 二月，進攻雲南會城，屯歸化寺，世璠遣將胡國柄等將萬人為像陣拒戰。

translations.literal: In the second month they advanced to attack the Yunnan provincial capital, encamped at Guihua Temple; Shifan dispatched General Hu Guobing and others with ten thousand men in an elephant formation to resist battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the allied armies attacked the Yunnan provincial capital and encamped at Guihua Temple. Wu Shifan sent Hu Guobing and ten thousand men in an elephant formation to meet them.

sentences.zh: 彰泰、賚塔督兵進擊，大破之，斬國柄及裨將九，俘六百餘，追之，薄城。

translations.literal: Zhangtai and Prince La supervised the troops in advance and attack, routed them utterly, beheaded Guobing and nine staff generals, took more than six hundred prisoners, pursued them, and pressed close to the city.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhangtai and Prince La led the assault and shattered the rebel force, killing Hu Guobing and nine subordinate commanders and taking more than six hundred prisoners. The pursuit carried the Qing army to the city walls.

sentences.zh: 世璠將張國柱、李髮美等先後降。

translations.literal: Shifan's generals Zhang Guozhu, Li Famei, and others surrendered one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shifan's generals Zhang Guozhu, Li Famei, and others surrendered in succession.

sentences.zh: 臨安、姚安、大理、鶴慶、麗江諸府悉下。

translations.literal: The prefectures of Lin'an, Yao'an, Dali, Heqing, and Lijiang all fell.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectures of Lin'an, Yao'an, Dali, Heqing, and Lijiang all submitted.

sentences.zh: 世璠召馬寶、胡國柱、夏國相等還救雲南。

translations.literal: Shifan summoned Ma Bao, Hu Guozhu, Xia Guoxiang, and others back to relieve Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shifan recalled Ma Bao, Hu Guozhu, Xia Guoxiang, and the others to save Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 上諭趙良棟等分兵邀擊寶等。

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed Zhao Liangdong and others to divide the army and intercept Bao and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Zhao Liangdong and others to send detachments to intercept Ma Bao and his force.

sentences.zh: 寶自尋甸至楚雄，屯烏木，兵潰，與巴養元、趙國祚、鄭旺、李繼業、郎應璧等詣姚安降。

translations.literal: Bao from Xundian reached Chuxiong, encamped at Wumu, the army collapsed, and together with Ba Yangyuan, Zhao Guozuo, Zheng Wang, Li Jiye, Lang Yingbi, and others he went to Yao'an to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Bao marched from Xundian to Chuxiong and encamped at Wumu, but his army broke. He went to Yao'an with Ba Yangyuan, Zhao Guozuo, Zheng Wang, Li Jiye, Lang Yingbi, and others and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 國柱自麗江、鶴慶入雲龍州，窮蹙自縊死。

translations.literal: Guozhu from Lijiang and Heqing entered Yunlong Prefecture; driven to extremity, he hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guozhu entered Yunlong Prefecture from Lijiang and Heqing and, cornered at last, hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 夏國相自平越敗後走廣西，總兵李國樑遣兵圍之，亦與王永清、江義等出降，世璠援絕。

translations.literal: Xia Guoxiang after defeat at Pingyue fled to Guangxi; Regional Commander Li Guoliang dispatched troops to surround him; he also came out and surrendered together with Wang Yongqing, Jiang Yi, and others; Shifan's relief was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: After his defeat at Pingyue, Xia Guoxiang fled into Guangxi, where Regional Commander Li Guoliang surrounded him. He surrendered together with Wang Yongqing and Jiang Yi, and Wu Shifan was cut off from all relief.

sentences.zh: 趙良棟師自夾江克雅州，復建昌，渡金沙江，次武定，復進次綿竹。

translations.literal: Zhao Liangdong's army from Jiajiang captured Yazhou, recovered Jianchang, crossed the Jinsha River, halted at Wuding, and again advanced to halt at Mianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Liangdong's army took Yazhou from Jiajiang, recovered Jianchang, crossed the Jinsha River, halted at Wuding, and then pushed on to Mianzhu.

sentences.zh: 九月，進與彰泰、賚塔諸軍合。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he advanced and joined with Zhangtai, Prince La, and the other armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he marched in and joined Prince Zhangtai, Prince La, and the other Qing armies.

sentences.zh: 時圍城已數月未下，良棟議斷昆明湖水道，主速攻，督兵薄城，圍之數重。

translations.literal: At this time the siege had continued for several months without the city falling; Liangdong proposed cutting off the Kunming Lake water route, advocated a swift attack, supervised the troops to press close to the city, and encircled it in several rings.
translations.idiomatic: The siege had already dragged on for months without success. Zhao Liangdong proposed cutting Kunming Lake's water supply to the city and urged a rapid assault. He drove his troops to the walls and tightened the encirclement in ring after ring.

sentences.zh: 線緎等謀執世璠及郭壯圖以降，世璠與壯圖皆自殺。

translations.literal: Xian Yu and others plotted to seize Shifan and Guo Zhuangtu to surrender; Shifan and Zhuangtu both killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Xian Yu and others plotted to seize Wu Shifan and Guo Zhuangtu and deliver them to the Qing, but Wu Shifan and Guo Zhuangtu both took their own lives.

sentences.zh: 十月戊申，緎等以城降。

translations.literal: On wushen of the tenth month, Yu and the others surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: On the wushen day of the tenth month, Xian Yu and the others surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 穆佔與都統馬齊先入城，籍賊黨，執方光琛及其子學潛、從子學範，磔於軍前。

translations.literal: Muzhan and Commandant Ma Qi first entered the city, registered the rebel partisans, seized Fang Guangchen together with his son Xueqian and nephew Xuefan, and dismembered them before the army.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhan and Commandant Ma Qi were the first to enter the city. They catalogued the rebel partisans, seized Fang Guangchen along with his son Xueqian and nephew Xuefan, and had them torn apart before the army.

sentences.zh: 戮世璠屍，傳首京師。

translations.literal: Shifan's corpse was mutilated and his head sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shifan's corpse was mutilated and his head sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 世璠所署將吏一千五百餘、兵五千有奇，皆降。

translations.literal: More than fifteen hundred officers and more than five thousand soldiers appointed by Shifan all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: More than fifteen hundred officers and some five thousand soldiers whom Wu Shifan had appointed all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 雲南、貴州、四川、湖廣諸省悉平。

translations.literal: The provinces of Yunnan, Guizhou, Sichuan, and Huguang were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan, Guizhou, Sichuan, and Huguang were all pacified.

sentences.zh: 上令宣捷詔，赦天下。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered a proclamation of victory to be issued and granted amnesty to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor issued a proclamation of victory and granted a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 二十一年春，從議政王大臣請，析三桂骸，傳示天下。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-first year, following the request of the Prince Regents, Sangui's remains were dismembered and displayed to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twenty-first year, at the Prince Regents' request, Wu Sangui's remains were dismembered and displayed throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 懸世璠首於市。

translations.literal: Shifan's head was hung in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shifan's head was displayed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 磔馬寶、夏國相、李本深、王永清、江義，親屬坐斬。

translations.literal: Ma Bao, Xia Guoxiang, Li Benshen, Wang Yongqing, and Jiang Yi were dismembered; their kinsmen were punished with execution.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Bao, Xia Guoxiang, Li Benshen, Wang Yongqing, and Jiang Yi were executed by dismemberment, and their kinsmen were put to death as well.

sentences.zh: 斬高啟隆、張國柱、巴養元、鄭旺、李繼業，財產妻女入官。

translations.literal: Gao Qilong, Zhang Guozhu, Ba Yangyuan, Zheng Wang, and Li Jiye were beheaded; their property, wives, and daughters were confiscated by the state.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qilong, Zhang Guozhu, Ba Yangyuan, Zheng Wang, and Li Jiye were beheaded, and their property, wives, and daughters were confiscated.

sentences.zh: 三桂諸將，馬寶、王屏籓最驍勇善戰。

translations.literal: Among Sangui's generals, Ma Bao and Wang Pingfan were the most fierce, brave, and skilled in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Of Wu Sangui's generals, Ma Bao and Wang Pingfan were the fiercest and most formidable in battle.

sentences.zh: 寶初為流賊，降明桂王由榔為將。

translations.literal: Bao was originally a roving bandit; he surrendered to the Ming Prince of Gui, Youlang, and became a general.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Bao had begun as a bandit chief before entering the service of the Ming Prince of Gui, Zhu Youlang.

sentences.zh: 桂王奔南甸，寶降於三桂，為忠勇中營總兵。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Gui fled to Nandian, Bao surrendered to Sangui and became Regional Commander of the Loyal and Valiant Middle Camp.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Gui fled to Nandian, Ma Bao went over to Wu Sangui and was made Regional Commander of the Loyal and Valiant Middle Camp.

sentences.zh: 三桂反，率兵前驅，盡陷貴州至湖廣南境諸郡縣，封國公。

translations.literal: When Sangui rebelled, he led the army as vanguard, captured all the commanderies and counties from Guizhou to the southern border of Huguang, and was enfeoffed as Duke of the State.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled, Ma Bao led the vanguard and overran the prefectures and counties from Guizhou to the southern reaches of Huguang. He was enfeoffed as Duke of the State.

sentences.zh: 再入廣西，一入四川，敗走姚安，詣希福軍降，至是死。

translations.literal: He again entered Guangxi and once entered Sichuan, was defeated and fled to Yao'an, went to Xifu's army to surrender, and at this time died.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned again in Guangxi and once in Sichuan, was routed and fled to Yao'an, surrendered to General Xifu, and was put to death on this occasion.

sentences.zh: 屏籓亦三桂所倚任，代高啟隆為忠勇左營總兵。

translations.literal: Pingfan was also one on whom Sangui relied; he replaced Gao Qilong as Regional Commander of the Loyal and Valiant Left Camp.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pingfan was likewise one of Wu Sangui's most trusted commanders and succeeded Gao Qilong as Regional Commander of the Loyal and Valiant Left Camp.

sentences.zh: 三桂反，令入四川為王輔臣聲援。

translations.literal: When Sangui rebelled, he ordered him to enter Sichuan to support Wang Fuchen.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled, he sent Wang Pingfan into Sichuan to support Wang Fuchen.

sentences.zh: 自秦州退守保寧，敗我師蟠龍山。

translations.literal: He withdrew from Qinzhou to hold Baoning and defeated our army at Panlong Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew from Qinzhou to hold Baoning and defeated the Qing army at Panlong Mountain.

sentences.zh: 十九年，師克保寧，自殺。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year the army captured Baoning and he killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year the Qing army took Baoning, and he killed himself.

sentences.zh: 諸專閫大將叛降三桂助亂者：雲南提督張國柱，貴州提督李本深，總兵王永清，副將江義，四川總兵譚弘、吳之茂，湖廣總兵楊來嘉，廣東總兵祖澤清，而陝西提督王輔臣兵最強，亂尤劇。

translations.literal: The regional commanders and grand generals who rebelled and surrendered to Sangui to aid the rebellion were: Yunnan Regional Commander Zhang Guozhu, Guizhou Regional Commander Li Benshen, Regional Commander Wang Yongqing, Vice Commander Jiang Yi, Sichuan Regional Commanders Tan Hong and Wu Zhimao, Huguang Regional Commander Yang Laijia, and Guangdong Regional Commander Zu Zeqing; while Shaanxi Regional Commander Wang Fuchen had the strongest army and the rebellion was especially fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Among the frontier commanders who defected to Wu Sangui were Yunnan Regional Commander Zhang Guozhu, Guizhou Regional Commander Li Benshen, Regional Commander Wang Yongqing, Vice Commander Jiang Yi, Sichuan Regional Commanders Tan Hong and Wu Zhimao, Huguang Regional Commander Yang Laijia, and Guangdong Regional Commander Zu Zeqing. Shaanxi Regional Commander Wang Fuchen commanded the strongest force, and the disorder was fiercest where he fought.

sentences.zh: 國柱，明副將，來降。

translations.literal: Guozhu was a Ming vice commander; he came and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guozhu had been a Ming vice commander before he surrendered to the Qing.

sentences.zh: 從續順公沈永忠下湖南，又從可喜定廣東，累遷至提督。

translations.literal: He followed Prince Xushun Shen Yongzhong in descending on Hunan, again followed Kexi in pacifying Guangdong, and was repeatedly promoted until Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Prince Xushun Shen Yongzhong into Hunan and later joined Kexi in the pacification of Guangdong, rising step by step to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 三桂反，授以大將軍，封國公。

translations.literal: When Sangui rebelled, he was appointed Grand General and enfeoffed as Duke of the State.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled, Zhang Guozhu was made Grand General and enfeoffed as Duke of the State.

sentences.zh: 陷衡州，圍長沙，戰岳州，皆國柱力。

translations.literal: The seizure of Hengzhou, the siege of Changsha, and the battles at Yuezhou were all Guozhu's doing.
translations.idiomatic: The capture of Hengzhou, the siege of Changsha, and the fighting at Yuezhou were largely his work.

sentences.zh: 師圍世璠，乃自大理出降。

translations.literal: When the army besieged Shifan, he then came out from Dali to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qing army besieged Wu Shifan, he surrendered from Dali.

sentences.zh: 本深，明總兵高傑甥，傑死，以提督代將。

translations.literal: Benshen was a nephew of the Ming Regional Commander Gao Jie; when Jie died, he succeeded as general in the post of regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Li Benshen was a nephew of the Ming commander Gao Jie. After Gao Jie died, Li Benshen succeeded him as regional commander.

sentences.zh: 降於豫親王多鐸，授三等精奇尼哈番，累遷至提督。

translations.literal: He surrendered to Prince Yu Duo and was granted the third-rank hereditary title of jingkiniha; he was repeatedly promoted until Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He surrendered to Prince Yu Duo and received the third-rank hereditary title of jingkiniha, eventually rising to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 三桂反，授以將軍。

translations.literal: When Sangui rebelled, he was appointed General.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled, Li Benshen was made a general in his service.

sentences.zh: 彰泰師克貴陽，出降。

translations.literal: When Zhangtai's army captured Guiyang, he came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zhangtai took Guiyang, Li Benshen surrendered.

sentences.zh: 永清以黔西鎮，義以鎮遠協，戕文焜，先後附三桂。

translations.literal: Yongqing held the Qianxi garrison and Yi held the Zhenyuan brigade; they murdered Wen Kun and successively joined Sangui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yongqing commanded the Qianxi garrison and Jiang Yi the Zhenyuan brigade. They murdered Wen Kun and later joined Wu Sangui.

sentences.zh: 至是同死。

translations.literal: At this time they died together.
translations.idiomatic: They were executed together on this occasion.

sentences.zh: 弘，初以明將降，累遷至總兵。

translations.literal: Hong was originally a Ming general who surrendered; he was repeatedly promoted until Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Hong had begun as a Ming officer before surrendering to the Qing and rising to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 三桂反，與四川提督鄭蛟麟、總兵吳之茂合謀叛。

translations.literal: When Sangui rebelled, he joined in conspiracy to rebel with Sichuan Regional Commander Zheng Jiaolin and Regional Commander Wu Zhimao.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled, Tan Hong plotted rebellion together with Sichuan Regional Commander Zheng Jiaolin and Regional Commander Wu Zhimao.

sentences.zh: 蛟麟，明都司，自松山降。

translations.literal: Jiaolin was a Ming battalion commander; he surrendered from Songshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jiaolin had been a Ming battalion commander before surrendering after Songshan.

sentences.zh: 三桂使犯漢中，戰敗，復出降。

translations.literal: Sangui sent him to invade Hanzhong; he was defeated in battle and again came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui sent him against Hanzhong, but after defeat he surrendered to the Qing again.

sentences.zh: 弘獨力戰，屢攻鄖陽。

translations.literal: Hong alone fought with all his strength and repeatedly attacked Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Hong fought on alone and repeatedly assaulted Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 三桂授以將軍，封國公。

translations.literal: Sangui appointed him General and enfeoffed him as Duke of the State.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui made him a general and enfeoffed him as Duke of the State.

sentences.zh: 弘死，子天秘走萬縣，久之始出降，送京師。

translations.literal: When Hong died, his son Tianmi fled to Wan County; only after a long time did he come out to surrender and was sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After Tan Hong died, his son Tianmi fled to Wan County and remained at large for a long time before surrendering and being sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 是年五月，磔死。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of that year he was executed by dismemberment.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of that year he was torn apart in execution.

sentences.zh: 之茂，與屏籓合軍援輔臣，攻秦州，力戰，敗走松潘。

translations.literal: Zhimao joined forces with Pingfan to relieve Fuchen, attacked Qinzhou, fought fiercely, and was defeated and fled to Songpan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhimao joined Wang Pingfan's army to relieve Wang Fuchen, attacked Qinzhou, fought hard, and was beaten back to Songpan.

sentences.zh: 還與屏籓守漢中，城下，就擒，送京師誅之。

translations.literal: He returned and with Pingfan held Hanzhong; when the city fell he was seized and sent to the capital for execution.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to hold Hanzhong with Wang Pingfan, but when the city fell he was captured and sent to the capital for execution.

sentences.zh: 來嘉，初以鄭錦將降，授總兵。

translations.literal: Laijia, originally a general under Zheng Chenggong who surrendered, was appointed regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Laijia had originally been a general under Zheng Chenggong before he surrendered and was appointed regional commander.

sentences.zh: 三桂反，與副將洪福同叛，三桂授以將軍。

translations.literal: When Sangui rebelled, Laijia rebelled together with Vice General Hong Fu; Sangui granted him the title General.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled, Yang Laijia rebelled together with Vice General Hong Fu, and Wu Sangui made him a general.

sentences.zh: 來嘉屢攻南漳，福屢攻均州。

translations.literal: Laijia repeatedly attacked Nanzhang, and Fu repeatedly attacked Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Laijia repeatedly attacked Nanzhang, while Hong Fu repeatedly attacked Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 勒爾錦師渡江，福先降。

translations.literal: When Le'erjin's army crossed the river, Fu surrendered first.
translations.idiomatic: When Le'erjin's army crossed the Yangzi, Hong Fu surrendered first.

sentences.zh: 來嘉敗走巫山，复走重慶。

translations.literal: Laijia was defeated and fled to Wushan, then fled again to Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Laijia was defeated and fled to Wushan, then retreated again to Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 城下，出降，送京師，未至，死。

translations.literal: When the city fell he came out and surrendered; he was sent to the capital but died before arriving.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he came out to surrender and was sent to the capital, but he died before he arrived.

sentences.zh: 澤清，大壽子。

translations.literal: Zeqing was Dashou's son.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Zeqing was the son of Zu Dashou.

sentences.zh: 以高州叛降三桂。

translations.literal: He rebelled from Gaozhou and surrendered to Sangui.
translations.idiomatic: He rebelled from Gaozhou and went over to Wu Sangui.

sentences.zh: 尚之信降，澤清亦降。

translations.literal: When Shang Zhixin surrendered, Zeqing also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Shang Zhixin surrendered, Zu Zeqing surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 俄复叛，命之信討之，克高州，獲澤清及其子良楩，送京師磔死。

translations.literal: Soon he rebelled again; Zhixin was ordered to suppress him, captured Gaozhou, seized Zeqing and his son Liangbin, and sent them to the capital for dismemberment and execution.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he rebelled again. Shang Zhixin was ordered to suppress him, captured Gaozhou, seized Zu Zeqing and his son Liangbin, and sent them to the capital to be dismembered and executed.

sentences.zh: 輔臣初為盜，號馬鷂子。

translations.literal: Fuchen was originally a bandit known by the nickname Hawk.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fuchen had originally been a bandit known by the nickname the Hawk.

sentences.zh: 從姜瓖為亂，降於英親王阿濟格。

translations.literal: He followed Jiang Xiang in rebellion and surrendered to Prince Ying Ajige.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Jiang Xiang in rebellion and later surrendered to Prince Ying Ajige.

sentences.zh: 尋以侍衛從洪承疇南征，事承疇謹，除總兵。

translations.literal: Soon he served as an imperial bodyguard under Hong Chengchou on the southern campaign; he served Hong Chengchou diligently and was appointed regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He soon served as an imperial bodyguard under Hong Chengchou on the southern campaign, attended Hong Chengchou with scrupulous loyalty, and was appointed regional commander.

sentences.zh: 三桂留授援剿右鎮，從入緬甸，破桂王，遷提督。

translations.literal: Sangui retained him and appointed him to the Right Garrison for Relief and Suppression; he followed Sangui into Burma, defeated Prince Gui, and was promoted to Provincial Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui kept him on and appointed him to the Right Garrison for Relief and Suppression. He followed Wu Sangui into Burma, helped defeat Prince Gui, and was promoted to Provincial Commander.

sentences.zh: 三桂反，招使叛，輔臣以聞，授三等精奇尼哈番，官其子繼貞。

translations.literal: When Sangui rebelled he tried to induce Fuchen to rebel; Fuchen reported this and was granted third-rank jingqi nihahan, and his son Jizhen was given an official post.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled he tried to induce Wang Fuchen to join him. Wang Fuchen reported the overture to the court, was granted third-rank jingqi nihahan, and his son Jizhen was given an official post.

sentences.zh: 經略大學士莫洛自陝西入四川，以輔臣從。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Mo Luo, Commissioner-General, entered Sichuan from Shaanxi with Fuchen following.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Mo Luo, the commissioner-general, entered Sichuan from Shaanxi with Wang Fuchen in his train.

sentences.zh: 次寧羌，脅眾擊殺莫洛，反，三桂授以大將軍，固原、定邊、臨洮、蘭州、同州諸將吏悉附，大將軍貝勒董額討焉。

translations.literal: At Ningqiang he compelled his followers to kill Mo Luo and rebelled; Sangui granted him the title Grand General; commanders and officials of Guyuan, Dingbian, Lintao, Lanzhou, Tongzhou, and others all joined him; Grand General Prince Dong'e was dispatched to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: At Ningqiang he forced his followers to kill Mo Luo and rebelled. Wu Sangui made him Grand General, and the commanders and officials of Guyuan, Dingbian, Lintao, Lanzhou, Tongzhou, and the surrounding districts all rallied to him. Grand General Prince Dong'e was sent to suppress the revolt.

sentences.zh: 輔臣保平涼，久不下。

translations.literal: Fuchen held Pingliang and for a long time it could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fuchen held Pingliang, and for a long time the city could not be taken.

sentences.zh: 大學士圖海代將，督兵力攻，乃出降。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Tu Hai replaced the commander, directed a full-strength attack, and Fuchen then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Tu Hai replaced the field commander, pressed a full-strength assault, and Wang Fuchen then came out and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 詔复官爵，加太子太保，授靖寇將軍，從圖海駐漢中。

translations.literal: An edict restored his rank and titles, added Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, appointed him General for Pacifying Rebels, and he followed Tu Hai to garrison Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored his rank and titles, made him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and General for Pacifying Rebels, and he followed Tu Hai to garrison Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 輔臣內不自安，與其妻妾縊，獨不死；

translations.literal: Fuchen was ill at ease within himself; he and his wives and concubines hanged themselves, but he alone did not die;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fuchen could not live at ease with himself. He and his wives and concubines hanged themselves, but he alone survived;

sentences.zh: 圖海師還，偕至西安，一夕死。

translations.literal: When Tu Hai's army returned, Fuchen accompanied him to Xi'an and died one night.
