translations.idiomatic: When Tu Hai's army returned, Wang Fuchen accompanied him to Xi'an and died one night.

sentences.zh: 上不深罪，但命停世襲，罷繼貞官。

translations.literal: The emperor did not punish him severely but ordered that hereditary succession be stopped and Jizhen dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not punish him harshly, but ordered that hereditary succession be stopped and Jizhen dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 耿精忠，靖南王繼茂子。

translations.literal: Geng Jingzhong was the son of Prince Jingnan Jingmao.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Jingzhong was the son of Prince Jingnan Geng Jingmao.

sentences.zh: 順治中，繼茂遣入侍，世祖授以一等精奇尼哈番，尚肅親王豪格女，封和碩額駙。

translations.literal: During the Shunzhi reign Jingmao sent him to serve at court; the Shizu emperor granted him first-rank jingqi nihahan, matched him with a daughter of Prince Su Hooge, and enfeoffed him as imperial son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shunzhi reign Geng Jingmao sent him to serve at court. The Shizu emperor granted him first-rank jingqi nihahan, matched him with a daughter of Prince Su Hooge, and enfeoffed him as imperial son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 康熙十年，繼茂卒，襲爵。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kangxi Jingmao died and Jingzhong inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of the Kangxi reign Geng Jingmao died, and Geng Jingzhong inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 十二年，疏請撤籓，許之，遣侍郎陳一炳如福建料理。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he memorialized requesting withdrawal of the princely establishment; permission was granted and Vice Minister Chen Yibing was dispatched to Fujian to manage affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he memorialized requesting the withdrawal of the princely establishment. Permission was granted, and Vice Minister Chen Yibing was sent to Fujian to manage the transition.

sentences.zh: 三桂反，命仍留鎮，召一炳還。

translations.literal: When Sangui rebelled, Jingzhong was ordered to remain in command and Chen Yibing was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled, Geng Jingzhong was ordered to remain in command, and Chen Yibing was recalled.

sentences.zh: 三桂以書招精忠，精忠與籓下都統馬九玉，總兵曾養性、江元勳，參領白顯忠、徐文耀、王世瑜、王振邦、蔣得鋐等謀應三桂，獨九玉以為不可，養性等皆讚之。

translations.literal: Sangui sent a letter recruiting Jingzhong; Jingzhong together with his garrison colonel Ma Jiuyu, generals Zeng Yangxing and Jiang Yuanxun, and adjutants Bai Xianzhong, Xu Wenyao, Wang Shiyu, Wang Zhenbang, Jiang Dechuan, and others plotted to respond to Sangui; only Jiuyu thought it unwise, while Yangxing and the others all approved.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui sent a letter recruiting Geng Jingzhong. Geng Jingzhong together with his garrison colonel Ma Jiuyu, generals Zeng Yangxing and Jiang Yuanxun, and adjutants Bai Xianzhong, Xu Wenyao, Wang Shiyu, Wang Zhenbang, Jiang Dechuan, and others plotted to join him. Only Ma Jiuyu thought it unwise, while Yangxing and the others all approved.

sentences.zh: 十三年三月，發兵反，脅總督范承謨，不屈，執而幽之，並及其賓從眷屬。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirteenth year he raised troops in rebellion, coerced Governor Fan Chengmo, who would not submit; Fan was seized and imprisoned along with his guests, attendants, and family.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the thirteenth year he raised troops in rebellion and tried to coerce Governor Fan Chengmo, who refused to submit. Fan was seized and imprisoned, together with his guests, attendants, and family.

sentences.zh: 巡撫劉秉政降。

translations.literal: Governor Liu Bingzheng surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Liu Bingzheng surrendered.

sentences.zh: 精忠自稱總統兵馬大將軍。

translations.literal: Jingzhong styled himself Grand General Commanding All Forces.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Jingzhong styled himself Grand General Commanding All Forces.

sentences.zh: 蓄髮，易衣冠。

translations.literal: He let his hair grow and changed his dress.
translations.idiomatic: He let his hair grow out again and changed his dress.

sentences.zh: 鑄錢曰「裕民通寶」。

translations.literal: He cast coin bearing the inscription Yumin Tongbao.
translations.idiomatic: He cast coin bearing the inscription Yumin Tongbao.

sentences.zh: 以養性、顯忠、元勳為將軍，分陷延平、邵武、福寧、建寧、汀州諸府。

translations.literal: He appointed Yangxing, Xianzhong, and Yuanxun as generals and sent them to capture Yanping, Shaowu, Funing, Jianning, Tingzhou, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He made Yangxing, Xianzhong, and Yuanxun his generals and sent them to capture Yanping, Shaowu, Funing, Jianning, Tingzhou, and the other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 約三桂合兵入江西。

translations.literal: He arranged to join forces with Sangui and enter Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He arranged to join forces with Wu Sangui and enter Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 嗾潮州總兵劉進忠擾廣東。

translations.literal: He incited Chaozhou General Liu Jinzhong to harry Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He incited Chaozhou General Liu Jinzhong to harry Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 又招鄭錦發兵取沿海郡縣為聲援。

translations.literal: He also recruited Zheng Chenggong's son to send troops and seize coastal prefectures and counties as a supporting force.
translations.idiomatic: He also called on Zheng Chenggong's son to send troops and seize coastal prefectures and counties as a supporting force.

sentences.zh: 浙江總督李之芳聞亂，出駐衢州，遣副將王廷梅等四出禦戰。

translations.literal: Zhejiang Governor Li Zhifang, on hearing of the disorder, went out to garrison Quzhou and dispatched Vice Generals Wang Tingmei and others in four directions to meet the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhejiang Governor Li Zhifang heard of the rebellion, he went out to garrison Quzhou and dispatched Vice Generals Wang Tingmei and others in four directions to meet the enemy.

sentences.zh: 上命將軍賚塔出浙江，將軍希爾根出江西，削精忠爵，聲討。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered General Zaita into Zhejiang and General Xiligen into Jiangxi, stripped Jingzhong of his title, and proclaimed a punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered General Zaita into Zhejiang and General Xiligen into Jiangxi, stripped Geng Jingzhong of his title, and proclaimed a punitive campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 仍遣郎中周襄緒偕精忠護衛陳嘉猷齎敕招撫，精忠留之軍中。

translations.literal: He still dispatched Director Zhou Xiangxu together with Jingzhong's guard Chen Jiayou to bear an edict offering amnesty; Jingzhong detained them in his camp.
translations.idiomatic: He still sent Director Zhou Xiangxu together with Geng Jingzhong's guard Chen Jiayou to bear an edict offering amnesty, but Geng Jingzhong detained them in his camp.

sentences.zh: 養性與林沖、徐尚朝、馮公輔、沙有祥等將萬餘人出仙霞關，陷江山、平陽，游擊司定猷縛總兵蔡朝佐，以城降。

translations.literal: Yangxing with Lin Chong, Xu Shangchao, Feng Gongfu, Sha Youxiang, and others led more than ten thousand men out through Xianxia Pass, captured Jiangshan and Pingyang; Guerrilla Commander Si Dingyou bound Regional Commander Cai Chaozuo and surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Yangxing with Lin Chong, Xu Shangchao, Feng Gongfu, Sha Youxiang, and others led more than ten thousand men out through Xianxia Pass and captured Jiangshan and Pingyang. Guerrilla Commander Si Dingyou bound Regional Commander Cai Chaozuo and surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 渡飛雲江，攻瑞安不下。

translations.literal: They crossed the Feiyun River but failed to take Ruian.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed the Feiyun River but failed to take Ruian.

sentences.zh: 移師攻溫州，總兵祖弘勳以城降。

translations.literal: They shifted their army to attack Wenzhou; Regional Commander Zu Hongxun surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: They shifted their army to attack Wenzhou, and Regional Commander Zu Hongxun surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 巡道陳丹赤、永嘉知縣馬閟死之。

translations.literal: Circuit Intendant Chen Danchi and Yongjia Magistrate Ma Kang died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit Intendant Chen Danchi and Yongjia Magistrate Ma Kang died in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 精忠授弘勳將軍，眾至十萬，陷樂清、天台、仙居、嵊縣，而寧海、象山、新昌、餘姚諸縣土寇競起。

translations.literal: Jingzhong appointed Hongxun a general; his forces reached one hundred thousand; they captured Yueqing, Tiantai, Xianju, and Sheng County, while local bandits rose up in Ninghai, Xiangshan, Xinchang, Yuyao, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Jingzhong made Zu Hongxun a general. His forces swelled to one hundred thousand men, and they captured Yueqing, Tiantai, Xianju, and Sheng County, while local bandits rose up all across Ninghai, Xiangshan, Xinchang, Yuyao, and the surrounding counties.

sentences.zh: 養性請於精忠官其渠，使屯大嵐山，擾紹興、寧波。

translations.literal: Yangxing asked Jingzhong to grant bandit chiefs official rank and station them on Mount Dalanshan to harry Shaoxing and Ningbo.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Yangxing asked Geng Jingzhong to grant the bandit chiefs official rank and station them on Mount Dalanshan to harry Shaoxing and Ningbo.

sentences.zh: 破黃岩，總兵阿爾泰降。

translations.literal: They broke Huangyan; Regional Commander Aertai surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: They broke Huangyan, and Regional Commander Aertai surrendered.

sentences.zh: 分兵犯金華，精忠與其將周列、王飛石、桑明等陷廣信、建昌、饒州。

translations.literal: They divided forces to invade Jinhua; Jingzhong with his generals Zhou Lie, Wang Feishi, and Sang Ming captured Guangxin, Jianchang, and Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: They divided their forces to invade Jinhua, and Geng Jingzhong with his generals Zhou Lie, Wang Feishi, and Sang Ming captured Guangxin, Jianchang, and Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 復合玉山、永豐土寇東犯常山，陷開化、壽昌、淳安、遂安諸縣。

translations.literal: They again combined with bandits of Yushan and Yongfeng to invade Changshan from the east and captured Kaihua, Shoucang, Chunan, and Suian.
translations.idiomatic: They joined forces again with bandits from Yushan and Yongfeng, invaded Changshan from the east, and captured Kaihua, Shoucang, Chunan, and Suian.

sentences.zh: 別遣兵攻徽州、婺源、祁門。

translations.literal: Separate forces were sent to attack Huizhou, Wuyuan, and Qimen.
translations.idiomatic: Separate detachments were sent to attack Huizhou, Wuyuan, and Qimen.

sentences.zh: 上令康親王杰書為奉命大將軍，貝子傅喇塔為寧海將軍，率師下浙江。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Prince Kang Jieshu Grand General on Imperial Commission and Prince Fuzhalata General for Pacifying the Sea, and they led armies south into Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Prince Kang Jieshu Grand General on Imperial Commission and Prince Fuzhalata General for Pacifying the Sea, and they led their armies south into Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 又以岳樂、喇布兩軍為聲援。

translations.literal: The armies of Yuele and Labu were also sent as a supporting force.
translations.idiomatic: The armies of Prince Yuele and Labu were also sent as a supporting force.

sentences.zh: 將軍賚塔師次衢州，養性自常山來犯，賚塔同之芳遣兵擊卻之。

translations.literal: General Zaita's army encamped at Quzhou; Yangxing came from Changshan to attack; Zaita together with Li Zhifang dispatched troops and drove him back.
translations.idiomatic: General Zaita's army halted at Quzhou. Zeng Yangxing came down from Changshan to attack, but Zaita and Li Zhifang dispatched troops and drove him back.

sentences.zh: 副將牟大寅戰常山，斬精忠將張宏。

translations.literal: Vice General Mou Dayin fought at Changshan and beheaded Jingzhong's general Zhang Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Vice General Mou Dayin fought at Changshan and beheaded Geng Jingzhong's general Zhang Hong.

sentences.zh: 洪起元戰紹興，复嵊縣。

translations.literal: Hong Qiyuan fought at Shaoxing and recovered Sheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Qiyuan fought at Shaoxing and recovered Sheng County.

sentences.zh: 鮑虎戰淳安，擒飛石、明，复壽昌、遂安。

translations.literal: Bao Hu fought at Chunan, captured Feishi and Ming, and recovered Shoucang and Suian.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Hu fought at Chunan, captured Wang Feishi and Sang Ming, and recovered Shoucang and Suian.

sentences.zh: 養性、尚朝等以五萬人攻金華，副都統瑪哈達、總兵陳世凱等與戰於木道山，斬二萬餘級，養性走天台。

translations.literal: Yangxing, Shangchao, and others with fifty thousand men attacked Jinhua; Vice Colonel Mahada, General Chen Shikai, and others fought them at Mudao Mountain, beheaded more than twenty thousand, and Yangxing fled to Tiantai.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Yangxing, Xu Shangchao, and others attacked Jinhua with fifty thousand men. Vice Colonel Mahada, General Chen Shikai, and others fought them at Mudao Mountain, killed more than twenty thousand rebels, and Yangxing fled to Tiantai.

sentences.zh: 十四年，養性復以步騎數万攻金華，遣其將硃飛熊率舟師水陸並進，傅喇塔擊斬飛熊，養性退屯茂平嶺。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Yangxing again with tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry attacked Jinhua and sent his general Zhu Feixiong with a fleet to advance by land and water together; Fuzhalata attacked and beheaded Feixiong; Yangxing withdrew to encamp at Maoping Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Zeng Yangxing again attacked Jinhua with tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry and sent his general Zhu Feixiong with a fleet to advance by land and water together. Prince Fuzhalata attacked and killed Feixiong, and Yangxing withdrew to Maoping Ridge.

sentences.zh: 巡道許弘勳擊破大嵐山土寇，斬其渠。

translations.literal: Circuit Intendant Xu Hongxun defeated the bandits on Mount Dalanshan and beheaded their leader.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit Intendant Xu Hongxun defeated the bandits on Mount Dalanshan and beheaded their leader.

sentences.zh: 傅喇塔督兵自間道出茂平嶺背，養性兵潰，复黃岩、樂清。

translations.literal: Fuzhalata directed troops along a hidden route to the rear of Maoping Ridge; Yangxing's army routed; Huangyan and Yueqing were recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Fuzhalata led his troops along a hidden route to the rear of Maoping Ridge. Yangxing's army broke, and Huangyan and Yueqing were recovered.

sentences.zh: 養性走保溫州，傅喇塔督兵合圍。

translations.literal: Yangxing fled to hold Wenzhou; Fuzhalata directed troops to join in encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Yangxing fled to hold Wenzhou, and Prince Fuzhalata directed his troops to join in the encirclement.

sentences.zh: 瑪哈達擊敗尚朝、公輔、有祥等，复處州。

translations.literal: Mahada defeated Shangchao, Gongfu, Youxiang, and others and recovered Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mahada defeated Xu Shangchao, Feng Gongfu, Sha Youxiang, and the others and recovered Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 穆赫林擊敗林沖，复仙居。

translations.literal: Muhelin defeated Lin Chong and recovered Xianju.
translations.idiomatic: Muhelin defeated Lin Chong and recovered Xianju.

sentences.zh: 喇布以兵助將軍額楚定徽州、婺源、祁門。

translations.literal: Labu with troops assisted General Echu in securing Huizhou, Wuyuan, and Qimen.
translations.idiomatic: Labu sent troops to assist General Echu in securing Huizhou, Wuyuan, and Qimen.

sentences.zh: 將軍希爾根亦復建昌、饒州。

translations.literal: General Xiligen also recovered Jianchang and Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: General Xiligen also recovered Jianchang and Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 岳樂師次南昌，諭精忠，精忠以謾書答之。

translations.literal: Prince Yuele's army encamped at Nanchang and addressed Jingzhong; Jingzhong replied with an insulting letter.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuele's army halted at Nanchang and addressed Geng Jingzhong, who replied with an insulting letter.

sentences.zh: 上復遣其弟聚忠齎敕諭降，至衢州，精忠拒不納。

translations.literal: The emperor again sent his younger brother Juzhong bearing an edict summoning surrender; when they reached Quzhou, Jingzhong refused to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again sent his younger brother Juzhong bearing an edict summoning surrender, but when they reached Quzhou Geng Jingzhong refused to receive them.

sentences.zh: 精忠母周氏，阻精忠毋叛，精忠不聽，周氏憤死。

translations.literal: Jingzhong's mother Lady Zhou urged him not to rebel; Jingzhong would not listen, and Lady Zhou died of indignation.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Jingzhong's mother, Lady Zhou, urged him not to rebel, but he would not listen, and she died of indignation.

sentences.zh: 精忠攻衢州，戰屢敗，以馬九玉為將軍，率兵屯江山，而鄭錦兵至，據泉、漳諸地，與精忠搆釁。

translations.literal: Jingzhong attacked Quzhou but was repeatedly defeated; he appointed Ma Jiuyu a general and led troops to garrison Jiangshan; meanwhile Zheng Chenggong's son's troops arrived, seized Quanzhou, Zhangzhou, and other places, and clashed with Jingzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Jingzhong attacked Quzhou but was repeatedly defeated. He made Ma Jiuyu a general and led troops to garrison Jiangshan, but Zheng Chenggong's son's troops arrived, seized Quanzhou, Zhangzhou, and other places, and clashed with Geng Jingzhong.

sentences.zh: 尚可喜請援，上令喇布自江西下廣東。

translations.literal: Shang Kexi requested aid; the emperor ordered Labu down from Jiangxi into Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Kexi requested aid, and the emperor ordered Labu down from Jiangxi into Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 精忠遣其將邵連登等擾建昌，進攻撫州、贛州。

translations.literal: Jingzhong dispatched his generals Shao Liandeng and others to harry Jianchang and advance against Fuzhou and Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Jingzhong dispatched his generals Shao Liandeng and others to harry Jianchang and advance against Fuzhou and Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 三桂兵陷袁州、吉安，相犄角，阻師行。

translations.literal: Sangui's troops captured Yuanzhou and Ji'an; the two forces supported each other in a pincer and blocked the army's advance.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui's troops captured Yuanzhou and Ji'an. The two rebel forces supported each other in a pincer and blocked the Qing advance.

sentences.zh: 尚之信亦叛。

translations.literal: Shang Zhixin also rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Zhixin also rebelled.

sentences.zh: 十五年春，傅喇塔自黃岩進攻溫州，力戰，屢破敵壘。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifteenth year Fuzhalata from Huangyan attacked Wenzhou, fought fiercely, and repeatedly broke the enemy's fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifteenth year Prince Fuzhalata advanced from Huangyan against Wenzhou, fought fiercely, and repeatedly broke the enemy's fortifications.

sentences.zh: 養性憑江拒戰，累月未能薄城。

translations.literal: Yangxing fought from across the river to resist; for months they could not approach the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Yangxing fought from across the river to resist, and for months the Qing forces could not approach the walls.

sentences.zh: 上趣傑書自金華至衢州，下福建。

translations.literal: The emperor pressed Jieshu from Jinhua to Quzhou and then down into Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pressed Prince Jieshu from Jinhua to Quzhou and then down into Fujian.

sentences.zh: 八月，傑書與賚塔、之芳督兵擊九玉，戰於大溪灘，九玉敗走，克江山。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Jieshu with Zaita and Li Zhifang directed troops to attack Jiuyu; they fought at Daxi Beach; Jiuyu was defeated and fled; Jiangshan was taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Prince Jieshu with Zaita and Li Zhifang directed troops against Ma Jiuyu. They fought at Daxi Beach, Jiuyu was defeated and fled, and Jiangshan fell.

sentences.zh: 招仙霞關守將金應虎降，遂入關，拔浦城。

translations.literal: Xianxia Pass garrison commander Jin Yinghu was induced to surrender; the army then entered the pass and took Pucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xianxia Pass garrison commander Jin Yinghu was induced to surrender. The Qing army then entered the pass and took Pucheng.

sentences.zh: 鄭錦兵侵興化，將及福州。

translations.literal: Zheng Chenggong's son's troops invaded Xinghua and were nearing Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chenggong's son's troops invaded Xinghua and were nearing Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 精忠勢漸蹙，謀出降，先使人戕承謨及其客嵇永仁等。

translations.literal: Jingzhong's position grew increasingly desperate; he planned to surrender and first had people murder Fan Chengmo and his guest Ji Yongren and others.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Jingzhong's position grew increasingly desperate. He planned to surrender and first had Fan Chengmo and his guest Ji Yongren and others murdered.

sentences.zh: 傑書師進次建陽，書諭降精忠，答書請宣詔赦罪。

translations.literal: Jieshu's army advanced and encamped at Jianyang; he wrote urging Jingzhong to surrender; Jingzhong replied requesting that an edict of pardon be proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jieshu's army advanced to Jianyang and wrote urging Geng Jingzhong to surrender. Geng Jingzhong replied asking that an edict of pardon be proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 師復進，克建寧，次延平。

translations.literal: The army advanced again, captured Jianning, and encamped at Yanping.
translations.idiomatic: The army advanced again, captured Jianning, and halted at Yanping.

sentences.zh: 精忠遣其子顯祚及襄緒、嘉猷出迎師。

translations.literal: Jingzhong sent his son Xianzuo together with Xiangxu and Jiayou out to meet the army.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Jingzhong sent his son Xianzuo together with Zhou Xiangxu and Chen Jiayou out to meet the army.

sentences.zh: 傑書使齎敕宣示，精忠乃出降，請從軍討錦自效。

translations.literal: Jieshu had the edict displayed; Jingzhong then came out and surrendered and asked to follow the army against Zheng Chenggong's son to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jieshu had the edict displayed. Geng Jingzhong then came out and surrendered and asked to follow the army against Zheng Chenggong's son to redeem himself.

sentences.zh: 傑書以聞，詔复爵，以其弟昭忠為鎮平將軍，駐福州，命精忠從軍討錦。

translations.literal: Jieshu reported this; an edict restored Jingzhong's title, appointed his younger brother Zhaozhong General for Pacifying the Region and stationed him at Fuzhou, and ordered Jingzhong to follow the army against Zheng Chenggong's son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jieshu reported this to the throne. An edict restored Geng Jingzhong's title, appointed his younger brother Zhaozhong General for Pacifying the Region and stationed him at Fuzhou, and ordered Geng Jingzhong to follow the army against Zheng Chenggong's son.

sentences.zh: 錦敗，還台灣。

translations.literal: Zheng Chenggong's son was defeated and retreated to Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chenggong's son was defeated and retreated to Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 乃移師趨潮州，進忠出降，令精忠駐焉。

translations.literal: The army then shifted toward Chaozhou; Jinzhong came out and surrendered; Jingzhong was ordered to garrison there.
translations.idiomatic: The army then shifted toward Chaozhou. Liu Jinzhong came out and surrendered, and Geng Jingzhong was ordered to garrison there.

sentences.zh: 養性在溫州，屢出戰，傅喇塔督兵擊破之。

translations.literal: Yangxing was at Wenzhou and repeatedly came out to fight; Fuzhalata directed troops and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Yangxing was at Wenzhou and repeatedly came out to fight, but Prince Fuzhalata directed his troops and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 養性墮水，復入城困守，精忠降，亦降，仍為籓下總兵。

translations.literal: Yangxing fell into the water, re-entered the city and held on under siege; when Jingzhong surrendered, Yangxing also surrendered and remained a general under the princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Yangxing fell into the water, re-entered the city, and held on under siege. When Geng Jingzhong surrendered, Yangxing surrendered as well and remained a general under the princely establishment.

sentences.zh: 十六年，遣顯祚入侍，授散秩大臣。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Xianzuo was sent to serve at court and granted the rank of minister without portfolio.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Xianzuo was sent to serve at court and granted the rank of minister without portfolio.

sentences.zh: 籓下參領徐鴻弼等使赴兵部具狀，訐精忠降後尚蓄逆謀，昭忠亦以鴻弼等狀聞，上留中未發。

translations.literal: Adjutants under the princely establishment including Xu Hongbi were sent to the Board of War to submit written accusations that Jingzhong after surrender still harbored treasonous designs; Zhaozhong also reported Hongbi's accusations; the emperor kept the matter within the palace and did not act.
translations.idiomatic: Adjutants under the princely establishment, including Xu Hongbi, were sent to the Board of War to submit written accusations that Geng Jingzhong still harbored treasonous designs after his surrender. Zhaozhong also reported Hongbi's accusations, but the emperor kept the matter within the palace and did not act.

sentences.zh: 十七年，上令精忠還福州，以其祖及父之喪還葬。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the emperor ordered Jingzhong back to Fuzhou to return and bury the remains of his grandfather and father.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the emperor ordered Geng Jingzhong back to Fuzhou to return and bury the remains of his grandfather and father.

sentences.zh: 是秋，三桂死，傑書疏請誅精忠，上諭曰：「今廣西、湖南、四川俱定，賊黨引領冀歸正者不止千百。

translations.literal: That autumn Sangui died; Jieshu memorialized requesting Jingzhong's execution; the emperor instructed: Guangxi, Hunan, and Sichuan are all now pacified, and rebel partisans by the hundreds and thousands are looking to submit.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Wu Sangui died. Prince Jieshu memorialized requesting Geng Jingzhong's execution, but the emperor instructed: "Guangxi, Hunan, and Sichuan are all now pacified, and rebel partisans by the hundreds and thousands are looking to submit.

sentences.zh: 驟誅精忠，或致寒心。

translations.literal: To execute Jingzhong suddenly might cause others to lose heart.
translations.idiomatic: To execute Geng Jingzhong suddenly might cause others to lose heart.

sentences.zh: 宜令自請來京，庶事皆寧貼。」

translations.literal: He should be made to request permission to come to the capital of his own accord, so that all affairs may settle peacefully.
translations.idiomatic: He should be made to request permission to come to the capital of his own accord, so that all affairs may settle peacefully."

sentences.zh: 十九年，精忠請入覲，上以九玉為總兵，轄籓下兵。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Jingzhong requested an audience at court; the emperor appointed Jiuyu regional commander to command the forces under the princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Geng Jingzhong requested an audience at court. The emperor appointed Ma Jiuyu regional commander to command the forces under the princely establishment.

sentences.zh: 昭忠、聚忠又疏劾精忠，上乃下鴻弼等狀，令法司按治，系精忠於獄。

translations.literal: Zhaozhong and Juzhong again memorialized to impeach Jingzhong; the emperor then issued Hongbi's accusations and ordered the judicial authorities to investigate and imprisoned Jingzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozhong and Juzhong again memorialized to impeach Geng Jingzhong. The emperor then issued Hongbi's accusations, ordered the judicial authorities to investigate, and imprisoned Geng Jingzhong.

sentences.zh: 遣聚忠赴福州宣撫所部。

translations.literal: [The emperor] dispatched Juzhong to Fuzhou to reassure and pacify the fief troops.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched Geng Juzhong to Fuzhou to reassure and pacify the fief troops.

sentences.zh: 是歲，之信以悖逆誅。

translations.literal: That year Zhixin was executed for treason and rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Shang Zhixin was executed for treason and rebellion.

sentences.zh: 二十年，雲南平。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Yunnan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, Yunnan was pacified.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，法司具獄上，上諭廷臣欲寬之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year the judicial authorities completed the case and submitted it; the emperor told the court officials he wished to show leniency.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, the judicial authorities completed the case and submitted it. The emperor told his court officials that he wished to show leniency.

sentences.zh: 大學士明珠奏精忠負恩謀反，罪浮​​於之信。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Mingzhu memorialized that Jingzhong had betrayed imperial favor and plotted rebellion, his crime exceeding Zhixin's.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Mingzhu memorialized that Geng Jingzhong had betrayed imperial favor and plotted rebellion, and that his crime was greater even than Shang Zhixin's.

sentences.zh: 乃與養性、顯忠、元勳、進忠、文耀、世瑜、振邦、得鋐並磔於市。

translations.literal: Thereupon together with Yangxing, Xianzhong, Yuanxun, Jinzhong, Wenyao, Shiyu, Zhenbang, and Dexuan he was dismembered in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Jingzhong was then dismembered in the marketplace together with Yangxing, Xianzhong, Yuanxun, Jinzhong, Wenyao, Shiyu, Zhenbang, and Dexuan.

sentences.zh: 顯祚、弘勳等皆斬。

translations.literal: Xianzuo, Hongxun, and others were all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzuo, Hongxun, and others were all beheaded.

sentences.zh: 秉政逮詣京師，道死。

translations.literal: Bingzheng was arrested and sent to the capital but died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzheng was arrested and sent to the capital but died on the road.

sentences.zh: 尚之信，平南王可喜子。

translations.literal: Shang Zhixin was a son of Prince of Pingnan Shang Kexi.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Zhixin was the son of Prince of Pingnan Shang Kexi.

sentences.zh: 順治中，可喜遣入侍，世祖以可喜功多，令之信秩視公爵。

translations.literal: In the Shunzhi era Kexi sent him to serve at court; the Shizu Emperor, considering Kexi's many achievements, ordered that Zhixin's rank be treated as that of a duke.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shunzhi reign, Kexi sent him to serve at court. Because of Kexi's many achievements, the Shunzhi Emperor ordered that Zhixin's rank be treated as that of a duke.

sentences.zh: 康熙十年，聖祖允可喜請，令之信佐軍事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kangxi the Sage Ancestor granted Kexi's request and ordered Zhixin to assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of the Kangxi reign, the Kangxi Emperor granted Kexi's request and ordered Zhixin to assist in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 之信酗酒嗜殺，可喜老病，營別宅以居，號令自擅。

translations.literal: Zhixin was given to heavy drinking and bloodthirstiness; Kexi being old and ill, built a separate residence to live in, while Zhixin issued orders on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixin drank heavily and was bloodthirsty. Kexi, now old and ill, built a separate residence and withdrew from daily affairs, while Zhixin issued orders on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 十二年，可喜用其客金光策，上疏請以二佐領歸老海城，而以之信襲爵留鎮。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Kexi employed his retainer Jin Guangce, who memorialized requesting that two commanders be sent to escort him in retirement to Haicheng while Zhixin should inherit the title and remain as garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, Kexi employed his retainer Jin Guangce, who memorialized the throne requesting that two commanders escort Kexi in retirement to Haicheng while Zhixin should inherit the title and remain as garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 光，浙江義烏人，佐可喜久，以捕佛山亂民江鵬翥功，​​授鴻臚寺卿銜。

translations.literal: Guang was a native of Yiwu in Zhejiang; he had long assisted Kexi, and for capturing the Foshan rebel Jiang Pengzhu was granted the rank of Grand Master for Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Guang was a native of Yiwu in Zhejiang. He had long served Kexi, and for capturing the Foshan rebel Jiang Pengzhu he was granted the rank of Grand Master for Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 屢以之信暴戾狀告可喜，為可喜謀，冀得見上自陳。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he reported Zhixin's violent behavior to Kexi and made plans for Kexi, hoping to be granted an audience with the emperor to plead his own case.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly reported Zhixin's violent behavior to Kexi and made plans on Kexi's behalf, hoping that Kexi might gain an audience with the emperor and plead his own case.

sentences.zh: 上以可喜疏下部議，令並移所部，遣尚書梁清標如廣東料理。

translations.literal: The emperor referred Kexi's memorial to the ministries for deliberation, ordering that all fief troops be transferred together and dispatching Minister Liang Qingbiao to Guangdong to manage affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor referred Kexi's memorial to the ministries for deliberation, ordered that all fief troops be transferred together, and dispatched Minister Liang Qingbiao to Guangdong to manage affairs.

sentences.zh: 三桂反，命可喜仍留鎮，召清標還。

translations.literal: When Sangui rebelled, the emperor ordered Kexi to remain as garrison commander and recalled Qingbiao.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled, the emperor ordered Kexi to remain as garrison commander and recalled Liang Qingbiao.

sentences.zh: 總兵劉進忠以潮州叛，可喜遣次子之孝率兵討之。

translations.literal: Regional commander Liu Jinzhong rebelled at Chaozhou; Kexi sent his second son Zhixiao at the head of troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commander Liu Jinzhong rebelled at Chaozhou. Kexi sent his second son Zhixiao at the head of troops to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 上授之孝平南大將軍，而命之信以討寇將軍銜協謀征剿。

translations.literal: The emperor invested Zhixiao as Grand General of Pingnan and ordered Zhixin to assist in planning the suppression under the title of General for Pacifying Bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor invested Zhixiao as Grand General of Pingnan and ordered Zhixin, under the title of General for Pacifying Bandits, to assist in planning the campaign.

sentences.zh: 鄭錦遣兵助進忠。

translations.literal: Zheng Jing sent troops to aid Jinzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jing sent troops to aid Liu Jinzhong.

sentences.zh: 總兵祖澤清復以高州叛，孫延齡將馬雄引三桂將董重民、李廷棟、王弘勳等陷雷、廉二郡。

translations.literal: Regional commander Zu Zeqing again rebelled at Gaozhou; Sun Yanling's general Ma Xiong led Wu Sangui's generals Dong Chongmin, Li Tingdong, Wang Hongxun, and others to seize the two prefectures of Lei and Lian.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commander Zu Zeqing again rebelled at Gaozhou. Sun Yanling's general Ma Xiong led Wu Sangui's generals Dong Chongmin, Li Tingdong, Wang Hongxun, and others in seizing the prefectures of Lei and Lian.

sentences.zh: 之孝退保惠州。

translations.literal: Zhixiao retreated to defend Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiao retreated to Huizhou to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 十五年春，可喜病益劇，之信代治事。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifteenth year Kexi's illness grew worse, and Zhixin took over the administration.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifteenth year, Kexi's illness grew worse and Zhixin took over the administration.

sentences.zh: 三桂招可喜籓下水師副將趙天元、總兵孫楷宗相繼​​叛，之信遂降三桂，遣兵守可喜籓府，戒毋白事，殺光以徇。

translations.literal: Sangui induced Kexi's fief vice-commander of the naval force Zhao Tianyuan and regional commander Sun Kaizong to rebel in succession; Zhixin then surrendered to Sangui, sent troops to guard Kexi's princely residence, forbade anyone to report affairs, and executed Guang as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui induced Kexi's fief vice-commander of the naval force Zhao Tianyuan and regional commander Sun Kaizong to rebel in succession. Zhixin then surrendered to Wu Sangui, posted troops to guard Kexi's princely residence, forbade anyone to report to Kexi, and executed Guang as a warning to others.

sentences.zh: 罷之孝兵，使侍可喜，可喜以憂憤卒。

translations.literal: Zhixiao's troops were disbanded and he was made to attend Kexi; Kexi died of grief and indignation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiao's troops were disbanded and he was made to attend his father. Kexi died of grief and indignation.

sentences.zh: 三桂授之信招討大將軍、輔德公，旋進號輔德親王，而以重民為兩廣總督，駐肇慶。

translations.literal: Sangui invested Zhixin as Grand General for Pacification and Duke of Fude, then soon promoted him to Prince of Fude, while appointing Chongmin governor-general of the Two Guangs, stationed at Zhaoqing.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui invested Zhixin as Grand General for Pacification and Duke of Fude, then soon promoted him to Prince of Fude, while appointing Dong Chongmin governor-general of the Two Guangs at Zhaoqing.

sentences.zh: 謝厥扶者，故蜑戶，以繒船數百附馬雄。

translations.literal: Xie Juefu was a former Dan boat-dweller who joined Ma Xiong with several hundred silken-sailed boats.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Juefu was a former Dan boat-dweller who joined Ma Xiong with several hundred silken-sailed craft.

sentences.zh: 天元之叛，厥扶實誘之。

translations.literal: Juefu had in fact instigated Tianyuan's rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In truth it was Juefu who had instigated Tianyuan's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 三桂亦授以將軍，使與重民水陸相援應，屢檄之信出兵。

translations.literal: Sangui also invested him as general, having him support Chongmin by land and sea, and repeatedly ordered Zhixin to send out troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui also invested Juefu as a general and had him coordinate with Chongmin by land and sea, while repeatedly ordering Zhixin to send out troops.

sentences.zh: 之信賂以庫金十萬，乃不復相促迫。

translations.literal: Zhixin bribed him with one hundred thousand taels from the treasury, whereupon he no longer pressed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixin bribed him with one hundred thousand taels from the treasury, whereupon he no longer pressed Zhixin to march.

sentences.zh: 之信旋遣使詣喇布軍，具疏請立功贖罪，上敕慰諭之。

translations.literal: Zhixin soon sent emissaries to Labu's army, submitting a detailed memorial requesting to redeem his crime through meritorious service; the emperor issued an edict of reassurance and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixin soon sent emissaries to Prince Labu's army, submitting a detailed memorial asking to redeem his crimes through meritorious service. The emperor issued an edict reassuring and encouraging him.

sentences.zh: 十六年，之信复疏請敕趣喇布軍入廣東。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Zhixin again memorialized requesting an edict urging Labu's army to enter Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, Zhixin again memorialized requesting an edict ordering Labu's army into Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 之信密嗾重民所部兵噪索餉，乘間擒重民，擊敗厥扶，走入海。

translations.literal: Zhixin secretly incited Chongmin's troops to clamor for pay, seized Chongmin in the confusion, defeated Juefu, who fled into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixin secretly incited Chongmin's troops to clamor for pay, seized Chongmin in the confusion, defeated Juefu, who fled to sea.

sentences.zh: 乃遣副都統尚之瑛迎師，疏言闔屬歸正，並請敘籓下總兵王國棟、長史李天植等襄贊功。

translations.literal: Thereupon he dispatched vice commander-in-chief Shang Zhiying to welcome the imperial army, memorializing that all his territory had returned to allegiance, and requesting honors for fief regional commander Wang Guodong, chief secretary Li Tianzhi, and others for their assistance.
translations.idiomatic: He then dispatched vice commander-in-chief Shang Zhiying to welcome the imperial army, memorializing that his entire domain had returned to allegiance and requesting honors for fief regional commander Wang Guodong, chief secretary Li Tianzhi, and others for their assistance.

sentences.zh: 時方多故，而可喜有大勳，上優容之，命之信襲平南親王，國棟等復舊職。

translations.literal: Affairs were turbulent at the time, but Kexi had great merit, so the emperor treated him with special forbearance, ordering Zhixin to inherit the princedom of Pingnan, and Guodong and others to resume their former posts.
translations.idiomatic: Affairs were turbulent at the time, but Kexi had earned great merit, so the emperor treated Zhixin with special forbearance, ordered him to inherit the princedom of Pingnan, and restored Guodong and the others to their former posts.

sentences.zh: 之信使入貢，上諭曰：「昔爾先人在時，屢獻方物。

translations.literal: Zhixin sent tribute envoys; the emperor instructed them, saying: "In the days when your forebear was alive, he repeatedly presented regional products.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixin sent tribute envoys. The emperor instructed them, saying, "In the days when your forebear was alive, he repeatedly presented regional products.

sentences.zh: 比年事變，信使弗通。

translations.literal: In recent years affairs have been in turmoil and envoys have not come.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years affairs have been in turmoil and envoys have not come.

sentences.zh: 每念爾先人忠貞不二，為國忘家，朕甚愍焉！

translations.literal: Whenever I think of your forebear's unwavering loyalty, putting the state before family, I am deeply moved with compassion!
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I think of your forebear's unwavering loyalty, putting the state before family, I am deeply moved with compassion!

sentences.zh: 王克承先志，遣使遠來，朕見物輒念爾先人。

translations.literal: The prince has succeeded in carrying on his forebear's will, sending envoys from afar; whenever I see these gifts I think of your forebear.
translations.idiomatic: The prince has succeeded in carrying on his forebear's will, sending envoys from afar. Whenever I see these gifts I think of your forebear.

sentences.zh: 王其安輯粵東，以繼爾先人未盡之志。

translations.literal: Let the prince settle and pacify eastern Guangdong, to continue what your forebear left unfinished.
translations.idiomatic: Let the prince settle and pacify eastern Guangdong, to continue what your forebear left unfinished.

sentences.zh: 貢獻細務，勞人費事，今當暫止。」

translations.literal: Tribute in such detail is troublesome and wasteful; for now it should be suspended."
translations.idiomatic: Tribute in such detail is troublesome and wasteful; for now it should be suspended."

sentences.zh: 是年秋，三桂遣其從孫世琮據廣西，巡撫傅弘烈率師討之，复梧州、潯州，規取桂林，之信令總兵尚從志以三千人從。

translations.literal: That autumn Sangui sent his grandnephew Shizong to hold Guangxi; Governor Fu Honglie led troops against him, recovered Wuzhou and Xunzhou, planned to take Guilin, and Zhixin ordered regional commander Shang Congzhi to follow with three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, Wu Sangui sent his grandnephew Shizong to hold Guangxi. Governor Fu Honglie led troops against him, recovered Wuzhou and Xunzhou, and planned to take Guilin. Zhixin ordered regional commander Shang Congzhi to follow with three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 上令之信自韶州進取宜章、郴州、永州，之信不赴。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Zhixin to advance from Shaozhou to take Yizhang, Chenzhou, and Yongzhou; Zhixin did not go.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Zhixin to advance from Shaozhou to take Yizhang, Chenzhou, and Yongzhou, but Zhixin did not go.

sentences.zh: 將軍莽依圖攻韶州，擊敗三桂將馬寶、胡國柱等。

translations.literal: General Mangyitu attacked Shaozhou and defeated Sangui's generals Ma Bao, Hu Guozhu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: General Mangyitu attacked Shaozhou and defeated Wu Sangui's generals Ma Bao, Hu Guozhu, and others.

sentences.zh: 上命之信移師梧州，又不赴。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Zhixin to move his army to Wuzhou; again he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Zhixin to move his army to Wuzhou. Again he did not go.

sentences.zh: 十七年春，上以莽依圖深入廣西，命之信策應。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventeenth year, with Mangyitu advancing deep into Guangxi, the emperor ordered Zhixin to coordinate in support.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventeenth year, with Mangyitu advancing deep into Guangxi, the emperor ordered Zhixin to coordinate in support.

sentences.zh: 之信仍以高、雷、廉三郡初定，疏請留鎮省城。

translations.literal: Zhixin still pleaded that the three prefectures of Gao, Lei, and Lian had only just been pacified, memorializing to remain garrison commander at the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixin still pleaded that the prefectures of Gaozhou, Leizhou, and Lianzhou had only just been pacified and memorialized to remain at the provincial capital as garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 上乃命發兵應莽依圖，之信遣國棟率兵赴宜章。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered troops dispatched to support Mangyitu; Zhixin sent Guodong to lead troops to Yizhang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered troops dispatched to support Mangyitu. Zhixin sent Guodong to lead troops to Yizhang.

sentences.zh: 及三桂死，之信乃請自進廣西，命為奮武大將軍，從師並進。

translations.literal: When Sangui died, Zhixin then requested to advance into Guangxi himself; he was ordered as Grand General Fenwu and marched together with the main army.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui died, Zhixin then requested to advance into Guangxi himself. He was appointed Grand General Fenwu and marched together with the main army.

sentences.zh: 十八年，天元出降，之信疏請誅之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Tianyuan came out to surrender; Zhixin memorialized requesting his execution.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, Tianyuan came out to surrender. Zhixin memorialized requesting his execution.

sentences.zh: 師進次橫州，自言病作，遽還。

translations.literal: The army advanced and halted at Hengzhou; he claimed illness came on and hurried back.
translations.idiomatic: The army advanced and halted at Hengzhou. Zhixin claimed he had taken ill and hurried back.

sentences.zh: 上命以所部從莽依圖並進，之信令籓下總兵時應運率以往。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered his troops to follow Mangyitu in the advance together; Zhixin had fief regional commander Shi Yingyun lead them there.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered his troops to follow Mangyitu in the joint advance. Zhixin had fief regional commander Shi Yingyun lead them there.

sentences.zh: 及莽依圖將攻桂林，留應運守南寧。

translations.literal: When Mangyitu was about to attack Guilin, Yingyun was left to guard Nanning.
translations.idiomatic: When Mangyitu was about to attack Guilin, Yingyun was left to guard Nanning.

sentences.zh: 三桂兵據武宣，之信又疏言海寇宜防，將召應運還。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui's troops held Wuxuan; Zhixin again memorialized that coastal bandits should be guarded against and was about to recall Yingyun.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui's troops held Wuxuan. Zhixin again memorialized that coastal bandits should be guarded against and was about to recall Yingyun.

sentences.zh: 上复諭趣之，十九年春，之信乃自將攻武宣。

translations.literal: The emperor again issued orders urging him on; in the spring of the nineteenth year Zhixin finally led the attack on Wuxuan in person.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again issued orders urging him on. In the spring of the nineteenth year, Zhixin finally led the attack on Wuxuan in person.

sentences.zh: 之信與之孝不相能，以之孝嘗典兵，不欲其居廣州，疏請遣還京師。

translations.literal: Zhixin and Zhixiao could not get along; because Zhixiao had once held military command, Zhixin did not want him in Guangzhou and memorialized requesting that he be sent back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixin and Zhixiao could not get along. Because Zhixiao had once held military command, Zhixin did not want him in Guangzhou and memorialized requesting that he be sent back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 之信殘暴猜忌，醉輒怒，執佩刀擊刺，又屢以鳴鏑射人。

translations.literal: Zhixin was cruel, suspicious, and given to rage when drunk, seizing his sword to strike and stab, and repeatedly shooting people with whistling arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixin was cruel and suspicious. When drunk he would fly into a rage, seizing his sword to strike and stab, and he repeatedly shot people with whistling arrows.

sentences.zh: 楷宗叛复降，上貸其罪，之信杖殺之。

translations.literal: Kaizong had rebelled and then surrendered again; the emperor pardoned his crime, but Zhixin beat him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Kaizong had rebelled and then surrendered again. The emperor pardoned his crime, but Zhixin beat him to death.

sentences.zh: 護衛張永祥為之信齎疏詣京師，上召見，授總兵。

translations.literal: Bodyguard Zhang Yongxiang carried a memorial from Zhixin to the capital; the emperor summoned him for an audience and invested him as regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Bodyguard Zhang Yongxiang carried a memorial from Zhixin to the capital. The emperor summoned him for an audience and invested him as regional commander.

sentences.zh: 之信故阻抑，复屢辱以鞭箠。

translations.literal: Zhixin had deliberately blocked and restrained him, and again repeatedly humiliated him with whipping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixin had deliberately blocked and restrained him and again repeatedly humiliated him with the whip.

sentences.zh: 怒護衛張士選語忤，射之，殘其足，諸護衛皆不平。

translations.literal: Angered that bodyguard Zhang Shixuan's words offended him, he shot him and crippled his leg; all the bodyguards were resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Angered that bodyguard Zhang Shixuan's words had offended him, he shot him and crippled his leg. All the bodyguards were resentful.

sentences.zh: 國棟與副都統尚之璋、總兵甯天祚密謀圖之信。

translations.literal: Guodong with vice commander-in-chief Shang Zhizhang and regional commander Ning Tianzuo secretly plotted to take Zhixin.
translations.idiomatic: Guodong, together with vice commander-in-chief Shang Zhizhang and regional commander Ning Tianzuo, secretly plotted to seize Zhixin.

sentences.zh: 巡撫金俊疏言：「之信兇殘暴虐，猶存異志。

translations.literal: Governor Jin Jun memorialized, saying: "Zhixin is fierce, cruel, and tyrannical, and still harbors disloyal intent.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Jin Jun memorialized, saying, "Zhixin is fierce, cruel, and tyrannical, and still harbors disloyal intent.

sentences.zh: 臣察其左右俱義憤不平，因密約都統王國棟等共酌機宜，之信旦夕就擒。

translations.literal: Your subject observes that all those around him are filled with righteous indignation; therefore in secret I have arranged with commander-in-chief Wang Guodong and others to plan the matter together, and Zhixin will be taken at any moment.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject observes that all those around him are filled with righteous indignation. Therefore in secret I have arranged with commander-in-chief Wang Guodong and others to plan the matter together, and Zhixin will be taken at any moment.

sentences.zh: 乞敕議行誅，以為人臣懷二心者戒。」

translations.literal: I beg that Your Majesty order deliberation on carrying out execution, to serve as a warning to ministers who harbor divided loyalties."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Your Majesty order deliberation on carrying out execution, to serve as a warning to ministers who harbor divided loyalties."

sentences.zh: 國棟亦上疏自述與俊、之璋、天祚合謀圖之信，又代之信母舒氏、胡氏疏言：「之信怙惡不悛，有不臣之心。

translations.literal: Guodong also memorialized describing in his own words the joint plot with Jun, Zhizhang, and Tianzuo to take Zhixin, and also submitted on behalf of Zhixin's mothers Lady Shu and Lady Hu, saying: "Zhixin persists in wickedness without reform and has the heart of a subject who refuses allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Guodong also memorialized describing in his own words the joint plot with Jun, Zhizhang, and Tianzuo to seize Zhixin, and also submitted on behalf of Zhixin's mothers Lady Shu and Lady Hu, saying, "Zhixin persists in wickedness without reform and has the heart of a subject who refuses allegiance.

sentences.zh: 恐禍延宗祀，乞上行誅。」

translations.literal: Fearing calamity will reach the ancestral line, we beg Your Majesty to order execution."
translations.idiomatic: Fearing calamity will reach the ancestral line, we beg Your Majesty to order execution."

sentences.zh: 上諭趣之信出師。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Zhixin to hurry out on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Zhixin to hurry out on campaign.

sentences.zh: 之信既赴武宣，永祥、士選詣京師告變。

translations.literal: Once Zhixin had gone to Wuxuan, Yongxiang and Shixuan went to the capital to report the mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhixin had gone to Wuxuan, Yongxiang and Shixuan went to the capital to report the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 上遣侍郎宜昌阿以巡視海疆至潮州，諭將軍賚塔移師，並令總督金光祖、提督折爾肯、副都統金榜選、總兵班際盛傳詔逮之信。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched Vice Minister Yichang'a to inspect the coastal regions and proceed to Chaozhou, instructing General Zaita to move his army, and also ordering Governor Jin Guangzu, Provincial Commander Zhe'erken, Vice Commander Jinfaxuan, and Regional Commander Ban Jisheng to deliver an edict and arrest Zhixin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched Vice Minister Yichang'a to inspect the coastal regions and proceed to Chaozhou, instructing General Zaita to move his army. He also ordered Governor Jin Guangzu, Provincial Commander Zhe'erken, Vice Commander Jinfaxuan, and Regional Commander Ban Jisheng to deliver an edict and arrest Zhixin.

sentences.zh: 之信與光祖、榜選、際盛等攻克武宣，之信入城。

translations.literal: Zhixin with Guangzu, Bangxuan, Jisheng, and others captured Wuxuan; Zhixin entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixin, together with Guangzu, Bangxuan, Jisheng, and others, captured Wuxuan. Zhixin entered the city.

sentences.zh: 光祖等屯城外，得國棟檄，合兵圍城，傳詔逮之信。

translations.literal: Guangzu and the others encamped outside the city; receiving Guodong's dispatch, they combined forces to besiege the city and delivered the edict to arrest Zhixin.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzu and the others encamped outside the city. Receiving Guodong's dispatch, they combined forces to besiege the city and delivered the edict to arrest Zhixin.

sentences.zh: 之信就逮，還廣州，上疏自辨。

translations.literal: Zhixin was arrested, returned to Guangzhou, and submitted a memorial in his own defense.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixin was arrested, returned to Guangzhou, and submitted a memorial in his own defense.

sentences.zh: 上令削爵，逮詣京師。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered his title stripped and that he be arrested and sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered his title stripped and that he be arrested and sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 籓下兵駐廣西，訛言師至雲南，即分置城守，眾情恟懼。

translations.literal: The fief troops stationed in Guangxi, hearing a rumor that the army had reached Yunnan, immediately dispersed to garrison the cities, and the men were alarmed and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: The fief troops stationed in Guangxi heard a rumor that the army had reached Yunnan, immediately dispersed to garrison the cities, and the men were alarmed and fearful.

sentences.zh: 上命宜昌阿、賚塔宣敕慰諭。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Yichang'a and Zaita to proclaim the edict and offer reassurance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Yichang'a and Zaita to proclaim the edict and offer reassurance.

sentences.zh: 七月，宜昌阿將以之信赴京師。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Yichang'a was about to escort Zhixin to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, Yichang'a was about to escort Zhixin to the capital.

sentences.zh: 天植怒國棟發難，白之信母，與之信弟之節、之璜、之瑛召國​​棟議事，伏兵殺之。

translations.literal: Tianzhi, angered that Guodong had raised the affair, reported to Zhixin's mother and, with Zhixin's brothers Zhijie, Zhihuang, and Zhiying, summoned Guodong to discuss affairs and killed him with hidden troops.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzhi, angered that Guodong had raised the affair, reported to Zhixin's mother and, with Zhixin's brothers Zhijie, Zhihuang, and Zhiying, summoned Guodong to discuss affairs and killed him with hidden troops.

sentences.zh: 賚塔率兵捕治，天植自服造謀，之信不與聞。

translations.literal: Zaita led troops to arrest and punish them; Tianzhi confessed to having plotted the affair, and Zhixin was said not to have known.
translations.idiomatic: Zaita led troops to arrest and punish them. Tianzhi confessed to having plotted the affair, and Zhixin was said not to have known.

sentences.zh: 護衛田世雄言之信實使天植殺國棟。

translations.literal: Bodyguard Tian Shixiong stated that Zhixin had in fact ordered Tianzhi to kill Guodong.
translations.idiomatic: Bodyguard Tian Shixiong stated that Zhixin had in fact ordered Tianzhi to kill Guodong.

sentences.zh: 獄上，上命賜之信死，之節、之璜、之瑛、天植皆斬。

translations.literal: When the case was submitted, the emperor ordered Zhixin granted death, and Zhijie, Zhihuang, Zhiying, and Tianzhi were all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was submitted, the emperor ordered Zhixin granted death. Zhijie, Zhihuang, Zhiying, and Tianzhi were all beheaded.

sentences.zh: 舒氏、胡氏貸其罪，並毋籍沒。

translations.literal: Ladies Shu and Hu were pardoned their crimes, and their property was not confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Ladies Shu and Hu were pardoned their crimes, and their property was not confiscated.

sentences.zh: 世雄以不先發，坐杖流。

translations.literal: Shixiong, for not reporting first, was sentenced to beating and exile.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiong, for not reporting first, was sentenced to beating and exile.

sentences.zh: 上复諭宜昌阿曰：「之信雖有罪，其妻子不可凌辱，當護還京師。」

translations.literal: The emperor again instructed Yichang'a, saying: "Although Zhixin is guilty, his wife and children must not be humiliated; they should be escorted back to the capital."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again instructed Yichang'a, saying, "Although Zhixin is guilty, his wife and children must not be humiliated. They should be escorted back to the capital."

sentences.zh: 又令察罷之信諸虐政。

translations.literal: He also ordered an investigation into abolishing Zhixin's various tyrannical policies.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered an investigation into abolishing Zhixin's various tyrannical policies.

sentences.zh: 所部十五佐領改隸漢軍，駐防廣州。

translations.literal: The fifteen company commanders under his authority were transferred to the Han Banner corps and garrisoned at Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The fifteen company commanders under his authority were transferred to the Han Banner corps and garrisoned at Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 之信初叛，提督嚴自明附之。

translations.literal: When Zhixin first rebelled, Provincial Commander Yan Ziming joined him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhixin first rebelled, Provincial Commander Yan Ziming joined him.

sentences.zh: 自明，明參將，降，從總督孟喬芳徵撫陝、甘，又擊張獻忠，破桂王，有功，授三等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: Ziming was a Ming vice commander; after surrendering he followed Governor Meng Qiaofang in pacifying Shaanxi and Gansu, also fought Zhang Xianzhong, defeated the Prince of Gui, and for his merit was granted a third-rank ashan i hafan.
translations.idiomatic: Ziming had been a Ming vice commander. After surrendering he followed Governor Meng Qiaofang in pacifying Shaanxi and Gansu, also fought Zhang Xianzhong, defeated the Prince of Gui, and for his merit was granted a third-rank ashan i hafan.

sentences.zh: 之信遣攻南康，敗走南安，先之信降，授鑾儀使。

translations.literal: Zhixin sent him to attack Nankang; defeated, he fled to Nan'an and surrendered before Zhixin did, and was appointed Director of Ceremonial Escort.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixin sent him to attack Nankang. Defeated, he fled to Nan'an and surrendered before Zhixin did, and was appointed Director of Ceremonial Escort.

sentences.zh: 病死。

translations.literal: He died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness.

sentences.zh: 孫延齡，漢軍正紅旗人。

translations.literal: Sun Yanling was a member of the Plain Red Banner of the Han Eight Banners.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yanling was a member of the Plain Red Banner of the Han Eight Banners.

sentences.zh: 父龍，從孔有德來歸，授二等阿思哈尼哈番，從有德廣西。

translations.literal: His father Long followed Kong Youde in coming over to allegiance, was granted a second-rank ashan i hafan, and followed Youde to Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Long followed Kong Youde in coming over to allegiance, was granted a second-rank ashan i hafan, and followed Youde to Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 有德以女四貞字延齡。

translations.literal: Youde gave his daughter Sizhen in marriage to Yanling.
translations.idiomatic: Youde gave his daughter Sizhen in marriage to Yanling.

sentences.zh: 及有德死事，龍亦戰死，加拖沙喇哈番，以延齡襲。

translations.literal: When Youde died in battle, Long also died fighting; an additional tosaha hafan was added, and Yanling inherited the rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Youde died in battle, Long also died fighting. An additional tosaha hafan was added, and Yanling inherited the rank.

sentences.zh: 四貞尚幼，還京師，孝莊皇后育之宮中，賜白金萬，歲俸視郡主。

translations.literal: Sizhen was still young; she returned to the capital, was raised in the palace by Empress Dowager Xiaozhuang, was granted ten thousand taels of silver, and received an annual stipend equal to that of a commandery princess.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhen was still young. She returned to the capital, was raised in the palace by Empress Dowager Xiaozhuang, was granted ten thousand taels of silver, and received an annual stipend equal to that of a commandery princess.

sentences.zh: 長，命仍適延齡。

translations.literal: When she came of age, she was ordered to marry Yanling as before.
translations.idiomatic: When she came of age, she was ordered to marry Yanling as before.

sentences.zh: 有德所部諸將，線國安功最高。

translations.literal: Among the generals under Youde's command, Xian Guo'an had the highest merit.
translations.idiomatic: Among the generals under Youde's command, Xian Guo'an had the highest merit.

sentences.zh: 國安與有德同起事，偕來降。

translations.literal: Guo'an had risen in rebellion together with Youde and came over to allegiance with him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo'an had risen in rebellion together with Youde and came over to allegiance with him.

sentences.zh: 從入關，西破李自成，南破桂王，累擢廣西提督，駐南寧。

translations.literal: He followed the army into the pass, defeated Li Zicheng in the west and the Prince of Gui in the south, was repeatedly promoted to provincial commander of Guangxi, and was stationed at Nanning.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the army through the pass, defeated Li Zicheng in the west and the Prince of Gui in the south, was repeatedly promoted to provincial commander of Guangxi, and was stationed at Nanning.

sentences.zh: 李定國陷桂林，盡殺其孥。

translations.literal: Li Dingguo captured Guilin and killed all of Guo'an's wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dingguo took Guilin and slaughtered Guo'an's entire family.

sentences.zh: 國安與總兵馬雄、全節力戰复桂林，走定國。

translations.literal: Guo'an, together with the brigade generals Ma Xiong and Quan Jie, fought fiercely to recover Guilin and drove off Li Dingguo.
translations.idiomatic: Guo'an, together with Brigade Generals Ma Xiong and Quan Jie, fought fiercely to retake Guilin and drove Li Dingguo away.

sentences.zh: 累加太子太保、徵蠻將軍，封三等伯，統有德舊部駐桂林。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Pacification-of-Barbarians General, enfeoffed as a third-rank count, and commanded Youde's former troops stationed at Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted, receiving the titles Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Pacification-of-Barbarians General, and was enfeoffed as a third-rank count. He took command of Youde's former troops and was stationed at Guilin.

sentences.zh: 康熙五年，以老乞休。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kangxi, on grounds of old age he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Kangxi reign, he requested retirement on grounds of old age.

sentences.zh: 上以延齡有德壻，四貞生長軍中，習騎射，通武事，乃授延齡鎮守廣西將軍，代國安統有德舊部。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering that Yanling was Youde's son-in-law and that Sizhen had grown up in the army, was skilled in horsemanship and archery, and understood military affairs, appointed Yanling Military Governor of Guangxi to replace Guo'an in commanding Youde's former troops.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor considered that Yanling was Youde's son-in-law, and that Sizhen had grown up in the army, skilled in horsemanship and archery and versed in military affairs. He therefore appointed Yanling Military Governor of Guangxi, assigning him to replace Guo'an in command of Youde's former troops.

sentences.zh: 予四貞郡主儀仗，偕赴鎮。

translations.literal: Sizhen was granted the ceremonial guard of a commandery princess, and they proceeded to the garrison together.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhen was granted the ceremonial guard befitting a commandery princess, and together they departed for the garrison.

sentences.zh: 延齡漸驕縱，十一年，御史馬大士劾延齡擅除武職，兵部既駁奏，延齡复疏請，恣肆不臣，上命申禁。

translations.literal: Yanling gradually grew arrogant and unrestrained. In the eleventh year, Censor Ma Dashi memorialized accusing Yanling of appointing military officials on his own authority. After the Ministry of War had already rejected the memorial in its reply, Yanling again submitted a petition requesting permission, behaving wantonly in a disloyal manner; the emperor ordered that he be firmly forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling gradually grew arrogant and unrestrained. In the eleventh year, Censor Ma Dashi memorialized the throne, accusing Yanling of appointing military officials on his own authority. The Ministry of War had already rejected the request in its reply, yet Yanling submitted another petition all the same, behaving with wanton disloyalty. The emperor ordered that he be firmly forbidden from doing so.

sentences.zh: 十二年，所部都統王永年，副都統孟一茂，參領胡同春、李一第等列延齡縱兵殃民狀，牒總督金光祖，光祖以聞。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, the commander-in-chief of his forces Wang Yongnian, the deputy commander-in-chief Meng Yimao, and the deputy commanders Hu Tongchun, Li Yidi, and others listed the facts of Yanling's letting his troops harm the people, sent a formal report to Governor-General Jin Guangzu, and Guangzu reported it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, the commander-in-chief of his forces Wang Yongnian, the deputy commander-in-chief Meng Yimao, and the deputy commanders Hu Tongchun, Li Yidi, and others submitted a detailed account of how Yanling had allowed his troops to ravage the populace. They sent a formal dispatch to Governor-General Jin Guangzu, who reported the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上遣侍郎勒德洪按治，得實，請逮延齡治罪，特命寬之。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched Vice Minister Le Dehong to investigate; the charges were found true, and he requested that Yanling be arrested and punished, but the emperor specially ordered leniency.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched Vice Minister Le Dehong to conduct an inquiry. The charges were found to be true, and Dehong requested that Yanling be arrested and punished. The emperor, however, specially ordered that he be treated with leniency.

sentences.zh: 三桂反，上授延齡撫蠻將軍，起國安都統。

translations.literal: When Sangui rebelled, the emperor granted Yanling the title of Pacifying Barbarians General and recalled Guo'an as commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled, the emperor granted Yanling the title Pacifying Barbarians General and recalled Guo'an to serve as commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時節已前卒，雄代國安為提督，命與巡撫馬雄鎮合謀剿禦。

translations.literal: Quan Jie had already died earlier; Xiong replaced Guo'an as provincial commander, and was ordered to join Governor Ma Xiongzhen in planning suppression and defense.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Jie had already died by then. Ma Xiong replaced Guo'an as provincial commander and was ordered to work with Governor Ma Xiongzhen on plans for suppression and defense.

sentences.zh: 十三年二月，延齡舉兵反，殺永年、一茂、同春、一第，幽雄鎮及其眷屬。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirteenth year, Yanling raised troops in rebellion, killed Yongnian, Yimao, Tongchun, and Yidi, and imprisoned Xiongzhen and his family.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the thirteenth year, Yanling took up arms in rebellion. He killed Yongnian, Yimao, Tongchun, and Yidi, and imprisoned Ma Xiongzhen along with his family.

sentences.zh: 詔奪官爵，聲討。

translations.literal: An edict stripped him of office and rank and proclaimed punitive action against him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped him of office and rank, and the court proclaimed its campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 延齡乃上疏言光祖、雄誘永年等謀害，上審其誣，諭尚可喜與光祖籌策進攻。

translations.literal: Yanling then submitted a memorial stating that Guangzu and Xiong had incited Yongnian and the others to plot his murder; the emperor examined the claim and found it false, and instructed Shang Kexi and Guangzu to devise a plan of attack.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling then submitted a memorial claiming that Guangzu and Ma Xiong had incited Yongnian and the others to plot against him. The emperor reviewed the accusation, found it to be slander, and instructed Shang Kexi and Guangzu to devise a plan of attack.

sentences.zh: 延齡自稱安遠大將軍，移牒平樂、梧州諸郡。

translations.literal: Yanling styled himself Grand General of Pacifying the Distance and sent dispatches to the prefectures of Pingle, Wuzhou, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling styled himself Grand General of Pacifying the Distance and issued dispatches to the prefectures of Pingle, Wuzhou, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 雄與總兵江義亦以柳州叛應三桂。

translations.literal: Xiong, together with the brigade general Jiang Yi, also rebelled at Liuzhou in response to Sangui.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xiong, together with Brigade General Jiang Yi, also rebelled at Liuzhou in support of Wu Sangui.

sentences.zh: 國安病死。

translations.literal: Guo'an died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Guo'an died of illness.

sentences.zh: 延齡招致萬羊山土寇，與所部合設五鎮，鎮兵二千。

translations.literal: Yanling recruited bandits from Mount Wanyang, and together with his own troops established five garrisons with two thousand men in each garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling recruited bandits from Mount Wanyang. Together with his own forces he established five garrisons, each with two thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 俄又自稱安遠王。

translations.literal: Before long he styled himself King of Pacifying the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he styled himself King of Pacifying the Distance.

sentences.zh: 慶陽知府傅弘烈當三桂未反，疏發諸不軌事，謫戍蒼梧，延齡既叛，授以將軍。

translations.literal: When Sangui had not yet rebelled, Fu Honglie, the prefect of Qingyang, had memorialized exposing various acts of disloyalty and was banished to serve at Cangwu. After Yanling rebelled, he was granted the title of general.
translations.idiomatic: While Wu Sangui had not yet rebelled, Fu Honglie, prefect of Qingyang, had memorialized the throne exposing various acts of disloyalty and was banished to Cangwu. After Yanling rebelled, Yanling appointed him general.

sentences.zh: 弘烈說延齡迎師，四貞尤力勸之。

translations.literal: Honglie urged Yanling to welcome the armies, and Sizhen especially pressed him hard to do so.
translations.idiomatic: Honglie urged Yanling to welcome the imperial armies, and Sizhen in particular pressed him vigorously to do so.

sentences.zh: 十六年，延齡遣弘烈迎師江西。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, Yanling dispatched Honglie to welcome the armies in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, Yanling dispatched Honglie to Jiangxi to welcome the imperial armies.

sentences.zh: 三桂诇知之，使從孫世琮率兵逼桂林，執殺延齡，四貞督兵禦戰。

translations.literal: Sangui learned of this through espionage and sent his grandnephew Shizong to lead troops to press upon Guilin, seized and killed Yanling, and Sizhen directed the troops in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui learned of this through spies and sent his grandnephew Shi Zong at the head of an army to march on Guilin. He seized and executed Yanling, while Sizhen took command of the troops in the defense.

sentences.zh: 世琮乃留其將李廷棟戍桂林，出掠平樂、潯州、橫州、南寧。

translations.literal: Shizong then left his general Li Tingdong to garrison Guilin and went out to plunder Pingle, Xunzhou, Hengzhou, and Nanning.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zong then left his general Li Tingdong to garrison Guilin and launched raids against Pingle, Xunzhou, Hengzhou, and Nanning.

sentences.zh: 弘烈還至平樂，延齡將劉彥明、徐洪鎮、徐上遠等擒斬廷棟，與國安子成仁並出降。

translations.literal: When Honglie returned to Pingle, Yanling's generals Liu Yanming, Xu Hongzhen, Xu Shangyuan, and others captured and executed Tingdong; together with Guo'an's son Chengren they all came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Honglie returned to Pingle, Yanling's generals Liu Yanming, Xu Hongzhen, and Xu Shangyuan captured and executed Li Tingdong. Together with Guo'an's son Chengren, they all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 四貞還京師。

translations.literal: Sizhen returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhen returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 雄亦從有德南征有功，授二等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: Xiong had also followed Youde south in campaign with merit, and was granted a second-rank ashan i hafan.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xiong had also accompanied Youde on the southern campaigns with distinction and was granted a second-rank ashan i hafan.

sentences.zh: 既與郭義叛，義偕嚴自明攻南康，敗走。

translations.literal: After he rebelled together with Guo Yi, Yi together with Yan Ziming attacked Nankang and was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: After he rebelled alongside Guo Yi, Guo Yi joined with Yan Ziming in an attack on Nankang, was defeated, and fled.

sentences.zh: 雄旋病死雒容。

translations.literal: Xiong soon afterward died of illness at Luorong.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xiong soon afterward died of illness at Luorong.

sentences.zh: 子承廕出降，進伯爵，授左江總兵。

translations.literal: His son Chengyin came out to surrender, was advanced to the rank of count, and was appointed brigade general of the Left River.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chengyin surrendered, was promoted to count, and was appointed brigade general of the Left River.

sentences.zh: 十九年二月，复叛，紿弘烈登舟，襲破其營，殺之。

translations.literal: In the second month of the nineteenth year, he rebelled again, deceiving Honglie into boarding a boat, launching a surprise attack that broke his camp, and killing him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the nineteenth year, he rebelled again. He lured Fu Honglie aboard a boat, then launched a surprise attack that overran his camp and killed him.

sentences.zh: 六月，复降，逮詣京師，論死。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he surrendered again, was arrested and brought to the capital, and was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he surrendered again, was arrested and brought to the capital, and was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 義奪官，放還原籍。

translations.literal: Yi was stripped of office and released to return to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yi was stripped of office and sent back to his native place.

sentences.zh: 論曰：聖祖初親政，舉大事書殿柱，即首「三籓」。

translations.literal: The commentator says: When the Sagely Ancestor first took personal rule, he wrote great affairs on the palace columns, and "the Three Feudatories" headed the list.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: When the Kangxi Emperor first took the reins of government in his own hands, he listed the great affairs of state on the palace columns—and "the Three Feudatories" stood first.

sentences.zh: 可喜乞歸老，曷嘗言撤籓？

translations.literal: When Kexi requested return to retire in old age, when did he ever speak of abolishing the feudatories?
translations.idiomatic: When Shang Kexi asked permission to retire, did he ever once speak of abolishing the feudatories?

sentences.zh: 撤籓自廷議，實上指也。

translations.literal: The abolition of the feudatories originated in court deliberations, but in truth it was at the emperor's direction.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal to abolish the feudatories arose in court deliberations, but in truth it was the emperor's own intent.

sentences.zh: 三桂反，精忠等響應，東南六七行省皆陷寇。

translations.literal: When Sangui rebelled, Jingzhong and others responded in kind, and six or seven provinces of the southeast all fell to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled, Geng Jingzhong and others answered his call, and six or seven southeastern provinces fell entirely into rebel hands.

sentences.zh: 上先發兵守荊州，阻寇毋使遽北。

translations.literal: The emperor first dispatched troops to hold Jingzhou and block the rebels so they would not swiftly advance north.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor first sent troops to hold Jingzhou, blocking the rebels so they could not quickly push north.

sentences.zh: 分遣禁旅屯太原、兗州、江寧、南昌，首尾相顧，次第漸進，千里赴鬥而師不勞。

translations.literal: He separately dispatched the imperial guard to garrison at Taiyuan, Yanzhou, Jiangning, and Nanchang, with front and rear mutually supporting each other, advancing step by step in order; though they fought a thousand li away, the armies were not worn out.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched imperial troops to garrison Taiyuan, Yanzhou, Jiangning, and Nanchang, arranging them so front and rear could support each other and advance in steady sequence—so that though the armies fought a thousand li from home, they did not grow exhausted.

sentences.zh: 三桂白首舉事，意上方少，諸王諸將帥佐開國者皆物故，變起且恇擾。

translations.literal: Sangui, white-haired, raised the standard of rebellion, thinking the emperor was still young, that the princes and the generals and commanders who had assisted at the founding of the dynasty had all passed away, and that when crisis erupted there would be alarm and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui, his hair white, took up arms in rebellion. He assumed the emperor was still young, that the princes and the veteran generals who had helped establish the dynasty were all dead, and that when trouble erupted the court would panic in disarray.

sentences.zh: 及聞上從容指揮，軍報迅速，閫外用命，始嘆非所料。

translations.literal: When he heard that the emperor calmly directed operations, that military reports moved swiftly, and that commanders in the field obeyed orders, he only then sighed that this was not what he had expected.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that the emperor was directing operations with calm assurance, that military dispatches moved swiftly, and that commanders in the field obeyed without question, he could only sigh that matters had not unfolded as he had expected.

sentences.zh: 制勝於廟堂，豈不然歟？

translations.literal: To prevail from the council hall—is this not so?
translations.idiomatic: To prevail from the council chamber—is this not exactly what happened?

sentences.zh: 上不欲歸咎建議撤籓諸臣，三桂等奉詔罷鎮，亦必曲意保全之。

translations.literal: The emperor did not wish to blame the officials who had proposed abolishing the feudatories; even when Sangui and the others received the edict to relinquish their fiefs, he would certainly have made every effort to protect them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had no wish to blame the officials who had advised abolishing the feudatories. Even when Wu Sangui and the others received the edict ordering them to surrender their fiefs, the emperor would surely have done everything in his power to protect them.

sentences.zh: 惜乎三桂等未能喻也！

translations.literal: Alas, Sangui and the others could not understand!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—Wu Sangui and his ilk failed to understand!
